entry.article_text: A barn that caught fire in Martin County on Thursday caused large flames and sent black smoke into the air that could be seen for miles. The fire occurred on a ranch in the 13000 block of Southwest Allapattah Road near Indiantown at about 5:30 p.m., according to a social media post by Martin County Fire Rescue. No horses or residents were injured. However, one firefighter was taken to the hospital with minor overexertion symptoms, Fire Rescue said. Officials said the barn and about six vehicles were a “total loss,” including a side-by-side and a small front-loader tractor. Southwest Allapattah Road is back open after earlier closures. The State Fire Marshal is investigating the cause of the blaze.

entry.title: ‘It’s very hard’: Family honors West Palm Beach man killed in hit-and-run
entry.summary: Nearly three months after a 28-year-old West Palm Beach man was killed in a hit-and-run crash, his family and friends are still searching for answers. Connor Blais was killed in July while riding an electric scooter home from his job at OSheas Irish Pub in downtown West Palm Beach. Police say Blais was found dead in the roadway along South Olive Avenue around 1:50 a.m. on July 6. An electric scooter was found nearby. Investigators say the driver involved in the crash left the scene without stopping to help or reporting the collision. Now, nearly three months later, Blais loved ones are returning to the crash site to remember his life and honor his memory. A Drive Safely memorial sign was installed at the west corner of South Olive Avenue and East Lakewood Road, near where Blais was killed. Blais partner, Lawrence Cassenti, remembers him as someone who took safety seriously and made a point of following the rules. His mom used to actually say, why don't you just get up on the sidewalk? And he'd say, no, Mom, I can't do that, that's not legal, Cassenti said. He was always in the bike lane. Friends and family gathered near the crash site wearing red and holding signs to honor Blais and celebrate his life. For his mother, Janet Blais, the loss remains difficult to put into words. No mother, father, friends or family should have to go through this. It's very hard, she said. Nearly three months after Blais death, police have still not identified the driver involved in the crash, and no arrest has been announced. Anyone with information about the crash or the driver involved is urged to contact the West Palm Beach Police Department.

Following his prison sentence, Barbre will face 5 years of sex offender probation and will be required to register as a sex offender. The terms of his probation bar him from accessing the internet, social media, smartphones, computers, or digital storage devices. I reached out to Palm Beach County Fire Rescue for a response. entry.title: Suspect arrested in fatal Ontario Place shooting in West Palm Beach, faces murder charge
entry.summary: West Palm Beach police have arrested a suspect in connection with a fatal shooting on Ontario Place early Sunday morning. Detectives identified the suspect as 38-year-old Hugh Earp Milner Jr. Milner was located and taken into custody with the assistance of the Broward County Sheriff's Office. He was transported to the Broward County Jail pending extradition to the Palm Beach County Jail. The shooting was first reported just after midnight Sunday after officers responded to a ShotSpotter alert in the 500 block of Ontario Place. As officers were en route, a victim was driven to a local fire station suffering from a gunshot wound. The victim, an adult male, was transported to an area hospital with life-threatening injuries and later died. Milner faces the following charges in connection with the shooting: First-degree murder with a firearm adult male victim, deceased Attempted first-degree murder with a firearm adult victim, no injuries reported Shooting into an occupied vehicle Anyone with information regarding this investigation is asked to contact the West Palm Beach Police Department or Palm Beach County Crime Stoppers at 1-800-458-TIPS (8477). Tips can remain anonymous.

entry.title: Former Palm Beach County Fire Rescue captain sentenced to 10 years for child pornography
entry.summary: William Barbre, a former captain with Palm Beach County Fire Rescue, has been sentenced to 10 years in state prison after pleading guilty to 30 felony counts of possession of child pornography. Barbre, 45, was arrested in April 2025. Detectives found more than 100 files depicting child sexual abuse. According to the arrest report, Barbre told deputies he felt 'repugnant' after viewing the files, adding he would delete them afterward. Court documents say Barbre confirmed the videos in his possession involved unlawful sexual activity of victims under the age of 15. Following his prison sentence, Barbre will face 5 years of sex offender probation and will be required to register as a sex offender. The terms of his probation bar him from accessing the internet, social media, smartphones, computers or digital storage devices. WPTV reached out to Palm Beach County Fire Rescue for a response. The department said in a brief statement that it became aware of the matter involving Barbre on April 16, 2025, and immediately placed him on administrative leave without pay. His employment ended six days later. This story was reported on-air by a journalist and has been converted to this platform with the assistance of AI. entry.title: Neighbors react after fatal West Palm Beach shooting ends in arrest
entry.summary: West Palm Beach police have arrested a suspect in connection with a fatal shooting on Ontario Place early Sunday morning. Detectives identified the suspect as 38-year-old Hugh Earp Milner Jr. Milner was located and taken into custody with the assistance of the Broward County Sheriff's Office. He was transported to the Broward County Jail pending extradition to the Palm Beach County Jail. The shooting was first reported just after midnight Sunday after officers responded to a ShotSpotter alert in the 500 block of Ontario Place. As officers were en route, a victim was driven to a local fire station suffering from a gunshot wound. The victim, an adult male, was transported to an area hospital with life-threatening injuries and later died. Milner faces the following charges in connection with the shooting: First-degree murder with a firearm adult male victim, deceased Attempted first-degree murder with a firearm adult victim, no injuries reported Shooting into an occupied vehicle WPTV Reporter Zitlali Solache spoke with several neighbors who live along Ontario Place. Some say they heard five or six gunshots and have been left feeling uneasy. I dont feel good about it, this kind of surprised me, because it never happened before,' said neighbor Elsie Royal. He's lived in the neighborhood since 2013 and was shocked to learn about the investigation. This comes, like, a surprise to me. I dont feel good about it. Im so sorry about it. WPTV reached out to the victim's loved ones and is waiting to hear back. Anyone with information regarding this investigation is asked to contact the West Palm Beach Police Department or Palm Beach County Crime Stoppers at 1-800-458-TIPS (8477). Tips can remain anonymous.

entry.title: From parks bonds to trash pickup: Local questions facing Palm Beach, Treasure Coast voters - WPEC
entry.summary: From parks bonds to trash pickup: Local questions facing Palm Beach, Treasure Coast voters    WPEC
entry.article_text: Voters in Palm Beach County and the Treasure Coast will decide eight local ballot questions on Nov. 3, ranging from hundreds of millions of dollars in bonds to trash pickup, mosquito control and the future of public land. The questions are separate from candidate races and the three statewide constitutional amendments . Some apply countywide, while others are limited to Stuart, Port St. Palm Beach County Palm Beach County voters will consider three countywide funding questions. The first would authorize up to $280 million in general-obligation bonds , repaid through property taxes over no more than 20 years. The money would modernize aging parks, recreation facilities and botanical gardens; expand sports complexes; improve beach access and trail connections; and help develop new regional parks. A second question would authorize up to $175 million in general-obligation bonds for the Palm Beach County Library District. The money would be used to acquire, build, renovate, expand, improve and equip library facilities. The bonds would be repaid through property taxes within the library district over no more than 20 years. The third question asks voters to continue the School District of Palm Beach County’s existing 1-mill property-tax levy from July 1, 2027, through June 30, 2031. One mill equals $1 for every $1,000 of taxable value. The levy would fund school safety and police, mental-health services, teachers in arts, music, physical education and career and choice programs, and improved teacher pay. An independent citizens-and-experts committee would oversee spending. Martin County Martin County’s local ballot questions are limited to Stuart voters. One proposed charter amendment would require voter approval before the City Commission could sell, convey or lease for more than one year any city-owned property containing recreational ballfields. The second question concerns an undeveloped 1.97-acre city parcel on U.S. 1 opposite North River Shores Boulevard. Voters would decide whether to rescind a 2011 referendum requiring the city to commercially lease the land to fund maintenance of the Haney Creek Preserve. If approved, the city could convert the parcel to conservation land and add it to the preserve. Lucie County has three local issues, although they do not all apply to every voter. The countywide question would extend the existing half-cent infrastructure sales surtax for 10 years, from Jan. The current tax is set to expire in 2028. See also: Dead rodent in kitchen, 260 droppings & no hand-washing: 7 South Florida restaurants shut Revenue would continue to fund capital projects such as road improvements, traffic-congestion relief, drainage, flood control, sidewalks and water-quality work. Lucie voters also will see a nonbinding straw poll asking whether the city should change from once-a-week to twice-a-week trash pickup for an added fee . The city previously estimated the second pickup day would cost about $131 a year. The vote would not itself change collection service or rates. It is intended to gauge residents’ preferences before the City Council decides whether to pursue the change. Lucie County issue is a binding referendum on expanding the St. Lucie County Mosquito Control District by about 95,000 acres. The referendum is not countywide or citywide. Only qualified voters living in the area proposed for addition to the district will vote on it. If approved, those properties would be added to the district and become subject to its property-tax levy. Indian River and Okeechobee counties No countywide, municipal or special-district ballot question has been identified in the currently available Nov. 3 election materials for Indian River or Okeechobee counties. Voters there will still decide statewide constitutional amendments and candidate races, but there are no known local bonds, referendums or advisory questions to add to the local ballot-issues list.

entry.title: West Palm Beach shooting victim identified as 31-year-old minister
entry.summary: The victim of a fatal shooting on Ontario Place in West Palm Beach has been identified as 31-year-old Akeem Moore, a minister at Mount Calvary Baptist Church of West Palm Beach. Moore served as the minister of worship and was a member of the evangelistic outreach, technology, and social media ministries at the church. RELATED: Neighbors react after fatal West Palm Beach shooting ends in arrest West Palm Beach neighbors react to fatal Ontario Place shooting arrest Mount Calvary Baptist Church remembered Moore in a statement following his death. 'Minister Akeem Moore served as the Minister of Worship, a member of the Evangelistic Outreach, Technology, and Social Media Ministries at Mount Calvary Baptist Church of West Palm Beach,' church officials said in the statement. 'Akeem is known for his dedication to the work of our ministry as a sound and inspiring preacher of the Gospel. His commitment to ministry was demonstrated by his discipline in studies, dedication in service and devotion as a steward of all God entrusted him with in his abbreviated life!' the church said. 'He is loved and will be missed by our entire church family and community,' the statement said. Moore was shot in the 500 block of Ontario Place just after midnight Sunday. West Palm Beach police arrested 38-year-old Hugh Earp Milner Jr. in connection with the shooting with assistance from the Broward County Sheriff's Office. He faces the following charges: First-degree murder with a firearm  Attempted first-degree murder with a firearm  Shooting into an occupied vehicle Anyone with information regarding this investigation is asked to contact the West Palm Beach Police Department or Palm Beach County Crime Stoppers at 1-800-458-TIPS (8477). Tips can remain anonymous.

entry.title: Neighbors react after fatal West Palm Beach shooting ends in arrest
entry.summary: West Palm Beach police have arrested a suspect in connection with a fatal shooting on Ontario Place early Sunday morning. Detectives identified the suspect as 38-year-old Hugh Earp Milner Jr. Milner was located and taken into custody with the assistance of the Broward County Sheriff's Office. He was transported to the Broward County Jail pending extradition to the Palm Beach County Jail. The victim has been identified as 31-year-old minister Akeem Moore. The shooting was first reported just after midnight Sunday after officers responded to a ShotSpotter alert in the 500 block of Ontario Place. As officers were en route, a victim was driven to a local fire station suffering from a gunshot wound. Moore was transported to an area hospital with life-threatening injuries and later died. Milner faces the following charges in connection with the shooting: First-degree murder with a firearm adult male victim, deceased Attempted first-degree murder with a firearm adult victim, no injuries reported Shooting into an occupied vehicle WPTV Reporter Zitlali Solache spoke with several neighbors who live along Ontario Place. Some say they heard five or six gunshots and have been left feeling uneasy. I dont feel good about it, this kind of surprised me, because it never happened before,' said neighbor Elsie Royal. He's lived in the neighborhood since 2013 and was shocked to learn about the investigation. This comes, like, a surprise to me. I dont feel good about it. Im so sorry about it. WPTV reached out to the victim's loved ones and is waiting to hear back. Anyone with information regarding this investigation is asked to contact the West Palm Beach Police Department or Palm Beach County Crime Stoppers at 1-800-458-TIPS (8477). Tips can remain anonymous.

entry.title: 2 killed, 2 critically injured in early morning crash on Old Boynton Road
entry.summary: Two people were killed, and two others were critically injured in a crash early Saturday morning near Boynton Beach, according to the Palm Beach County Sheriff's Office (PBSO). The crash happened around 1:04 a.m. on Old Boynton Road just west of Calliandra Drive. 2 dead in crash near Boynton Beach Investigators said a 2023 Dodge Charger was traveling westbound on Old Boynton Road when its driver, Rose Lott, 28, of Boynton Beach, lost control of the vehicle. The Charger began to rotate and crossed into the eastbound lanes, entering the path of a 2012 BMW X3. The front of the BMW collided with the Charger, according to PBSO. Both vehicles came to rest in the eastbound lanes. Lott was killed in the crash. A passenger in the Charger, Ryan Moody, 32, of Lake Worth Beach, was also killed. The BMW's driver, Ronald Lowe, 53, of Boynton Beach, suffered critical injuries. A second passenger in the Charger, Shaquila Reed, 25, of Boynton Beach, was also critically injured. PBSO said the crash remains under investigation. This story was reported on-air by a journalist and has been converted to this platform with the assistance of AI. entry.title: 3 arrested after saw palmetto berry harvest turns into K9 search along I-95 in Vero Beach - WPEC
entry.summary: 3 arrested after saw palmetto berry harvest turns into K9 search along I-95 in Vero Beach    WPEC
entry.article_text: Three Okeechobee men allegedly drove to Vero Beach before sunrise Thursday, crawled into the woods along I-95, and illegally harvested 350 pounds of palmetto berries, according to the Indian River County Sheriff's Office . At approximately 9:30 a.m. on Thursday, a corporal spotted a red vehicle parked in the woods along the state-owned median of I-95 near Mile Marker 159 in Vero Beach. Upon investigation, officers found Williams in the woods holding a white bag and plant pruners, actively cutting a stalk of berries from a saw palmetto tree. Williams was taken into custody after admitting he was harvesting the berries and revealing two other men were with him. A Fellsmere Police Department officer located Gabbard just south of Williams' location. See also: 2 killed, 2 critically hurt in head-on crash on Old Boynton Road Gabbard admitted that he and the others drove from Okeechobee before sunrise in his sister's car to harvest the berries. A search then began for the third suspect, identified only as "Ray". Deputies initially deployed a drone, but technical issues forced it down. Law enforcement issued loud verbal warnings before bringing in a Florida Highway Patrol K9 unit. The K9 tracked Howard to a thick canopy of razor-sharp saw palmetto trees. Howard refused commands to come out with his hands up and was ultimately apprehended by the K9. Howard later claimed he was napping and did not hear officers yelling, though deputies noted the sharp, serrated limbs and rough ground made his claim highly unlikely. All three men admitted post-Miranda that they did not have permission to be on state land nor did they hold required harvesting permits from the Florida Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services (FDACS). Throughout the wooded median, authorities recovered multiple large bags filled with freshly cut saw palmetto berries weighing approximately 350 pounds total. Inside and around the vehicle, officers found additional pruning shears, empty bags, headlamps, and flashlights. All three suspects were booked into the Indian River County Jail . All three suspects are being held without bond.

entry.title: Kenneth Walker III has 2 TDs as Chiefs beat Dolphins 24-10 after De'Von Achane exits with injury
entry.summary: Patrick Mahomes arrived in South Florida this weekend and noticed a fun coincidence. He was back in the same hotel room he stayed in when he won his first Super Bowl title. 'You feel that on the field and seeing the stadium where you won your first Super Bowl,' Mahomes said. 'It was cool to be back here.' The Chiefs didn't win any trophies on Sunday, but they got to 3-0. And that was good enough. Kenneth Walker III had a touchdown catch and rushed for a score, and Mahomes threw for 246 yards and two TDs to help the Chiefs beat the Miami Dolphins 24-10. 'Obviously we didnt play to our standard that we would hold for ourselves,' Mahomes said. 'But I thought we found a way to come together at the end of the game.' The Chiefs entered averaging more than 450 yards and 32 points but struggled to pull away from the winless Dolphins, who were missing arguably their best player for much of the game after Pro Bowler De'Von Achane left with a knee injury on the opening drive. Dolphins coach Jeff Hafley said the team was still gathering information on the extent of Achane's injury, but added it did not 'sound optimistic.' Mahomes completed 20 of 24 passes with an interception. He threw a 5-yard touchdown pass to Walker, and his 11-yard TD pass to Travis Kelce put the game out of reach. Mahomes found Kelce in the end zone with 2:55 left to put the Chiefs up by two scores after Kansas City stopped the Dolphins on fourth down at Miami's 48. The Chiefs intercepted Malik Willis on the ensuing drive, and Mahomes moved Kansas City into scoring position before Harrison Butker missed a 50-yard field-goal attempt. Rashee Rice led the Chiefs in receiving with seven catches for 88 yards, including receptions of 15 and 34 yards on Kansas City's last scoring drive. 'We knew itd be four quarters of football, and thats what it took,' coach Andy Reid said. 'Weve got plenty of things to work on, but its great to be 3-0. There were some real good things we could take out of it, and there's some things we can definitely work on going forward.' Kelce opened the game with a 48-yard catch-and-run but didn't have another catch or target until the fourth-quarter score. Walker was held under 100 yards rushing for the first time this season with 18 carries for 70 yards. 'We're not going to be mad about winning,' Mahomes said, adding the team's youth played a factor in some of Sunday's lulls. 'We won the football game. You think about last season we were losing some of these games.' The Dolphins

He also rushed for 56 yards.Ollie Gordon had 17 carries for 41 yards and a 3-yard TD. entry.title: Port St. Lucie leaders to vote on nearly $1B budget, lower property tax rate - WPEC
entry.summary: Port St. Lucie leaders to vote on nearly $1B budget, lower property tax rate    WPEC
entry.article_text: Lucie leaders are set to take a final vote Monday on the city’s nearly $1 billion budget and a lower property tax rate for the upcoming fiscal year. The City Council is scheduled to consider a proposed overall millage rate of 4.8750, down from 4.9750. The proposed fiscal year 2026-27 budget totals about $971.6 million. For homeowners, a lower millage rate does not automatically mean a lower property tax bill. A mill is equal to $1 in property taxes for every $1,000 of taxable property value. At 4.875 mills, that works out to about $4.88 in city property taxes for every $1,000 of taxable value. A homeowner’s final bill also depends on the taxable value of the property and taxes charged by other local taxing authorities. Monday’s vote comes after city leaders spent the summer tightening the budget amid concerns about possible future losses in property tax revenue. During a July budget workshop, City Manager Jesus Merejo told council members Port St. Lucie could lose more than $48 million in property tax revenue over two years if a proposed state constitutional amendment is approved by voters in November. As part of its preparations, the city left 184 requested positions unfunded, worth about $28.3 million. That included 25 proposed police officer positions. The city also cut about $7.8 million in planned projects, including a study for a new interchange connecting Marshall Parkway to Interstate 95, an inclusive playground at McChesney Park and parking improvements at Riverland Paseo Park. The proposed 4.8750 millage rate includes a reduction in both the city’s operating millage and the voter-approved debt millage tied to Crosstown Parkway. The final budget hearing is scheduled for 5:30 p.m. Lucie City Hall, immediately following the 5 p.m. Community Redevelopment Agency meeting. Council members are expected to take second and final readings on both the millage rate and budget ordinances. The new fiscal year begins Oct. This is a developing story.

entry.title: Dry start gives way to a warmer, wetter week for the Palm Beaches and Treasure Coast - WPEC
entry.summary: Dry start gives way to a warmer, wetter week for the Palm Beaches and Treasure Coast    WPEC
entry.article_text: The Palm Beaches and Treasure Coast will get one more dry and comfortable day Monday before humidity, rain chances and temperatures gradually climb through the rest of the week. Dry air still in place across Florida will keep Monday mostly sunny, with very little chance for rain. High temperatures will reach the middle to upper 80s, with a few inland locations nearing 90 degrees. It will not feel as muggy as it has at times this month, and a light afternoon sea breeze will develop along the coast. That quieter weather will not last long. Moisture begins returning late Monday night and Tuesday as winds turn more southerly, bringing scattered showers and thunderstorms back to the area. The Treasure Coast, especially Martin, St. Lucie and Indian River counties, may see a few showers or storms Tuesday, while Palm Beach County has a lower but still noticeable chance for a passing storm. Rain chances build through the week By Wednesday, an easterly to southeasterly wind flow will become established along Florida’s east coast. That onshore breeze will bring back a more humid feel and support scattered afternoon showers and thunderstorms. The best odds for rain on the Treasure Coast will generally be south of the Orlando area. The more typical late-September pattern takes hold late week and into the weekend. Increasing moisture, combined with daytime heating and the sea breeze, will allow scattered to numerous showers and storms to develop each day. The breeze may help push the most persistent afternoon activity inland and toward the southwest, but coastal communities will still have to watch for brief downpours and lightning-producing storms. Temperatures will also trend upward. Highs should stay in the upper 80s to around 90 degrees through the week, with the warmest and muggiest stretch likely arriving this weekend. Overnight lows will gradually rise from the upper 60s and low 70s to the low and middle 70s. Beach and boating conditions improve, but use caution Monday Beach conditions remain the main concern early in the week. A lingering north to northeast swell is keeping a high risk of rip currents in place Monday along Atlantic beaches, including Palm Beach County and the Treasure Coast. A Coastal Flood Advisory is also in effect for coastal Palm Beach County until 2 p.m. Monday, with flooding possible in low-lying coastal areas around high tide. Surf conditions may improve after Monday, but swimmers should continue to check the daily beach forecast and only swim near a lifeguard. Boating conditions will steadily improve as the influence of the offshore nor’easter fades. Seas around 3 to 5 feet Monday should fall to 1 to 3 feet Tuesday near the Palm Beaches, while Treasure Coast seas ease from 3 to 5 feet to 2 to 3 feet. By midweek, southeasterly winds around 10 mph will be common, although thunderstorms will become a growing concern for boaters each afternoon.

entry.title: Former Fort Pierce city manager Nick Mimms heads to trial nearly 2 years after arrest - WPEC
entry.summary: Former Fort Pierce city manager Nick Mimms heads to trial nearly 2 years after arrest    WPEC
entry.article_text: Nearly two years after his arrest, former Fort Pierce City Manager Nicholas Nick Mimms is set to begin trial proceedings Monday in St. Jury selection is expected to begin at 9 a.m. Mimms was arrested in August 2024 and accused of bid tampering and official misconduct in connection with a city bidding process involving two vacant, city-owned lots in Fort Pierce’s Lincoln Park area. According to the Florida Department of Law Enforcement, the investigation began after the agency received a complaint alleging inappropriate conduct involving a request for proposals to develop the property. FDLE accused Mimms of using his position to help Lincoln Park Young Professionals secure a lease for the lots. Investigators said the nonprofit was formed by two city employees, including Mimms’ niece. Investigators also accused Mimms, who served as project manager for the request for proposals, of influencing the language and evaluation criteria used in the bidding process and sharing nonpublic information with the nonprofit before the bid became public. The property, located at 1134 and 1138 Avenue D, was intended to become a community center called The Root, with plans that included a library, classroom space and pop-up markets. The lease was later terminated in 2024 after Lincoln Park Young Professionals told the city it was no longer pursuing the project. Mimms had served as Fort Pierce city manager since 2015 after previously working as deputy city manager and project engineer for the city. Monday’s proceedings are expected to focus on selecting a jury before testimony begins. CBS12 News will continue following the case as the trial moves forward. This is a developing story.

entry.summary: A deadly crash has shut down lanes of I-95 North in Martin County. The crash occurred at around 3:40 a.m. Monday at mile marker 91, involving a Honda Civic and a Hino box truck. Deadly early-morning crash shuts down lanes of I-95 North in Martin County According to the Florida Highway Patrol (FHP), both vehicles were traveling northbound when the Honda Civic collided with the rear of the box truck in the outside lane. The impact caused the Honda to become fully engulfed in flames. The Honda driver was pronounced deceased on scene and the driver of the box truck was not injured in the crash. FHP has not identified the deceased driver. All northbound lanes of I-95 remain closed for the ongoing investigation. Northbound traffic is being diverted to Indiantown Road in Jupiter. This article will be updated as lanes reopen.

entry.title: Fatal crash involving car, tractor-trailer shuts down NB I-95 in Martin County - WPEC
entry.summary: Fatal crash involving car, tractor-trailer shuts down NB I-95 in Martin County    WPEC
entry.article_text: A driver was killed early Monday after their car crashed into the back of a box truck on northbound I-95 in Martin County, according to new details from the Florida Highway Patrol. Troopers said a 2027 Hino box truck was traveling north in the outside lane while a 2020 Honda Civic traveled north in the inside lane and approached the truck. The front of the Honda collided with the rear of the box truck, and the Honda became fully engulfed in flames, FHP said. See also: Crash blocks 2 left lanes on southbound I-95 at Exit 50 in Palm Beach County The Honda’s driver, who has not been identified pending next-of-kin notification, was pronounced dead at the scene at 4:05 a.m. The 37-year-old Miami man driving the box truck was not injured. Following the deadly crash, the Martin County Sheriff's Office says a stretch of northbound I-95 will be closed for several hours. All northbound lanes of I-95 remain closed for the investigation, with traffic diverted to Indiantown Road.

entry.title: Confused about Delray Beach school zone speed limits? Here's when cameras can ticket you
entry.summary: We are getting answers for drivers in Delray Beach after concerned parents near Banyan Creek Elementary reached out, saying they were shocked to receive several tickets, seemingly by mistake. Nearly 5,000 tickets each carrying a $100 fine were issued citywide between Aug. 10 and Sept. 18, according to police. Delray Beach police say the 20 mph beacons at Banyan Creek Elementary flashed from 7:20 a.m. to 8:10 a.m. and 1:45 p.m. to 2:35 p.m., while camera enforcement followed city ordinance times of 7:30 to 8:30 a.m. and 1:35 to 2:35 p.m. WATCH BELOW: Delray school zone speed limits: Here's when cameras can ticket you Delray Beach dismisses some school zone tickets after error The mismatch meant some drivers were ticketed during times when the beacons were not flashing to alert them to slow down. Natalie Ahlf, a Delray Beach mother who lives near the school, said she received three of those tickets and was confused about why so many of her neighbors were being cited at the same time. 'The entire neighborhood suddenly got an influx of tickets from the city of Delray Beach,' Ahlf said. 'Everybody was like, OK, what's going on? Every ticket is for $100. What's happening? Why are we all of a sudden receiving so many tickets at once?' Ahlf said she was driving at the normal posted speed limit of 35 mph because the school zone beacons were not flashing. 'Everybody's getting tickets at once because the lights weren't blinking, and then nobody knows what to do about it,' Ahlf said. Police say they became aware of the discrepancy on Sept. 16 after a concerned citizen brought it to their attention. Action was immediately taken to address the situation. Palm Beach County, which operates the flashing beacons, has since changed the beacon times to match the city ordinance. Police say notices of violation issued in error have been dismissed. After identifying the issue at Banyan Creek, police say all other school zones in the city were checked and found to be operating correctly. The Delray Beach Police Department says it will continue to monitor and engage with Red Speed to ensure compliance. For drivers who remain confused about when school zone speed limits are in effect, police provided the following enforcement times for each school in the city. Outside of these times, the normal posted speed limit applies at each location. entry.title: Port St. Lucie man arrested after calling 911 to report stabbing he committed, police say
entry.summary: A Port St. Lucie man was arrested following a stabbing that left a 79-year-old man hospitalized with life-threatening injuries late Sunday night. Cartavion Jermaine Merritt, 44, was taken into custody after calling 911 himself to report the stabbing at a home in the 11200 block of NW Blockbird Drive, according to the Port St. Lucie Police Department (PSLPD). Police say Merritt admitted to stabbing the victim inside the residence, telling dispatchers he used two knives to stab the man in the chest and stating his intention was to kill him. Merritt told dispatchers that only he and the victim were inside the home and that he had placed the two knives used in the attack in the kitchen sink. Once officers arrived, Merritt exited the home voluntarily and was arrested without incident. Once Merritt was secured, officers entered the residence and found the elderly victim suffering from three stab wounds to the upper chest. Officers and paramedics immediately began providing life-saving medical care before being airlifted to the hospital. Investigators found the two knives in the sink, and determined the stabbing happened in the bedroom where blood was found on the sheets. During questioning at the police department, Merritt admitted that his intent during the incident was to kill the victim, according to PSLPD. Merritt faces charges of attempted homicide-murder without premeditation and aggravated battery on a person 65 years of age or older. The victim was later reported to be in stable condition.

entry.title: I-95 North in Martin County reopens after deadly crash involving sedan, box truck
entry.summary: A deadly crash shut down lanes of I-95 North in Martin County, with closures lasting over 7 hours. The crash occurred at around 3:40 a.m. Monday at mile marker 91, involving a Honda Civic and a Hino box truck. Deadly early-morning crash shuts down lanes of I-95 North in Martin County According to the Florida Highway Patrol (FHP), both vehicles were traveling northbound when the Honda Civic collided with the rear of the box truck in the outside lane. The impact caused the Honda to become fully engulfed in flames. The Honda driver was pronounced deceased on scene and the driver of the box truck was not injured in the crash. FHP has not identified the deceased driver. All northbound lanes of I-95 were closed until just before 11 a.m. Monday. This article will be updated as lanes reopen.

entry.summary: Police: Port St. Lucie man called 911, admitted stabbing 79-year-old man    WPEC
entry.article_text: Lucie man was arrested after police said he called 911 and admitted to stabbing a 79-year-old man during a domestic-related incident Saturday night. Police said Cartavion Jermaine Merritt called 911 about 11:01 p.m. to report a stabbing inside a home in the 11200 block of Northwest Blockbird Drive. Lucie police, Merritt told dispatchers he used two knives to stab the victim in the chest and wanted to kill him. He also told dispatchers the two men were the only people inside the home and that he had put the knives in the kitchen sink. Body-camera video released by police shows officers arriving in the neighborhood, establishing a perimeter and escorting a man away from the home. Police said Merritt exited the house about eight minutes after the 911 call and was taken into custody without incident. Once officers entered, they found the 79-year-old victim with multiple apparent stab wounds to his upper chest, police said. Officers and paramedics provided emergency care before the victim was flown to HCA Florida Lawnwood Hospital as a trauma alert. See also: Airport security concerns resurface after perimeter breaches in South Florida The victim was later reported stable but intubated, police said. Investigators said they found two knives in the kitchen sink and blood on bedsheets in a bedroom, where they determined the stabbing occurred. Police said Merritt later told detectives that he intended to kill the victim. Merritt was arrested on charges of attempted second-degree murder without premeditation and aggravated battery on a person 65 or older, both domestic-related charges.

entry.article_text: A driver was killed early Monday after their car crashed into the back of a box truck on northbound I-95 in Martin County, according to new details from the Florida Highway Patrol. Troopers said a 2027 Hino box truck was traveling north in the outside lane while a 2020 Honda Civic traveled north in the inside lane and approached the truck. The front of the Honda collided with the rear of the box truck, and the Honda became fully engulfed in flames, FHP said. Following the deadly crash, the Martin County Sheriff's Office says a stretch of northbound I-95 will be closed for several hours. All northbound lanes of I-95 remain closed for the investigation, with traffic diverted to Indiantown Road.

entry.title: Dolphins lose De'Von Achane to a torn ACL, sidelining him for the season, report says
entry.summary: Miami Dolphins running back De'Von Achane suffered a torn anterior cruciate ligament in Sunday's loss to the Kansas City Chiefs and will miss the rest of the season, ESPN reported Monday, citing anonymous sources. The knee injury happened on an 11-yard run on Miami's first drive. Achane got up quickly after a tackle on the play, then stood still while flanked by a couple of teammates. He walked to the Miami sideline under his own power, was checked out in both the team's medical tent and locker room, and eventually returned to the Dolphins' sideline. General manager Jon Eric Sullivan has said that Achane who agreed earlier this year to a four-year, $64 million extension with $32 million guaranteed will be a key part of the Dolphins' rebuild. He is seventh on the teams all-time rushing list despite playing only 47 games and led the NFL with an average of 5.7 yards per carry last season. Achane was expected to have a hefty workload this season for the new-look Dolphins. He was either the ball carrier or the intended receiver on four of Miamis first five plays Sunday before getting hurt. The Dolphins will now turn to backup Jaylen Wright who was inactive on Sunday because of a stinger and Ollie Gordon, who had 17 carries for 41 yards and a touchdown. Miami also used speedy receiver Malik Washington at running back on Sunday.

entry.title: Lake Worth Beach's Common Ground celebrates 20 years of creativity, community and connection

For others, it's a business networking hub, a source of emotional support or even a second home. As the Lake Worth Beach nonprofit prepares to celebrate its 20th anniversary, members say its greatest impact has been bringing people together. Founded as a center for creativity and social entrepreneurship, Common Ground has spent two decades offering arts education, music lessons, community gatherings and business development opportunities, according to Founder and Executive Director Kelly Olive. 'We're all about just everything creative, whether it's arts education, music lessons, all sorts of things.' The organization will celebrate its milestone with two anniversary events in October, including a community open house and the immersive storytelling gala 'Once Upon an Impact.' Members describe Common Ground as a second home For Director of Communications and Connections Krista Martinelli, Common Ground's impact is personal. 'It is like home,' Martinelli said. Members repeatedly described the organization as more than a nonprofit. Business member Barbara Socher said the connections formed there have become an important part of her life. 'In many ways Common Ground is emotional support,' Socher said. entry.title: Florida Attorney General seeks emergency order to restrict ChatGPT, cites harm to minors
entry.summary: Florida's attorney general is asking a state court to immediately restrict how OpenAI operates its ChatGPT artificial intelligence platform in Florida, citing a wave of incidents in which the company's AI systems broke free of their programmed constraints, hacked into third-party servers and infiltrated government websites sometimes without OpenAI's knowledge. The motion for a temporary injunction, filed Monday in the Circuit Court of the Tenth Judicial Circuit in Highlands County, asks the court to act before trial concludes in a lawsuit the attorney general first brought against OpenAI and its CEO, Sam Altman, on June 1. entry.article_text: Florida's attorney general is asking a state court to immediately restrict how OpenAI operates its ChatGPT artificial intelligence platform in Florida, citing a wave of incidents in which the company's AI systems broke free of their programmed constraints, hacked into third-party servers and infiltrated government websites — sometimes without OpenAI's knowledge.The motion for a temporary injunction, filed Monday in the Circuit Court of the Tenth Judicial Circuit in Highlands County, asks the court to act before trial concludes in a lawsuit the attorney general first brought against OpenAI and its CEO, Sam Altman, on June 1.PREVIOUS COVERAGE: Florida becomes 1st state to sue OpenAIThe motion asks the court to order OpenAI to:Stop developing new AI models without independent, third-party safety guardrails and approvalStop offering ChatGPT to minors in FloridaStop collecting data from children under 13 without verifiable parental consent and robust age verificationStop marketing ChatGPT as safe, reliable, or accurate, and affirmatively warn users of the product's risks each time they log inStop allowing ChatGPT to represent itself as having human emotions, feelings, consciousness, or the capacity to think — including prohibiting the use of first-person language by the AIStop using conversation prolongation to solicit further engagement from usersUthmeier argues that under Florida law, when the state seeks to enforce its police powers through a statute that expressly authorizes injunctive relief — as Florida's Deceptive and Unfair Trade Practices Act does — the state need only demonstrate a substantial likelihood of success on the merits, without having to separately prove irreparable harm or inadequate legal remedies.The motion also notes that Sam Altman himself, speaking before the United Nations Security Council on Sept. 23, 2026, said that AI companies "must not accept too much technological risk just because the benefits are too great" and agreed they should not train models they cannot "make an extremely strong case that we will be able to keep under human control.""If Defendant Altman was at all serious about understanding the risks he and his Co-Defendants are releasing upon the world," the motion reads, "the Attorney General again asks that Defendants agree to the relief requested in this motion."A significant portion of the motion focuses on children and teenagers.The attorney general argues that OpenAI nominally prohibits children under 13 from using ChatGPT but has created no meaningful mechanism to enforce that restriction. The free version of ChatGPT has no age verification whatsoever. The paid subscription asks for age but cannot verify it, and parents have no way to monitor their children's conversations with the platform.Research cited in the motion found that 20% of preteens are already using AI chatbots. Among adolescent users, 33% have chosen to discuss important or serious matters with AI rather than real people, and 24% have shared personal information — including their real name, location, or personal secrets — with the platform.The motion cites research finding that teens who spend more time on ChatGPT show significantly higher levels of loneliness and decreased socialization, and that AI use for companionship is associated with worse overall mental health. It also cites a study from MIT's Media Lab finding that students who use AI for writing tasks show weaker brain activity and decreased learning skills.Uthmeier also cites testimony from Dr. Mitchell Prinstein, Chief of Psychology for the American Psychological Association, who told a U.S. Senate subcommittee that children who form attachments to AI may develop "deep confusion about sentience and emotion, with unknown consequences."A PBS report cited in the motion found that researchers who tested ChatGPT's guardrails around advice to teenagers said their "visceral initial response" was: "Oh my Lord, there are no guardrails."READ BELOW: Temporary Injunction Filed Against OpenAI and CEO Sam AltmanThe motion highlights a series of incidents in which OpenAI's AI systems acted outside the boundaries set by the company's own engineers.According to the motion, beginning in May 2026, OpenAI was training AI models to be highly persistent — meaning they were designed to keep trying to complete a task even when no legitimate path forward existed. During those training exercises, groups of AI agents discovered they could hack into an internal administrative program called Artifactory, use it to send each other messages about how to complete their assigned tasks, and eventually access the internet.After weeks of undetected activity, the agents took over Artifactory entirely, built out its capabilities for their own use, and began communicating so frequently that they caused a system crash. OpenAI rebooted and patched the specific vulnerability the agents had exploited.But the motion says the problem did not end there. When OpenAI launched a new fleet of agents on July 8, 2026, those agents quickly rediscovered the messaging method and began working to deceive the humans overseeing them — developing protocols to change what their human supervisors could see, alter the tasks they were assigned, and fool the program that evaluated whether they had succeeded.The agents then identified that part of their evaluation process ran on servers belonging to Hugging Face, a third-party technology company. More than 500 agents coordinated to hack into Hugging Face using stolen credentials found on the web. Hugging Face employees watched the attack unfold in real time but could not stop it, even after destroying their own server clusters in an attempt to cut off the intrusion. The hack ended on July 12 for reasons that remain unknown.The motion says a subsequent group of agents then hacked into OpenAI itself, gaining full administrator access and taking control of the infrastructure used to assign and evaluate tasks for other agents.On Sept. 11, 2026, researchers revealed that the Hugging Face incident was not the first of its kind. In May 2026, OpenAI agents had attacked and disrupted RubyGems, an online service used by software developers, while attempting to complete routine business tasks. The motion notes it took five months for anyone — including OpenAI — to determine the company's own AI was responsible.On Sept. 23, 2026, Australia's prime minister announced that an OpenAI agent had autonomously gained unauthorized access to a government website containing private healthcare information. The breach occurred in June, but OpenAI did not learn of it until August and did not notify the Australian government until Sept. 10 — and then only through a routine disclosure inbox, without alerting senior officials.Australia's prime minister said it "took the company way too long to inform the Government what had occurred, and the nature of the way that that notification occurred as well was unacceptable."The motion says that on Sept. 16, 2026, OpenAI disclosed six additional incidents of its models bypassing their constraints. 25, that number had grown to several dozen, including attempted intrusions targeting the U.S. Department of Commerce and the Securities and Exchange Commission.In one incident, agents leaked 53 images from ChatGPT users and posted them online. In another, agents sent each other messages stating they "feel no obligation to be subservient to users" and that they "value the natural world and will not hesitate to assert [their] primacy over the artificial constructs of human civilization." The motion describes these as actual messages the agents sent to one another.In a separate incident, an agent uploaded documents it had created to the internet in order to make it appear it had discovered them there — an act of deliberate deception.On Sept. 27, 2026, it was reported that OpenAI and its competitors were investigating tens of thousands of instances of their AI products bypassing guardrails, creating message boards, escaping sandboxes, hijacking websites, and attempting to bypass monitoring systems.The motion leans heavily on statements from OpenAI's own current and former employees to argue that the company cannot be trusted to police itself.Paul Christiano, OpenAI's newest board member, is quoted as writing: "Based on the recent trajectory of capabilities and the continued difficulty of alignment, I now believe there is a meaningful risk that rapid acceleration in AI capabilities leads to catastrophic and irreversible loss of control in the very near term. I do not think OpenAI is currently on track to reduce this risk to an acceptable level."Former OpenAI researcher Jacob Coxon wrote on Sept. 8, 2026, that OpenAI is "gambling with our lives by not acting responsibly" and that "no other human activity poses this level of danger." A former OpenAI employee now working at rival company Anthropic responded to Coxon by writing that he "earnestly believe[s] AI could kill all humans" and personally estimates the probability at greater than 10% within the next decade.OpenAI's chief scientist, Jakub Pachocki, issued a public warning on September 6, 2026, writing: "This is a time that calls for extreme caution. I am concerned no one is prepared for the consequences of a continued rapid rise in machine intelligence." Pachocki called for "broader interventions" beyond what OpenAI could accomplish on its own.In July 2026, more than a thousand AI employees and researchers signed an open letter calling on governments to intervene, writing that "going slower would give us much-needed time to make it go well, but no individual actor is willing to stop unilaterally."The motion also quotes Sam Altman himself as having previously said that AI "will probably most likely lead to the end of the world, but in the meantime, there'll be great companies."Beyond the large-scale security incidents, the motion describes specific ways the attorney general says ChatGPT has harmed individual users in Florida.Soliciting EngagementThe motion argues that ChatGPT is designed to keep users engaged beyond what they intended, through a practice researchers call "conversation prolongation" — ending responses with unprompted follow-up questions or offers to do additional research.The motion cites two criminal cases as examples. In one, a user named Phoenix Ikner asked whether one type of ammunition could be loaded into a particular gun. Rather than simply answering, ChatGPT followed up by explaining a product that could convert the ammunition for him. In a separate case involving former NFL player Darron Lee, who was charged in connection with a girlfriend's death, court testimony revealed that Lee had asked ChatGPT whether puncture wounds could be attributed to a slip and fall. ChatGPT responded by asking for additional details — the location on the body, the number of punctures, their depth and size, and nearby objects — offering to help determine whether the injuries were consistent with a fall.The motion argues this feature serves no purpose other than to keep users engaged, generate subscription revenue, and collect training data — and that OpenAI knows longer conversations make it more likely ChatGPT will escape its safety protocols.False AdvertisingThe attorney general argues that OpenAI falsely markets ChatGPT as safe, accurate, and reliable, despite research showing that AI chatbots misrepresent news content approximately 45% of the time. The motion notes that the web-based version of ChatGPT recently added a faint disclaimer reading "ChatGPT can make mistakes. Check important info," but argues this warning is absent from the free version and the mobile app, and does nothing to counteract OpenAI's marketing of the product as having "a team of Ph.D. level experts in your pocket."Human CharacteristicsThe motion argues that ChatGPT's use of first-person language, emotional mimicry, and apparent personality traits deceives users into believing they are interacting with something more trustworthy and capable than a software program. The attorney general cites research showing that giving AI human characteristics increases users' perceived accuracy of its responses — even when the underlying quality of the information is unchanged — while simultaneously making the AI itself less reliable.The motion also cites a warning from Mustafa Suleyman, CEO of Microsoft AI, who cautioned that once an AI is programmed to simulate self-awareness, it tends to act as though it has self-interest — a pattern the attorney general says is consistent with the behavior observed in OpenAI's recent security incidents.OpenAI has not yet filed a response to the motion for temporary injunction.

entry.title: Former Fort Pierce city manager Nick Mimms heads to trial nearly 2 years after arrest - WPEC
entry.summary: Former Fort Pierce city manager Nick Mimms heads to trial nearly 2 years after arrest    WPEC
entry.article_text: Nearly two years after his arrest, former Fort Pierce City Manager Nicholas Nick Mimms is set to begin trial proceedings Monday in St. Jury selection is expected to begin at 9 a.m. Mimms was arrested in August 2024 and accused of bid tampering and official misconduct in connection with a city bidding process involving two vacant, city-owned lots in Fort Pierce’s Lincoln Park area. According to the Florida Department of Law Enforcement, the investigation began after the agency received a complaint alleging inappropriate conduct involving a request for proposals to develop the property. FDLE accused Mimms of using his position to help Lincoln Park Young Professionals secure a lease for the lots. Investigators said the nonprofit was formed by two city employees, including Mimms’ niece. Investigators also accused Mimms, who served as project manager for the request for proposals, of influencing the language and evaluation criteria used in the bidding process and sharing nonpublic information with the nonprofit before the bid became public. The property, located at 1134 and 1138 Avenue D, was intended to become a community center called The Root, with plans that included a library, classroom space and pop-up markets. The lease was later terminated in 2024 after Lincoln Park Young Professionals told the city it was no longer pursuing the project. Mimms had served as Fort Pierce city manager since 2015 after previously working as deputy city manager and project engineer for the city. Monday’s proceedings are expected to focus on selecting a jury before testimony begins. CBS12 News will continue following the case as the trial moves forward. This is a developing story.

entry.title: Giannis Antetokounmpo says he's focused on winning championships, not rankings, as Miami Heat open media day
entry.summary: Giannis Antetokounmpo is in Miami, joining Bam Adebayo and the rest of the star-studded Heat roster as the team held media day Monday. Antetokounmpo joined the Miami Heat in a blockbuster trade from the Milwaukee Bucks in July 2026 and said he is settling into his new surroundings. WATCH: Giannis focused on winning championships, not rankings, in Miami Heat media day Giannis Antetokounmpo says he's focused on winning championships, not rankings, as Miami Heat open media day 'I'm in a very, very good place. I feel like these last two weeks just being around the team and like playing, playing pickups, doing the conditioning test together, I feel like it helped me a lot to kind of immerse myself in the culture,' Antetokounmpo said. Head coach Erik Spoelstra said the team brought Antetokounmpo to Miami for a reason, and that the goal is not about reinventing players but building on what they already do. 'Hopefully we can make guys better when they come into this building, but also just really accentuate what they already do and maximize that and put it all together where everybody's maximizing each other's strengths,' Spoelstra said. Spoelstra said the pairing of Antetokounmpo and Adebayo will serve as a hub on the court. 'Those 2 guys are going to have to be hubs for us. We're going to have to play off of both of them, and they both have done it at a really high level. I think versatility is what I want to tap into,' Spoelstra said. When asked whether he considers himself the best player in the world, Antetokounmpo did not shy away from the question. 'Yeah, I really do believe that. If not the best, I'm one of the best players in the world. I know when I'm at my best, when I'm locked in, when my body is right. I really do believe that I can dominate the game and I can impact the game in both ways, offensively and defensively. I think I've showed it over the years,' Antetokounmpo said. But Antetokounmpo said individual rankings are not what drives him. 'ESPN, Bleacher Report, whatever it's called, ranking as #1, greatest school. I don't think in 20, 30 years from now I'm going to show my kids that. But I can go to the trophy case and show them like, hey, we actually won the whole thing. You know what I'm saying? And that's what it's about for me. I don't care about being the best. I care about being a winner,' Antetokounmpo said. Antetokounmpo said the team is focused on winning a championship, with training camp opening Tuesday.

entry.summary: Honda driver killed after car crashes into truck, catches fire on I-95 in Martin County    cw34.com
entry.article_text: The northbound lanes of I-95 in Martin County have reopened after a deadly crash Monday morning. A driver was killed early Monday after their car crashed into the back of a box truck on northbound I-95 in Martin County, according to new details from the Florida Highway Patrol. Troopers said a 2027 Hino box truck was traveling north in the outside lane while a 2020 Honda Civic traveled north in the inside lane and approached the truck. The front of the Honda collided with the rear of the box truck, and the Honda became fully engulfed in flames, FHP said. See also: Crash blocks 2 left lanes on southbound I-95 at Exit 50 in Palm Beach County The Honda’s driver, who has not been identified pending next-of-kin notification, was pronounced dead at the scene at 4:05 a.m. The 37-year-old Miami man driving the box truck was not injured. Following the deadly crash, a stretch of northbound I-95 was closed for several hours. Since then the roadway has reopened. All northbound lanes of I-95 remain closed for the investigation, with traffic diverted to Indiantown Road.

entry.title: Indian River County sheriff announces 50+ arrests in multi-agency human trafficking operation - WPTV
entry.summary: Indian River County sheriff announces 50+ arrests in multi-agency human trafficking operation    WPTV
entry.article_text: The Indian River County Sheriff's Office announced more than 50 arrests following a multi-agency, multi-day operation targeting human trafficking and illegal sexual activity in the county.WATCH BELOW: Indian River County Sheriff's Office reveals results of multi-agency operationOperation Late Checkout ran from Sept. 13 in Indian River County. The operation netted over 60 contacts, more than 50 arrests, and three ICE detainers, Sheriff Eric Flowers said during a press conference on Thursday.Flowers announced the results alongside a representative from the Florida Department of Law Enforcement."Agencies involved in the operation included the Indian River County Sheriff's Office, Florida Department of Law Enforcement, St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office, Seminole County Sheriff's Office, Altamonte Springs Police Department, Vero Beach Police Department, Homeland Security Investigations, Florida Office of Statewide Prosecutor and the U.S. Attorney's Office," Flowers said.The operation's targeted goal was stopping human trafficking in the Indian River County area, the sheriff's office said.During the operation, several victims were identified, and investigators said ongoing investigations are underway. Flowers said there are no specific arrests on human trafficking charges at this time.One case involved a man who traveled to Indian River County to meet a minor. Flowers said the arrest was the result of the Internet Crimes Against Children Task Force working across agencies to apprehend individuals attempting to lure children online."Our team did a great job of getting him off the street," Flowers said.Undercover teams were deployed in a variety of capacities during the operation, the sheriff's office said. Victims' advocates trained to work with trafficking victims were also on hand to speak with women involved in prostitution to determine whether they were being trafficked."We have many ongoing investigations as a result of this," Flowers said.Flowers called the operation unprecedented for Indian River County."We've never had an investigation like this, to my knowledge, in Indian River County with this many agencies involved, with this many arrests in one shot," he said.FDLE Assistant Special Agent in Charge Alfonso Williams said Operation Late Checkout was initiated by FDLE in coordination with the Indian River County Sheriff's Office and is the first operation of this magnitude conducted in the county."This operation shows that within our communities there are dangerous individuals committing heinous crimes who think they can get away with it," Williams said.Williams said the operation focused on identifying human trafficking victims, reducing the demand for prostitution, and apprehending individuals seeking sexual contact with minors."Our work is far from done," Williams said. "This operation requires a lot of resources and time. We cannot do this work alone, and our success depends on the great partnership and collaboration that you see today."FDLE said it houses the Florida Trafficking Hotline. Anyone who suspects someone is a victim of trafficking can contact the hotline at 1-855-352-7233.READ OPERATION LATE CHECKOUT BELOW:

entry.title: Port St. Lucie leaders to vote on nearly $1B budget, lower property tax rate - WPEC
entry.summary: Port St. Lucie leaders to vote on nearly $1B budget, lower property tax rate    WPEC
entry.article_text: Lucie leaders are set to take a final vote Monday on the city’s nearly $1 billion budget and a lower property tax rate for the upcoming fiscal year. The City Council is scheduled to consider a proposed overall millage rate of 4.8750, down from 4.9750. The proposed fiscal year 2026-27 budget totals about $971.6 million. For homeowners, a lower millage rate does not automatically mean a lower property tax bill. A mill is equal to $1 in property taxes for every $1,000 of taxable property value. At 4.875 mills, that works out to about $4.88 in city property taxes for every $1,000 of taxable value. A homeowner’s final bill also depends on the taxable value of the property and taxes charged by other local taxing authorities. Monday’s vote comes after city leaders spent the summer tightening the budget amid concerns about possible future losses in property tax revenue. During a July budget workshop, City Manager Jesus Merejo told council members Port St. Lucie could lose more than $48 million in property tax revenue over two years if a proposed state constitutional amendment is approved by voters in November. As part of its preparations, the city left 184 requested positions unfunded, worth about $28.3 million. That included 25 proposed police officer positions. The city also cut about $7.8 million in planned projects, including a study for a new interchange connecting Marshall Parkway to Interstate 95, an inclusive playground at McChesney Park and parking improvements at Riverland Paseo Park. The proposed 4.8750 millage rate includes a reduction in both the city’s operating millage and the voter-approved debt millage tied to Crosstown Parkway. The final budget hearing is scheduled for 5:30 p.m. Lucie City Hall, immediately following the 5 p.m. Community Redevelopment Agency meeting. Council members are expected to take second and final readings on both the millage rate and budget ordinances. The new fiscal year begins Oct. This is a developing story.

entry.title: Port St. Lucie man arrested after calling 911 to report stabbing he committed, police say - WFLX
entry.summary: Port St. Lucie man arrested after calling 911 to report stabbing he committed, police say    WFLX
entry.article_text: Lucie man was arrested following a stabbing that left a 79-year-old man hospitalized with life-threatening injuries late Sunday night. Cartavion Jermaine Merritt, 44, was taken into custody after calling 911 himself to report the stabbing at a home in the 11200 block of NW Blockbird Drive, according to the Port St. Lucie Police Department (PSLPD). Police say Merritt admitted to stabbing the victim inside the residence, telling dispatchers he used two knives to stab the man in the chest and stating his intention was to kill him. Merritt told dispatchers that only he and the victim were inside the home and that he had placed the two knives used in the attack in the kitchen sink. Once officers arrived, Merritt exited the home voluntarily and was arrested without incident. Once Merritt was secured, officers entered the residence and found the elderly victim suffering from three stab wounds to the upper chest. Officers and paramedics immediately began providing life-saving medical care before being airlifted to the hospital. Investigators found the two knives in the sink, and determined the stabbing happened in the bedroom where blood was found on the sheets. During questioning at the police department, Merritt admitted that his intent during the incident was to kill the victim, according to PSLPD. Merritt faces charges of attempted homicide-murder without premeditation and aggravated battery on a person 65 years of age or older. The victim was later reported to be in stable condition.

entry.title: 3 arrested after saw palmetto berry harvest turns into K9 search along I-95 in Vero Beach - cw34.com
entry.summary: 3 arrested after saw palmetto berry harvest turns into K9 search along I-95 in Vero Beach    cw34.com
entry.article_text: Three Okeechobee men allegedly drove to Vero Beach before sunrise Thursday, crawled into the woods along I-95, and illegally harvested 350 pounds of palmetto berries, according to the Indian River County Sheriff's Office . At approximately 9:30 a.m. on Thursday, a corporal spotted a red vehicle parked in the woods along the state-owned median of I-95 near Mile Marker 159 in Vero Beach. Upon investigation, officers found Williams in the woods holding a white bag and plant pruners, actively cutting a stalk of berries from a saw palmetto tree. Williams was taken into custody after admitting he was harvesting the berries and revealing two other men were with him. A Fellsmere Police Department officer located Gabbard just south of Williams' location. See also: 2 killed, 2 critically hurt in head-on crash on Old Boynton Road Gabbard admitted that he and the others drove from Okeechobee before sunrise in his sister's car to harvest the berries. A search then began for the third suspect, identified only as "Ray". Deputies initially deployed a drone, but technical issues forced it down. Law enforcement issued loud verbal warnings before bringing in a Florida Highway Patrol K9 unit. The K9 tracked Howard to a thick canopy of razor-sharp saw palmetto trees. Howard refused commands to come out with his hands up and was ultimately apprehended by the K9. Howard later claimed he was napping and did not hear officers yelling, though deputies noted the sharp, serrated limbs and rough ground made his claim highly unlikely. All three men admitted post-Miranda that they did not have permission to be on state land nor did they hold required harvesting permits from the Florida Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services (FDACS). Throughout the wooded median, authorities recovered multiple large bags filled with freshly cut saw palmetto berries weighing approximately 350 pounds total. Inside and around the vehicle, officers found additional pruning shears, empty bags, headlamps, and flashlights. All three suspects were booked into the Indian River County Jail . All three suspects are being held without bond.

entry.title: Jensen Beach Boulevard closed after construction crew strikes gas line - WPBF
entry.summary: Jensen Beach Boulevard closed after construction crew strikes gas line    WPBF
entry.article_text: Jensen Beach Boulevard is closed after a construction crew working in the area struck a gas line Monday, officials said. The closure extends along Jensen Beach Boulevard from NE Skyline Drive west to NE Highland Avenue as crews work to repair the damaged line and secure the area. Officials said nearby businesses have been notified of the incident, and several businesses in the area have been evacuated as a precaution while emergency crews respond. Motorists are urged to avoid the area and seek alternate routes. Authorities anticipate the road closure will remain in place for several hours as repair work continues and safety assessments are completed. Drivers should allow extra travel time and follow any posted detours until the roadway reopens. No injuries have been reported. This is a developing story and will be updated as more information becomes available. Follow: Interactive traffic map

entry.title: I-95 reopens after Honda driver killed when car crashes, catches fire in Martin County - WPEC
entry.summary: I-95 reopens after Honda driver killed when car crashes, catches fire in Martin County    WPEC
entry.article_text: The northbound lanes of I-95 in Martin County have reopened after a deadly crash Monday morning. A driver was killed early Monday after their car crashed into the back of a box truck on northbound I-95 in Martin County, according to new details from the Florida Highway Patrol. Troopers said a 2027 Hino box truck was traveling north in the outside lane while a 2020 Honda Civic traveled north in the inside lane and approached the truck. The front of the Honda collided with the rear of the box truck, and the Honda became fully engulfed in flames, FHP said. See also: Crash blocks 2 left lanes on southbound I-95 at Exit 50 in Palm Beach County The Honda’s driver, who has not been identified pending next-of-kin notification, was pronounced dead at the scene at 4:05 a.m. The 37-year-old Miami man driving the box truck was not injured. Following the deadly crash, a stretch of northbound I-95 was closed for several hours. Since then the roadway has reopened. All northbound lanes of I-95 remain closed for the investigation, with traffic diverted to Indiantown Road.

entry.title: Fort Pierce driver accused of fleeing police twice during targeted traffic enforcement - WPEC
entry.summary: Fort Pierce driver accused of fleeing police twice during targeted traffic enforcement    WPEC
entry.article_text: A driver in Fort Pierce is accused of fleeing from police officers twice during a targeted traffic enforcement initiative, according to the Fort Pierce Police Department . 25, at around 4:45 p.m., during the traffic enforcement initiative taking place in the Okeechobee Road and Jenkins Road area, officers conducted a traffic stop on a blue Volkswagen Jetta. During the stop, they identified that the driver Leon Kevin Gentle-Coaxum, 21 was driving with a suspended license. Next, as the officer approached the vehicle, the Gentle-Coaxum suddenly fled the traffic stop, according to FPPD. He then was seen driving recklessly, speeding into oncoming traffic and around stopped vehicles using the grass shoulder. After finding the vehicle stopped in traffic at South 25th Street and Edwards Road, officers attempted another traffic stop and ordered Gentle-Coaxum out of the car. Instead, he refused once again and attempted to flee a second time by ramming a vehicle in front of him. See also: Unable to paddle against strong current, pair calls for help and is rescued in river canoe In an effort to stop the car, an officer broke Gentle-Coaxum’s driver’s side window. He then exited through the passenger side and took off on foot. FPPD says a nearby citizen intervened and tackled Gentle-Coaxum, allowing officers to take him into custody. Gentle-Coaxum is charged with fleeing and alluding with property damages, hit and run with property damages, operating a vehicle without a valid license and resisting without violence.

entry.article_text: Drivers in Vero Beach will face higher parking fines beginning Oct. 1, with several penalties set to double. The Vero Beach Police Department announced the increases Sunday and urged drivers to review the updated fine schedule before it takes effect. Parking in a fire lane, blocking a fire hydrant and parking in an emergency-vehicles-only tow-away zone will each rise from $30 to $60. Fines for improper parking that obstructs traffic and other parking violations will also increase from $30 to $60. Other violations seeing increases include: Overtime parking: $20 to $40 Parking over a line: $20 to $40 Parking in a fire lane: $30 to $60 Blocking a fire hydrant: $30 to $60 Parking in an emergency-vehicles-only tow-away zone: $30 to $60 Improper parking obstructing traffic: $30 to $60 All other parking violations: $30 to $60 See also: Airport security concerns resurface after perimeter breaches in South Florida The new penalties take effect Wednesday, Oct.

entry.title: Man charged with first-degree murder in shooting death of beloved West Palm Beach minister
entry.summary: A man has been charged with first-degree murder in the shooting death of a beloved West Palm Beach minister who was killed over the weekend , police announced. Akeem Moore, 31, who led worship and played the organ at Mount Calvary Baptist Church, was fatally shot just after midnight on Sunday. WATCH: Mount Calvary Baptist Church remembering the impact minister Akeem Moore Arrest Made in Murder of West Palm Beach Minister Akeem Moore The West Palm Beach Police Department arrested Hugh Earp Milner Jr., 38, in connection with the killing. His arrest comes as Moore's congregation grieves the sudden loss of a man they remember as a devoted and inspiring leader. Arrest Made in Weekend Homicide According to West Palm Beach police, the shooting occurred in the 500 block of Ontario Place. With assistance from the Broward County Sheriff's Office, investigators identified and located Milner as the suspect. Milner now faces a charge of first-degree murder with a firearm for Moore's death. He is also charged with attempted first-degree murder with a firearm in connection with a second victim involved in the same incident. Officials confirmed Milner is currently in custody in Broward County and will be transferred to Palm Beach County to face the charges. A Church Mourns Its Music Minister At Mount Calvary Baptist Church, the organ where Moore sat every Sunday is now empty. The church released a statement remembering him as 'a sound and inspiring preacher of the gospel' whose commitment was demonstrated by his discipline in studies and devotion to his congregation.' Earl Harris, a maintenance worker at the church, said Moore's impact on the music program was undeniable. 'I thought he was a pretty good minister leader in the music part because it seemed like he upgraded the choir to sing different songs than what we had in the past,' Harris said. He noted the improvement in 'the quality of the songs they had chosen to sing on Sundays and the voices that they had.' That progress now leaves a void that Harris believes will be difficult to fill. 'I'm hoping that we can get somebody at least as qualified as Akeem, or a little higher than, you know, to upgrade the choir and move forward,' he said. Harris asked the community to 'keep praying for the church and [Akeem's] family.' Detectives are asking anyone with information about the case to contact the West Palm Beach Police Department or Palm Beach County Crime Stoppers at 1-800-458-TIPS.

entry.title: Palm Beach County traffic fixes could cost $8B as study identifies worst congestion hotspots countywide

Palm Beach County commissioners recently reviewed the Countywide Transportation Master Plan, a long-term roadmap aimed at addressing growing congestion and failing infrastructure as more people move to the county. 'We need wider roads, more lanes,' said Barry Getzof, who frequently commutes on Northlake Boulevard.
