entry.title: Rabies alert issued in Martin County after raccoon tests positive in Stuart - WPEC
entry.summary: Rabies alert issued in Martin County after raccoon tests positive in Stuart    WPEC
entry.article_text: A rabid raccoon found in Stuart prompted the Florida Department of Health in Martin County to issue a 60-day alert Wednesday. The raccoon was captured Sunday off South Kanner Highway and later tested positive for rabies , according to the department. The alert covered an area bounded by Southeast Tressler Drive to the south, Southeast Federal Highway to the east and South Kanner Highway to the west. Health officials said rabies was present among wild animals in the area and urged residents and visitors to avoid contact with raccoons, bats, foxes, skunks, otters, bobcats, coyotes and other wildlife. Rabies is a deadly viral disease most commonly transmitted through the bite or scratch of an infected animal. An animal with rabies may appear healthy and can behave unusually friendly or aggressively. People who are bitten or scratched by a wild or domestic animal should wash the wound with soap and water, seek medical attention and report the incident to the Department of Health in Martin County at 772-221-4030 . Treatment administered after an exposure can prevent the disease. Officials recommended that residents take several precautions: Keep pets and livestock current on rabies vaccinations. Keep pets leashed and under direct supervision. Avoid handling or feeding wild and stray animals. Do not leave pet food or unsecured garbage outdoors. Prevent bats and other wildlife from entering homes, schools and other occupied buildings. Contact a licensed wildlife rehabilitator rather than bringing a wild animal into a home. See also: Florida mother leaves 4 children home alone while on Carnival cruise to Bahamas: Police Anyone whose pet or livestock is bitten should immediately contact a veterinarian and Martin County Animal Control at 772-463-3211 . Residents can also call animal control to report stray animals in their neighborhoods. More information is available at FloridaHealth.gov/Rabies .

entry.title: Toddler drowns in pond near family home in Martin County - WPEC
entry.summary: Toddler drowns in pond near family home in Martin County    WPEC
entry.article_text: A 23-month-old boy died Tuesday evening after he was found in a pond on his family's property, according to the Martin County Sheriff's Office . Deputies identified the child as Pablo Mendoza-Arroyo. According to the sheriff's office, the boy was outside with family members in the yard of a home along Darling Street in Port Salerno shortly after 5 p.m. Tuesday when he went out of sight. His mother and aunt realized he was missing and started searching. They found him in a pond on the property. Sheriff John Budensiek said the father was mowing the yard while the mother and her sister played with other children. Budensiek said there had been a fence around the pond at one point, but it had broken down over time and was no longer working. "It's a pond where if you walk in two feet, it drops off. And if you don't know how to swim, you're going to be in trouble," Budensiek said. "And in this case, sadly, our two year old did not know how to swim." Family members took the child to Cleveland Clinic South Hospital. The sheriff's office said he was pronounced dead in the emergency room despite lifesaving efforts. See also: Florida mother leaves 4 children home alone while on Carnival cruise to Bahamas: Police Family members told investigators the boy was out of sight for no more than 10 minutes, according to the sheriff's office. MCSO criminal investigators interviewed everyone at the scene and are reviewing the circumstances of the child's death. Budensiek said Wednesday that the medical examiner ruled the death an accidental drowning after an autopsy. "From all indications, everything that we've got through our investigation, this is a tragic accident," Budensiek said. He said investigators found no signs that the parents were reckless or inattentive. "Parents get distracted, I know that. So no one is disparaging the parents. In this case, this was an accidental drowning," Budensiek said. Budensiek encouraged parents to get young children into swim lessons and said the YMCA offers free classes for children as young as 2. Mindy York, president and co-founder of Baby Otter Swim School, said supervision is the most important way to prevent drownings. She also recommended door alarms, locked pool gates, and CPR training for parents. She said teaching children to swim is just as important. "We want to make sure that a child knows what to do if they fall into a body of water. Teach your children how to swim. It's like here in Florida, right? It's the leading cause of death in children under the age of five. With this death, now we're at 99," York said. She said children are never too young to start swim lessons. "I'm telling you, they absorb everything. So, we start at nine months, and we. We go all the way up to adults. So they're not too young to learn anything. They understand everything you say. And with a proper technique and speaking to them, they get it," York said.

entry.title: St. Lucie County Fire District attorney gives 90-day notice amid firefighter hazing fight - WPEC
entry.summary: St. Lucie County Fire District attorney gives 90-day notice amid firefighter hazing fight    WPEC
entry.article_text: Lucie County Fire District Attorney Kim Sabol is leaving the department, submitting her 90-day notice Wednesday as the agency faces an ongoing fight with its firefighters' union over the termination of three employees accused of hazing rookies. Sabol confirmed she submitted her notice Wednesday. It was not immediately clear whether her departure is connected to the ongoing dispute. My employment agreement requires 90 days' notice because it's a 3-year contract," Sabol told CBS12. "My last work day will be 12/31/2026." Sabol has served as the district's attorney since 2017, advising the Fire Board, fire chief and administration on legal matters including labor and employment issues and collective bargaining. Her departure comes as Professional Firefighters and Paramedics of St. Lucie County Local 1377 fights the discipline of five firefighters. The union has formally demanded arbitration for three terminated firefighters and two suspended personnel, arguing there was no just cause for the discipline. See also: Beyond the dashcam: FHP begins equipping troopers with body cameras The firefighters were disciplined after an outside investigation into videos showing senior personnel using a modified bug zapper to administer electric shocks to newer firefighters in incidents in March and September 2024. Fire District officials called the conduct hazing and said it violated department policies and created a culture of intimidation between senior and junior employees. According to previous reports , Local 1377 President Ryan Sapp said the incidents amounted to consensual station horseplay, pointing to an earlier Fort Pierce Police Department investigation that found no criminal wrongdoing. There was no kind of hazing whatsoever, and I could not believe that that's what was found," Sapp told CBS12. The union has also challenged the fairness of the Fire District's investigation, which was conducted by outside attorney John "J.K." Keller IV. Sapp said union attorneys believe the investigation was not impartial and that some questions appeared to be designed to reach a predetermined conclusion. The union also raised concerns that the law firm involved in the investigation has since been retained by the district for the upcoming arbitration. Two terminated firefighters, Jordon Hutchinson and Christopher Baldwin, have separately alleged whistleblower retaliation. The district has declined further comment while the contractual proceedings are ongoing. Sapp said the union remains willing to negotiate a resolution that could avoid arbitration, but any compromise would need to include reinstatement of the terminated firefighters. entry.title: ‘Akeem should be remembered as a hero’: WPB police reveal minister drove passenger to safety after being shot
entry.summary: New details from the West Palm Beach Police Department reveal that Minister Akeem Moores final act was one of heroism, as he drove his passenger to the safety of a fire station moments after being fatally shot. WATCH: Police Call killed WPB Minister Akeem Moore a Hero Police Call Slain WPB Minister Akeem Moore a Hero At a news conference, Police Chief Tony Araujo detailed the investigation into the 31-year-olds murder, painting a picture of a selfless man whose courage never wavered. 'Akeem should be remembered as a hero,' Araujo stated. A Selfless and Courageous Final Act According to police, Moore and a passenger were in a parked car on the 500 block of Ontario Place just after midnight Sunday when they were approached by 38-year-old Hugh Earp Milner Jr. The passenger knew and recognized Hugh and immediately believed he was mistaking them for another person, Araujo said. The situation escalated quickly. Hugh pulled a handgun from his waistband and pointed it at the occupants, the chief explained. After shots were fired, Moore, though mortally wounded, focused on saving his passenger. 'Even after being shot, he acted selflessly and courageously, driving his passenger to safety at a nearby fire station,' Araujo said. Moore later died from his injuries at a local hospital. Technology's Role in a Swift Arrest Chief Araujo also revealed how technology was critical in tracking down the suspect. He said Milner, who is homeless, fled the scene in a vehicle. Flock license plate readers helped investigators track the car as it traveled south into Broward County. This real-time intelligence allowed the Broward Sheriffs Office to quickly locate and stop the car, Araujo said. Milner was taken into custody and remains in Broward County, awaiting transfer to Palm Beach County to face charges of first-degree murder and attempted first-degree murder. As the case progresses, Moore's family continues to process their loss while searching for closure. 'Whatever justice is, truth, answers understanding why this happened to such an innocent person,' said Malik Brown, Moore's cousin. Anyone with information about the case is asked to contact the West Palm Beach Police Department or Palm Beach County Crime Stoppers at 1-800-458-TIPS. entry.title: St. Lucie County Fire District attorney gives 90-day notice amid firefighter hazing fight - cw34.com
entry.summary: St. Lucie County Fire District attorney gives 90-day notice amid firefighter hazing fight    cw34.com
entry.article_text: Lucie County Fire District Attorney Kim Sabol is leaving the department, submitting her 90-day notice Wednesday as the agency faces an ongoing fight with its firefighters' union over the termination of three employees accused of hazing rookies. Sabol confirmed she submitted her notice Wednesday. It was not immediately clear whether her departure is connected to the ongoing dispute. My employment agreement requires 90 days' notice because it's a 3-year contract," Sabol told CBS12. "My last work day will be 12/31/2026." Sabol has served as the district's attorney since 2017, advising the Fire Board, fire chief and administration on legal matters including labor and employment issues and collective bargaining. Her departure comes as Professional Firefighters and Paramedics of St. Lucie County Local 1377 fights the discipline of five firefighters. The union has formally demanded arbitration for three terminated firefighters and two suspended personnel, arguing there was no just cause for the discipline. See also: Beyond the dashcam: FHP begins equipping troopers with body cameras The firefighters were disciplined after an outside investigation into videos showing senior personnel using a modified bug zapper to administer electric shocks to newer firefighters in incidents in March and September 2024. Fire District officials called the conduct hazing and said it violated department policies and created a culture of intimidation between senior and junior employees. According to previous reports , Local 1377 President Ryan Sapp said the incidents amounted to consensual station horseplay, pointing to an earlier Fort Pierce Police Department investigation that found no criminal wrongdoing. There was no kind of hazing whatsoever, and I could not believe that that's what was found," Sapp told CBS12. The union has also challenged the fairness of the Fire District's investigation, which was conducted by outside attorney John "J.K." Keller IV. Sapp said union attorneys believe the investigation was not impartial and that some questions appeared to be designed to reach a predetermined conclusion. The union also raised concerns that the law firm involved in the investigation has since been retained by the district for the upcoming arbitration. Two terminated firefighters, Jordon Hutchinson and Christopher Baldwin, have separately alleged whistleblower retaliation. Lucie County Fire District received a 90-day notice of a resignation from its legal counsel today. The District Attorney is eligible for retirement, and the notice provides for continued service during the 90-day period," St. Lucie County Fire Rescue said in a statement. "The District will not speculate regarding the circumstances surrounding the resignation or any connection to other matters. Sapp said the union remains willing to negotiate a resolution that could avoid arbitration, but any compromise would need to include reinstatement of the terminated firefighters. Sabol's 90-day notice means she is expected to remain with the district during that period unless the terms of her departure change.

entry.title: Fort Pierce city clerk testifies about meetings in former city manager Nick Mimms corruption trial - WFLX
entry.summary: Fort Pierce city clerk testifies about meetings in former city manager Nick Mimms corruption trial    WFLX
entry.article_text: Fort Pierce City Clerk Linda Cox took the stand Wednesday as the trial of former city manager Nick Mimms entered its third day. Mimms was arrested in 2024 on charges of bid tampering and official misconduct. The jury heard first from Cox, who testified about a series of city meetings shown in video evidence by the state. One meeting, held in October 2019, showed a representative with Allegany Franciscan Ministries presenting a community center concept on behalf of the Lincoln Park Young Professionals for two vacant lots along Avenue D. The Lincoln Park Young Professionals had been awarded a $500,000 grant from Allegany Franciscan Ministries for the project. Among the organization’s board members was Caleta Scott, the niece of Mimms, as well as a city employee. According to the Florida Department of Law Enforcement, Mimms had begun the process of having the Avenue D land declared as surplus, even though it had been designated for use as parking for the nearby Lincoln Theater. Prosecutors questioned Cox about whether the city board relied on Mimms for accurate information. “Does the board also expect the defendant to give them correct information?” Assistant State Attorney Brandon White said. “Do they rely on the defendant to give correct information?” Assistant State Attorney Brandon White said. Attorneys also showed footage from future meetings of the Fort Pierce Redevelopment Agency, where the board voted to declare the lots surplus and later announced that the Lincoln Park Young Professionals had won the bid. WATCH BELOW: Opening statements begin in trial of former city manager Under cross-examination, the defense argued it was no secret that Mimms’ niece was among those seeking to obtain the property. Defense attorney Donald Murrell questioned Cox about whether she had raised any concerns at the time. “You knew they were city employees,” Murrell said. “And it bothered you that they were doing this?” Murrell said. “I thought it was a little odd,” Cox said. “You didn’t raise any objections,” Murrell said. Murrell also questioned Cox about the city attorney’s presence at the meetings. “He saw the same slideshow you saw, the same PowerPoint?” Murrell said. “He didn’t raise any objections or concerns, did he?” Murrell said. “Not at the meeting,” Cox said. Not that I know of,” Cox said. The trial is expected to last at least a week.

"They — being those positions— have essentially been able to investigate themselves." Those positions include the fire chief, assistant fire chief and district attorney. The issue stems from an alleged hazing incident we reported on earlier this year. A third-party investigator concluded that videos showing firefighters using a modified bug zapper to shock probationary firefighters depicted hazing. Three veteran firefighters — Doug Boudrias, Jordan Hutchinson and Christopher Baldwin — were fired as a result."It was just us in our downtime, joking around, having fun," Hutchinson said."We're all still friends," Boudrias said. The board is now asking two outside law firms to help draft a new complaint policy. Meanwhile, firefighters are casting ballots in a no-confidence vote regarding Lee."It basically says whether or not they trust and believe in him to lead this district," Fowler said. "So that is a huge thing if you have the majority of the men and women underneath you saying they can no longer serve under you, that's a pretty impactful message." Lee acknowledged the district lacks a clear complaint process. He told Investigative Reporter Kate Hussey: "I'm glad this board is finally taking this as a serious issue," adding he "welcomes any investigation from any agency."Per Sabol's resignation, Lee said it's a "sad day." When asked whether the board has that authority, Fowler said, "I think we might actually," adding, "The chief wants them back. The union is saying they want to come back. entry.article_text: The Martin County Medical examiner has ruled the drowning death of a 23-month-old boy an accidental drowning. Stay up to date: The latest headlines and weather from WPBF 25 Martin County Sheriff John Budenseik said the child's parents called 911. "We received one of the most heart wrenching 911 calls you can get," Budenseik said. According to investigators, Pablo Mendoza-Arrojo drowned in the area of Southeast Darling Street and Southeast Taylor Drive in Port Salerno and was found unresponsive in a pond on his family’s property in Port Salerno. The toddler was outside in the yard with family members shortly after 5 p.m. when he went missing for a short time. According to investigators, the child slipped out of sight for a short time. When Pablo’s mother and aunt realized he was missing, they began a frantic search and ultimately found him in the pond. "At some point there had been a fence around the pond, but it had been trampled down or broke down over time, so it wasn't really a functional fence,' Budensiek said. The family rushed him to Cleveland Clinic South, but despite lifesaving efforts, he was pronounced dead in the emergency room. Family members told investigators that Pablo had been out of sight for no more than 10 minutes. Martin County Sheriff’s Office criminal investigators interviewed everyone at the scene. The sheriff said it does not appear that anyone was being reckless. "Parents get distracted, I know that," Budensiek said. "So, no one is disparaging the parents. In this case, this was an accidental drowning. But we have to remember where we live and take the time and the effort or spend the money. Whatever you have to do to try to drown proof your child," Budensiek said. Charlene Lyons is the President and CEO for the YMCA Treasure Coast. She said she was devastated when she heard the news, "I started at the Y as a lifeguard, so aquatic safety is paramount to me,' Lyons said She wants the public to know they can contact the Y for information about swimming lessons. "Drowning is the great equalizer — it goes across every demographic, socioeconomic status — it doesn't matter, so it's important for everyone to learn to swim," Lyons. entry.title: Toddler drowns in pond near family home in Martin County - WPEC
entry.summary: Toddler drowns in pond near family home in Martin County    WPEC
entry.article_text: A 23-month-old boy died Tuesday evening after he was found in a pond on his family's property, according to the Martin County Sheriff's Office . Deputies identified the child as Pablo Mendoza-Arroyo. According to the sheriff's office, the boy was outside with family members in the yard of a home along Darling Street in Port Salerno shortly after 5 p.m. Tuesday when he went out of sight. His mother and aunt realized he was missing and started searching. They found him in a pond on the property. Sheriff John Budensiek said the father was mowing the yard while the mother and her sister played with other children. Budensiek said there had been a fence around the pond at one point, but it had broken down over time and was no longer working. "It's a pond where if you walk in two feet, it drops off. And if you don't know how to swim, you're going to be in trouble," Budensiek said. "And in this case, sadly, our two year old did not know how to swim." Family members took the child to Cleveland Clinic South Hospital. The sheriff's office said he was pronounced dead in the emergency room despite lifesaving efforts. See also: Florida mother leaves 4 children home alone while on Carnival cruise to Bahamas: Police Family members told investigators the boy was out of sight for no more than 10 minutes, according to the sheriff's office. MCSO criminal investigators interviewed everyone at the scene and are reviewing the circumstances of the child's death. Budensiek said Wednesday that the medical examiner ruled the death an accidental drowning after an autopsy. "From all indications, everything that we've got through our investigation, this is a tragic accident," Budensiek said. He said investigators found no signs that the parents were reckless or inattentive. "Parents get distracted, I know that. So no one is disparaging the parents. In this case, this was an accidental drowning," Budensiek said. Budensiek encouraged parents to get young children into swim lessons and said the YMCA offers free classes for children as young as 2. Mindy York, president and co-founder of Baby Otter Swim School, said supervision is the most important way to prevent drownings. She also recommended door alarms, locked pool gates, and CPR training for parents. She said teaching children to swim is just as important. "We want to make sure that a child knows what to do if they fall into a body of water. Teach your children how to swim. It's like here in Florida, right? It's the leading cause of death in children under the age of five. With this death, now we're at 99," York said. She said children are never too young to start swim lessons. "I'm telling you, they absorb everything. So, we start at nine months, and we. We go all the way up to adults. So they're not too young to learn anything. They understand everything you say. And with a proper technique and speaking to them, they get it," York said.

entry.article_text: A rabid raccoon found in Stuart prompted the Florida Department of Health in Martin County to issue a 60-day alert Wednesday. The raccoon was captured Sunday off South Kanner Highway and later tested positive for rabies , according to the department. The alert covered an area bounded by Southeast Tressler Drive to the south, Southeast Federal Highway to the east and South Kanner Highway to the west. Health officials said rabies was present among wild animals in the area and urged residents and visitors to avoid contact with raccoons, bats, foxes, skunks, otters, bobcats, coyotes and other wildlife. Rabies is a deadly viral disease most commonly transmitted through the bite or scratch of an infected animal. An animal with rabies may appear healthy and can behave unusually friendly or aggressively. People who are bitten or scratched by a wild or domestic animal should wash the wound with soap and water, seek medical attention and report the incident to the Department of Health in Martin County at 772-221-4030 . Treatment administered after an exposure can prevent the disease. Officials recommended that residents take several precautions: Keep pets and livestock current on rabies vaccinations. Keep pets leashed and under direct supervision. Avoid handling or feeding wild and stray animals. Do not leave pet food or unsecured garbage outdoors. Prevent bats and other wildlife from entering homes, schools and other occupied buildings. Contact a licensed wildlife rehabilitator rather than bringing a wild animal into a home. See also: Florida mother leaves 4 children home alone while on Carnival cruise to Bahamas: Police Anyone whose pet or livestock is bitten should immediately contact a veterinarian and Martin County Animal Control at 772-463-3211 . Residents can also call animal control to report stray animals in their neighborhoods. More information is available at FloridaHealth.gov/Rabies .

entry.title: St. Lucie County Fire District attorney gives 90-day notice amid firefighter hazing fight - WPEC
entry.summary: St. Lucie County Fire District attorney gives 90-day notice amid firefighter hazing fight    WPEC
entry.article_text: Lucie County Fire District Attorney Kim Sabol is leaving the department, submitting her 90-day notice Wednesday as the agency faces an ongoing fight with its firefighters' union over the termination of three employees accused of hazing rookies. Sabol confirmed she submitted her notice Wednesday. It was not immediately clear whether her departure is connected to the ongoing dispute. My employment agreement requires 90 days' notice because it's a 3-year contract," Sabol told CBS12. "My last work day will be 12/31/2026." Sabol has served as the district's attorney since 2017, advising the Fire Board, fire chief and administration on legal matters including labor and employment issues and collective bargaining. Her departure comes as Professional Firefighters and Paramedics of St. Lucie County Local 1377 fights the discipline of five firefighters. The union has formally demanded arbitration for three terminated firefighters and two suspended personnel, arguing there was no just cause for the discipline. See also: Beyond the dashcam: FHP begins equipping troopers with body cameras The firefighters were disciplined after an outside investigation into videos showing senior personnel using a modified bug zapper to administer electric shocks to newer firefighters in incidents in March and September 2024. Fire District officials called the conduct hazing and said it violated department policies and created a culture of intimidation between senior and junior employees. According to previous reports , Local 1377 President Ryan Sapp said the incidents amounted to consensual station horseplay, pointing to an earlier Fort Pierce Police Department investigation that found no criminal wrongdoing. There was no kind of hazing whatsoever, and I could not believe that that's what was found," Sapp told CBS12. The union has also challenged the fairness of the Fire District's investigation, which was conducted by outside attorney John "J.K." Keller IV. Sapp said union attorneys believe the investigation was not impartial and that some questions appeared to be designed to reach a predetermined conclusion. The union also raised concerns that the law firm involved in the investigation has since been retained by the district for the upcoming arbitration. Two terminated firefighters, Jordon Hutchinson and Christopher Baldwin, have separately alleged whistleblower retaliation. Lucie County Fire District received a 90-day notice of a resignation from its legal counsel today. The District Attorney is eligible for retirement, and the notice provides for continued service during the 90-day period," St. Lucie County Fire Rescue said in a statement. "The District will not speculate regarding the circumstances surrounding the resignation or any connection to other matters. Sapp said the union remains willing to negotiate a resolution that could avoid arbitration, but any compromise would need to include reinstatement of the terminated firefighters. Sabol's 90-day notice means she is expected to remain with the district during that period unless the terms of her departure change.

entry.title: St. Lucie County fire district attorney resigns amid hazing fallout; chief faces no-confidence vote - WFLX
entry.summary: St. Lucie County fire district attorney resigns amid hazing fallout; chief faces no-confidence vote    WFLX
entry.article_text: Lucie County Fire District’s attorney resigned minutes after a heated special fire board meeting Wednesday, as fallout from an alleged hazing investigation continues to threaten district leadership. Attorney Kim Sabol submitted her resignation letter effective in 90 days. She is the subject of several complaints tied to the hazing investigation. Nearly a dozen people spoke at the special meeting, which was called to address what board members described as a major gap in district policy: who investigates complaints against the district’s own leaders. “Since this district’s inception, we have not had a policy on how they handle complaints against themselves,” St. Lucie County Commissioner and Fire District Board Member Jamie Fowler said. “They — being those positions— have essentially been able to investigate themselves.” Those positions include the Fire Chief, Assistant Fire Chief, and District Attorney. The issue stems from an alleged hazing incident we reported on earlier this year. A third-party investigator concluded that videos showing firefighters using a modified bug zapper to shock probationary firefighters depicted hazing. Three veteran firefighters — Doug Boudrias, Jordan Hutchinson and Christopher Baldwin — were fired as a result. “It was just us in our downtime, joking around, having fun,” Hutchinson said. “We’re all still friends,” Boudrias said. “Us and the victims, there was no ill intent.” Months before the incident came to light, in September 2025, Boudrias and Hutchinson filed a complaint against Fire Chief Jeff Lee and Sabol. That complaint was denied by the district officials who were themselves named in it. “That’s not a good process,” Fowler said. The board is now asking two outside law firms to help draft a new complaint policy. Meanwhile, firefighters are casting ballots in a no-confidence vote regarding Lee. “It basically says whether or not they trust and believe in him to lead this district,” Fowler said. “So that is a huge thing if you have the majority of the men and women underneath you saying they can no longer serve under you, that’s a pretty impactful message.” Lee acknowledged the district lacks a clear complaint process. He told Investigative Reporter Kate Hussey: “I’m glad this board is finally taking this as a serious issue,” adding he “welcomes any investigation from any agency.” Per Sabol’s resignation, Lee said it’s a “sad day.” “She’s been a tremendous attorney for the district,” Lee said of Sabol. As for the vote of no confidence, Lee said he didn’t have much to say until it’s over with “We’ll see what the men and women decide,” Lee told Hussey. “I came up on the labor side, I’ve always fought for our men and women on the line.” Tension inside district headquarters was evident throughout Wednesday’s meeting. “This system is so broken,” one attendee said. They want action,” said retired fire captain Mike Jenkins. As the union’s legal fight to reinstate the three firefighters continues, calls are growing for the fire board to bypass arbitration and bring them back to work. When asked whether the board has that authority, Fowler said, “I think we might actually,” adding, “The chief wants them back. The union is saying they want to come back. I’m going to ask the board in a week from now — what do we want to do? What’s the process?” Firefighters are still casting ballots in the no-confidence vote. There is no word yet on when results will be released. This story was reported on-air by a journalist and has been converted to this platform with the assistance of AI. entry.title: 'Ready to answer the call': Jupiter Fire Rescue officially in service, marking historic transition
entry.summary: The new Jupiter Fire Rescue Department is officially in service, taking over all fire and emergency response duties for the town as of 12 a.m. on Oct. 1. The historic transition from Palm Beach County Fire Rescue was marked by a ceremony where Fire Chief Darrel Donatto made the first official radio call, declaring the new agency 'in service and ready to answer the call.' The launch is the culmination of a months-long journey, closely followed by WPTV, from the initial swearing-in of firefighters to the traditional 'push-in' ceremony for the new fire engines. WATCH: Jupiter's new fire department officially launch at midnight. Jupiter Fire Rescue Department now in serviceA New Era of Service At a ceremony at the Jupiter fire station to mark the official start of operations, Chief Donatto addressed firefighters and the community, acknowledging the moment's significance. 'Jupiter Fire Rescue will assume official responsibility for providing fire and emergency services to this community,' Donatto said. 'We gather here to recognize those who came before us and to reflect on the responsibility that we now inherit and to reaffirm the mission and principles that will guide this department from its very first call.' 'Ready to Answer the Call' Just after midnight, the chief's voice came over the radio, making the transition official and signaling to dispatchers and surrounding agencies that the new department was operational. 'Jupiter Chief, thank you to everyone. We look forward to serving together. Jupiter Fire Rescue is in service and ready to answer the call,' Donatto announced. For residents, dialing 911 for an emergency will not change. However, calls will now be dispatched to the new municipal department, and a Jupiter Fire Rescue engine and crew will respond. The move gives the Town of Jupiter direct control over its emergency services, staffing, and equipment for the first time in decades. entry.title: Jupiter Fire Rescue Department now in service
entry.summary: The Town of Jupiter officially launched its own fire rescue department at 12:01 a.m. Thursday, marking a historic milestone for the community's emergency services. The Jupiter Fire Rescue Department (JFRD) has assumed full responsibility for fire suppression and emergency medical services throughout the town, operating from three strategically located stations. The new department represents the culmination of more than three years of intensive planning and preparation to build a municipal fire rescue operation from scratch. WATCH: WPTV speaks to Jupiter Fire Rescue Department minutes after official launch Jupiter Fire Rescue Department now in service JFRD operates from Station 10 at 500 N. U.S. Highway 1 near Burt Reynolds Park, Temporary Station 11 at Abacoa Community Park, and Station 12 at 2197 W. Indiantown Road adjacent to Cinquez Park. The department employs 94 operational personnel, maintaining a minimum of 23 firefighters on duty during each shift to ensure round-the-clock coverage. Beyond emergency response, the town has also taken over fire prevention and inspection services through JFRD's Fire Prevention Division. This includes conducting fire inspections, reviewing building plans, and implementing other fire safety measures throughout Jupiter. Just before midnight, JFRD personnel gathered simultaneously at all three stations for ceremonial flag raisings and bell ceremonies. The traditional bell ceremony honored previous emergency responders while symbolically marking the beginning of JFRD's service to the community. Fire Chief Darrel Donatto officially placed the department in service after reading the department's mission statement and core values. JFRD operates under the mission statement 'Your Life, Our Mission.' Jupiter residents calling 911 for fire or medical emergencies will now be served exclusively by Jupiter Fire Rescue Department personnel.

entry.title: Rabies alert issued in Martin County after raccoon tests positive in Stuart - cw34.com
entry.summary: Rabies alert issued in Martin County after raccoon tests positive in Stuart    cw34.com
entry.article_text: A rabid raccoon found in Stuart prompted the Florida Department of Health in Martin County to issue a 60-day alert Wednesday. The raccoon was captured Sunday off South Kanner Highway and later tested positive for rabies , according to the department. The alert covered an area bounded by Southeast Tressler Drive to the south, Southeast Federal Highway to the east and South Kanner Highway to the west. Health officials said rabies was present among wild animals in the area and urged residents and visitors to avoid contact with raccoons, bats, foxes, skunks, otters, bobcats, coyotes and other wildlife. Rabies is a deadly viral disease most commonly transmitted through the bite or scratch of an infected animal. An animal with rabies may appear healthy and can behave unusually friendly or aggressively. People who are bitten or scratched by a wild or domestic animal should wash the wound with soap and water, seek medical attention and report the incident to the Department of Health in Martin County at 772-221-4030 . Treatment administered after an exposure can prevent the disease. Officials recommended that residents take several precautions: Keep pets and livestock current on rabies vaccinations. Keep pets leashed and under direct supervision. Avoid handling or feeding wild and stray animals. Do not leave pet food or unsecured garbage outdoors. Prevent bats and other wildlife from entering homes, schools and other occupied buildings. Contact a licensed wildlife rehabilitator rather than bringing a wild animal into a home. See also: Florida mother leaves 4 children home alone while on Carnival cruise to Bahamas: Police Anyone whose pet or livestock is bitten should immediately contact a veterinarian and Martin County Animal Control at 772-463-3211 . Residents can also call animal control to report stray animals in their neighborhoods. More information is available at FloridaHealth.gov/Rabies .

entry.title: Okeechobee family says 14-year-old daughter jumped from school bus to escape bullies, later attempted suicide
entry.summary: An Okeechobee family is demanding accountability from the school district after they say their 14-year-old daughter, in a desperate attempt to escape relentless bullying, jumped from a school bus window. The family says that after the girl returned home, she attempted to take her own life and was hospitalized for two days in the ICU. This family is now sharing their daughter's harrowing story to raise awareness and push for systemic changes to how bullying is handled. Their public plea and a planned protest aim to ensure that no other child has to endure what they say their daughter has gone through. A desperate escape captured on video The family of 14-year-old Estrella Ventura Meras, a seventh-grader at the Okeechobee Achievement Academy, says her bubbly personality has faded over the last month due to what they describe as escalating bullying by other girls at her school. The situation came to a head in an incident captured in a viral social media video, which WPTV is not showing. The video shows Estrella jumping from the bus window in the school parking lot and running away. 'She just feared for her life,' said Vanessa Sanchez, a family member. 'She didn't trust the bus driver to do anything. She didn't trust going out the front or back door, so she jumped out the bus window.' 'I'm tired of this' What the video doesn't show is what happened next. The family says when Estrella arrived home, she took a handful of medication and left a note saying, 'I'm tired of this,' in a suicide attempt. Her family found her in time to get her life-saving medical help. She is now recovering in a different hospital. 'Her mental state over the past month, has been degraded,' Sanchez said. A call for accountability The Okeechobee County School District released a statement acknowledging the incident, saying in part, 'Every student deserves to feel safe, and we take reports of bullying seriously.' The district confirmed it is investigating but stated that federal law limits its ability to comment on individual students. entry.title: 'We're tired': Delray Beach residents confront consultant over cemetery failures, resold burial plots
entry.summary: Dozens of frustrated Delray Beach residents confronted a city-hired consultant at a heated community meeting Thursday night, demanding solutions for systemic failures at the Delray Beach Memorial Gardens Municipal Cemetery, including cases where burial plots were allegedly resold. The emotional meeting was a culmination of months of resident complaints and WPTV investigations into poor conditions, maintenance issues and significant record-keeping errors. The anger and frustration voiced by families underscore the deep personal impact of the cemetery's problems, which have left some unable to locate their loved ones' graves and others, like one woman who spoke to WPTV, discovering the plot she bought 18 years ago was sold to someone else. The city has now tasked an outside firm with creating a plan for immediate and long-term fixes. 'Fix what's broken right now' One by one, residents shared painful and personal stories with Stephen Kuehne of Kuehne Cemetery Consulting. I got six family members that had to be cremated because they couldnt be buried out there, resident Andre Andrews said passionately. Were tired! RELATED: Delray Beach woman searches for missing grandparents' graves Delray Beach woman searches for grandparents' graves at neglected cemetery Nicole Ivy described the anguish of many families. We have other people who cant find their loved ones out there, she said. Those are our ancestors, and we want to preserve and protect them. The community's demands were clear: a comprehensive audit of all records, competent on-site staff, a citizen oversight board, and for the city to purchase more land for expansion. Get something done, besides just saying Im gonna look into it, resident Stanley George said. You need to get these people some solutions. A resold final resting place The record-keeping failures are not abstract problems. For Sandra Owens, the issue is painfully specific. She first shared her story with WPTV's Zitlali Solache at a 'Let's Hear It' community meet-up in July. In 2006, a year after her parents were buried, Owens purchased the plot next to them. But during a visit in 2024, she found a stranger buried in her spot. 'I went to visit my parents' burial site, and lo and behold, there's some guy buried with the whole plot and everything,' Owens said. entry.title: Toddler drowns in pond near family home in Martin County - WPEC
entry.summary: Toddler drowns in pond near family home in Martin County    WPEC
entry.article_text: A 23-month-old boy died Tuesday evening after he was found in a pond on his family's property, according to the Martin County Sheriff's Office . Deputies identified the child as Pablo Mendoza-Arroyo, who is remembered by loved ones for his bright smile and joyful spirit. Investigators say Pablo was outside with family members in the yard of a home along Darling Street in Port Salerno shortly after 5 p.m. Tuesday when he went out of sight. His mother and aunt realized he was missing and began searching. They later found him in a pond on the property Sheriff John Budensiek said the father was mowing the yard while the mother and her sister played with other children. Budensiek said there had been a fence around the pond at one point, but it had broken down over time and was no longer working. "It's a pond where if you walk in two feet, it drops off. And if you don't know how to swim, you're going to be in trouble," Budensiek said. "And in this case, sadly, our two-year-old did not know how to swim." Family members took the child to Cleveland Clinic South Hospital. The sheriff's office said he was pronounced dead in the emergency room despite lifesaving efforts. See also: Florida mother leaves 4 children home alone while on Carnival cruise to Bahamas: Police Family members told investigators the boy was out of sight for no more than 10 minutes, according to the sheriff's office. MCSO criminal investigators interviewed everyone at the scene and are reviewing the circumstances of the child's death. Budensiek said Wednesday that the medical examiner ruled the death an accidental drowning after an autopsy. "From all indications, everything that we've got through our investigation, this is a tragic accident," Budensiek said. One relative, Virginia Maldonado, said she hopes people remember Pablo by his smile and keep the family in their prayers. Others told CBS12 News Pablo was deeply loved by a large extended family spanning beyond Florida. According to the sheriff, investigators found no signs that the parents were reckless or inattentive. "Parents get distracted, I know that. So no one is disparaging the parents. In this case, this was an accidental drowning," Budensiek said. Budensiek encouraged parents to get young children into swim lessons and said the YMCA offers free classes for children as young as 2. Mindy York, president and co-founder of Baby Otter Swim School, said supervision is the most important way to prevent drownings. She also recommended door alarms, locked pool gates, and CPR training for parents. She said teaching children to swim is just as important. "We want to make sure that a child knows what to do if they fall into a body of water. Teach your children how to swim. It's like here in Florida, right? It's the leading cause of death in children under the age of five. With this death, now we're at 99," York said. She said children are never too young to start swim lessons. "I'm telling you, they absorb everything. So, we start at nine months, and we. We go all the way up to adults. So they're not too young to learn anything. They understand everything you say. entry.title: ‘Akeem should be remembered as a hero’: WPB police reveal minister drove passenger to safety after being shot
entry.summary: New details from the West Palm Beach Police Department reveal that Minister Akeem Moores final act was one of heroism, as he drove his passenger to the safety of a fire station moments after being fatally shot. WATCH: Police Call killed WPB Minister Akeem Moore a Hero Police Call Slain WPB Minister Akeem Moore a Hero At a news conference , Police Chief Tony Araujo detailed the investigation into the 31-year-olds murder, painting a picture of a selfless man whose courage never wavered. 'Akeem should be remembered as a hero,' Araujo stated. A Selfless and Courageous Final Act According to police, Moore and a passenger were in a parked car on the 500 block of Ontario Place just after midnight Sunday when they were approached by 38-year-old Hugh Earp Milner Jr. The passenger knew and recognized Hugh and immediately believed he was mistaking them for another person, Araujo said. The situation escalated quickly. Hugh pulled a handgun from his waistband and pointed it at the occupants, the chief explained. After shots were fired, Moore, though mortally wounded, focused on saving his passenger. 'Even after being shot, he acted selflessly and courageously, driving his passenger to safety at a nearby fire station,' Araujo said. Moore later died from his injuries at a local hospital. Technology's Role in a Swift Arrest Araujo also revealed how technology was critical in tracking down the suspect. He said Milner, who is homeless, fled the scene in a vehicle. Flock license plate readers helped investigators track the car as it traveled south into Broward County. This real-time intelligence allowed the Broward Sheriffs Office to quickly locate and stop the car, Araujo said. Milner was taken into custody and remains in Broward County, awaiting transfer to Palm Beach County to face charges of first-degree murder and attempted first-degree murder. As the case progresses, Moore's family continues to process their loss while searching for closure. 'Whatever justice is, truth, answers understanding why this happened to such an innocent person,' said Malik Brown, Moore's cousin. Anyone with information about the case is asked to contact the West Palm Beach Police Department or Palm Beach County Crime Stoppers at 1-800-458-TIPS. entry.title: St. Lucie County Fire District attorney gives 90-day notice amid firefighter hazing fight - cw34.com
entry.summary: St. Lucie County Fire District attorney gives 90-day notice amid firefighter hazing fight    cw34.com
entry.article_text: Lucie County Fire District Attorney Kim Sabol is leaving the department, submitting her 90-day notice Wednesday as the agency faces an ongoing fight with its firefighters' union over the termination of three employees accused of hazing rookies. Sabol confirmed she submitted her notice Wednesday. It was not immediately clear whether her departure is connected to the ongoing dispute. My employment agreement requires 90 days' notice because it's a 3-year contract," Sabol told CBS12. "My last work day will be 12/31/2026." Sabol has served as the district's attorney since 2017, advising the Fire Board, fire chief and administration on legal matters including labor and employment issues and collective bargaining. Her departure comes as Professional Firefighters and Paramedics of St. Lucie County Local 1377 fights the discipline of five firefighters. The union has formally demanded arbitration for three terminated firefighters and two suspended personnel, arguing there was no just cause for the discipline. See also: Beyond the dashcam: FHP begins equipping troopers with body cameras The firefighters were disciplined after an outside investigation into videos showing senior personnel using a modified bug zapper to administer electric shocks to newer firefighters in incidents in March and September 2024. Fire District officials called the conduct hazing and said it violated department policies and created a culture of intimidation between senior and junior employees. According to previous reports , Local 1377 President Ryan Sapp said the incidents amounted to consensual station horseplay, pointing to an earlier Fort Pierce Police Department investigation that found no criminal wrongdoing. There was no kind of hazing whatsoever, and I could not believe that that's what was found," Sapp told CBS12. The union has also challenged the fairness of the Fire District's investigation, which was conducted by outside attorney John "J.K." Keller IV. Sapp said union attorneys believe the investigation was not impartial and that some questions appeared to be designed to reach a predetermined conclusion. The union also raised concerns that the law firm involved in the investigation has since been retained by the district for the upcoming arbitration. Two terminated firefighters, Jordon Hutchinson and Christopher Baldwin, have separately alleged whistleblower retaliation. Lucie County Fire District received a 90-day notice of a resignation from its legal counsel today. The District Attorney is eligible for retirement, and the notice provides for continued service during the 90-day period," St. Lucie County Fire Rescue said in a statement. "The District will not speculate regarding the circumstances surrounding the resignation or any connection to other matters. Sapp said the union remains willing to negotiate a resolution that could avoid arbitration, but any compromise would need to include reinstatement of the terminated firefighters. Sabol's 90-day notice means she is expected to remain with the district during that period unless the terms of her departure change.

entry.title: Testimony begins in trial for former Fort Pierce city manager accused of bid tampering - WPBF
entry.summary: Testimony begins in trial for former Fort Pierce city manager accused of bid tampering    WPBF
entry.article_text: Opening statements began Tuesday in the trial of former Fort Pierce City Manager Nick Mimms, who faces charges of bid tampering and official misconduct involving city-owned properties and a nonprofit linked to his niece. Prosecutors told jurors they would present emails, witness testimony, and city documents to support their case. They alleged Mimms used his position to influence the bidding process for the development of city-owned properties. Mimms carefully, skillfully steered the bid for the development of this property so that it would end up in the hands of two city employees. And one of those employees was Mr. Mimms' niece," Bridges said. Deep Dive: WPBF 25 News Investigates Mimms is accused of helping Lincoln Park Young Professionals, a nonprofit founded by his niece, secure a lease to develop two city-owned properties. The defense attorney Donald Murrell described Mimms' relationship with his niece as distant. "The state puts a lot of emphasis on the fact that she is my client's niece, and she is, but she can fairly be called a distant niece if that's at all possible," Murrell said. The defense argued that Mimms did not conspire to commit the crime. "If you follow the law, you follow the facts, and we're comfortable at the end of this case you will find that Mr. Mimms is not guilty," Murrell said. The state also called its first witness, and several city officials, including the mayor, are expected to testify. entry.title: 'Most heart-wrenching': Toddler drowns in Martin County Pond, sheriff calls it a tragic accident - WPBF
entry.summary: 'Most heart-wrenching': Toddler drowns in Martin County Pond, sheriff calls it a tragic accident    WPBF
entry.article_text: The Martin County Medical examiner has ruled the drowning death of a 23-month-old boy an accidental drowning. Stay up to date: The latest headlines and weather from WPBF 25 Martin County Sheriff John Budenseik said the child's parents called 911. "We received one of the most heart wrenching 911 calls you can get," Budenseik said. According to investigators, Pablo Mendoza-Arrojo drowned in the area of Southeast Darling Street and Southeast Taylor Drive in Port Salerno and was found unresponsive in a pond on his family’s property in Port Salerno. The toddler was outside in the yard with family members shortly after 5 p.m. when he went missing for a short time. According to investigators, the child slipped out of sight for a short time. When Pablo’s mother and aunt realized he was missing, they began a frantic search and ultimately found him in the pond. "At some point there had been a fence around the pond, but it had been trampled down or broke down over time, so it wasn't really a functional fence,' Budensiek said. The family rushed him to Cleveland Clinic South, but despite lifesaving efforts, he was pronounced dead in the emergency room. Family members told investigators that Pablo had been out of sight for no more than 10 minutes. Martin County Sheriff’s Office criminal investigators interviewed everyone at the scene. The sheriff said it does not appear that anyone was being reckless. "Parents get distracted, I know that," Budensiek said. "So, no one is disparaging the parents. In this case, this was an accidental drowning. But we have to remember where we live and take the time and the effort or spend the money. Whatever you have to do to try to drown proof your child," Budensiek said. Charlene Lyons is the President and CEO for the YMCA Treasure Coast. She said she was devastated when she heard the news, "I started at the 'Y' as a lifeguard, so aquatic safety is paramount to me,' Lyons said She wants the public to know they can contact the YMCA for information about swim lessons. "Drowning is the great equalizer — it goes across every demographic, socioeconomic status — it doesn't matter, so it's important for everyone to learn to swim," Lyons. The family has set up a GoFundMe account to assist during this difficult time. For more information about swim lessons, log on to the YMCA Treasure Coast website posted here. entry.title: As Buc-ee's nears construction, development interest builds in northern St. Lucie County - WPEC
entry.summary: As Buc-ee's nears construction, development interest builds in northern St. Lucie County    WPEC
entry.article_text: Buc-ee’s may be best known for its massive travel centers, barbecue sandwiches and loyal fan base, but on the Treasure Coast, county leaders say the proposed development could signal something even bigger: a wave of growth along the Indrio Road corridor in northern St. After years of planning and review, the proposed Buc-ee’s at Interstate 95 and Indrio Road has completed the county’s planning process, bringing the long-discussed project one step closer to reality. The proposed 76,000-square-foot travel center would feature approximately 120 fuel pumps and could become the largest Buc-ee’s location in Florida. Buc-ee’s Nearing Construction Phase According to St. Lucie County Planning and Development Services Director Benjamin Balcer, the project has cleared its local planning hurdles. "They are completely 100% finished with the planning process," Balcer said. "Our board will not see this again." Balcer said the company is now awaiting final approvals from the Florida Department of Transportation and the Florida Department of Environmental Protection before construction can begin. "As far as the county is concerned, their building permit and their site development permit is pretty much at the tail end and ready to go," Balcer said. "It's really just pulling the trigger on Buc-ee's end to start the process." Buc-ee's has previously targeted a 2028 opening date. Development Interest Growing Along Indrio Road While the travel center itself would bring jobs and tax revenue, county officials say its presence also shines a spotlight on a corridor already attracting significant development interest. For now, much of the area remains undeveloped, with cattle grazing across wide stretches of rural land. But Balcer said developers are increasingly looking at opportunities along Indrio Road. "It's kind of an untapped resource," he said. "At the moment, we're seeing a lot of development interest, whether that's pre-application meetings, developers coming in and talking about concept plans, or actual formal applications." Balcer stopped short of calling Buc-ee's the direct catalyst for that interest, but acknowledged that a major national company can influence future investment decisions. "I don't know if Buc-ee's is a catalyst that actually drives development," he said. "But whenever you have a large national commercial entity like Buc-ee's, it does move the needle whenever people see that type of investment." Why the Corridor Is Attracting Attention The area has benefited from recent road and utility improvements, making it increasingly attractive for future residential and commercial projects. County officials say they are already seeing proposals emerge throughout the area. "But all through that Indrio Road corridor, we do see more retail, mixed-use residential projects that are starting to come in and gain traction," Balcer said. Several large developments are either proposed or moving through the review process near the future Buc-ee's site. The proposed Club at Indrio Creek , located south of Indrio Road, could bring hundreds of new homes to the area. Another proposal, Indrio Town Center , would transform approximately 85 acres near Indrio Road and Emerson Avenue into a mixed-use development featuring retail, office space and residential uses. Perhaps the most controversial proposal was Indrio Groves , a development planned near Spanish Lakes Fairways that could add more than 3,000 homes to the area. The size of that proposal has raised concerns among nearby residents who worry about traffic and infrastructure demands. The discussion was tabled over the summer. Residents Voice Infrastructure Concerns But as development proposals continue to stack up, some residents worry infrastructure isn't keeping pace. "That's what people are concerned about," said Jeff Bourassa, president of the Spanish Lakes Fairways Homeowners Association. If they put another 3,000 homes, we're in trouble." Bourassa said residents are worried local roads are not equipped to handle the level of growth being proposed. They're cowpaths," Bourassa said. "There's nothing that was put in for infrastructure." County officials say they understand those concerns. "People are concerned," Balcer said. "Traffic impacts, changing their lifestyle. This is a historical agricultural kind of community." Looking Ahead Whether Buc-ee's ultimately becomes a transformational project remains to be seen. County leaders say the larger story is what comes next for the surrounding area. If Buc-ee's opens and several proposed developments move forward, the character of the Indrio Road corridor could change dramatically over the next decade. "If Buc-ee's does come online, and the projects that are in the pipeline do develop," Balcer said, "you'll see a big difference in the Indrio Road corridor."

entry.title: Toddler drowns in pond on family's property in Martin County
entry.summary: A 23-month-old boy died Tuesday evening after being found floating in a pond on his family's property, according to the Martin County Sheriff's Office. The child was playing outside in the yard along Darling Street with family members shortly after 5 p.m. when he slipped out of sight for a brief period. When the child's mother and aunt realized he was missing, they began searching for him and found him in a pond on the property. The family immediately rushed the toddler to Cleveland Clinic South, where medical staff performed lifesaving efforts. Despite their attempts, he was pronounced dead in the emergency room. Family members told investigators the child was out of their sight for no more than 10 minutes. Martin County Sheriff's Office criminal investigators interviewed everyone present at the scene and are reviewing the circumstances surrounding the tragedy. The investigation remains ongoing.

entry.summary: Martin County rejected a plan for homes, a new state law offers another route    cw34.com
entry.article_text: A new Florida law could offer another path toward housing on 396 acres near Kanner Highway, after Martin County commissioners voted against advancing a residential proposal for the land last year. The property, known as Waterside, lies south of SW 96th Street, between Kanner Highway and the St. The applicant previously sought to change its designation from agricultural to low-density residential. Commissioners voted 5 0 in November 2025 not to advance that request. Now, Kanner/96th Street Investments LLC has asked commissioners to certify the property as an agricultural enclave under a state law that took effect July 1. Florida business records list The Kolter Group as the LLC’s manager. A hearing on the certification request is scheduled for October 13. Senior Planner Jenna Knobbe said the application requests a density of about 3.1 homes per acre, or roughly 1,200 single-family homes. That is a proposed figure, not an approved home count. Jim Harvey, president of Brookfield Kolter Land Partners, declined to comment on the request. We have no comment at this time, Harvey said in an email to CBS12 News. The law is meant for certain agricultural properties that are already surrounded by development or land planned for it. To qualify, an applicant must meet specific requirements involving the property’s agricultural history, surrounding land, size and access to services such as roads, water and sewer. Whether Waterside meets those requirements is what commissioners must decide. Commissioners can deny certification if the land does not qualify. But they must base their decision on the law’s criteria not simply whether they want homes built there. A denial requires written findings, which the applicant can challenge in court. If the county takes no action within 90 days of receiving an application, state law says the land must be certified. See also: Woman accused of driving wrong way with 0.20 BAC in deadly crash gets house arrest Certification would not approve a subdivision. It would let the applicant later submit qualifying housing plans based on what is allowed on neighboring land. The law says those plans must be treated as an allowed use even if the county’s existing growth plan or zoning would otherwise prohibit it. County staff would still review the plans, but the law does not require another commission hearing on them. It does take away some of the local control for local governments for deciding where development may or may not take place, Knobbe said in an interview. She said certification is the only part of this process that would go before commissioners. If certified, the property owner could submit development plans for administrative review without another commission hearing or vote on those plans. Martin County has long tried to keep new neighborhoods from spreading into rural areas. The new law raises a question: If this land qualifies, can commissioners still stop homes from being built outside the county’s planned growth area? Greg Braun, executive director of The Guardians of Martin County, said his organization wants development to follow the county’s existing growth plan. Tallahassee legislators seem to think that they know better about what’s going on locally than our local elected officials, and we think that that’s wrong, Braun said. Gil Smart, advocacy director for Friends of the Everglades, said his organization opposed the law because of concerns about development and public involvement. People value the open space, the green space, as they see them being taken away and bulldozed flat so we can build more housing, Smart said. People are going to have something to say about that, and they need to have a say in that. Commissioners did not decide the Waterside request Tuesday. They unanimously approved fees for reviewing applications under the new law: $8,150 to review whether property qualifies and $16,600 to review development plans submitted later. Knobbe said the law puts staff on a tight schedule. The county has 30 days to review a certification application and issue a report. A public hearing must follow within another 30 days. We've kind of had to drop everything that we're working on and prioritize that application, Knobbe told commissioners Tuesday. A separate deadline would apply if the land is certified and the applicant submits development plans: County staff would have no more than 180 days to review them. These are very expedited timeframes for what we typically will do for a major development plan type of review, because there’s a lot of moving parts, Knobbe said. The property is outside the county’s urban service district, where the county generally directs more intensive development and plans for supporting services. Knobbe said the county had not necessarily planned for that level of development on these properties. Roads, drainage, water and sewer would still need review. Knobbe said the county would need to negotiate with the developer over who pays for any needed infrastructure improvements. I think the effect is going to be more traffic. I think the effect is going to be more sprawl. I think the effect is going to be municipal services overextended, Smart said. No homes were approved Tuesday. The October 13 hearing is about whether Waterside qualifies for the new process, not approval of a housing site plan.

entry.title: Rabies alert issued in Martin County after raccoon tests positive in Stuart - WPEC
entry.summary: Rabies alert issued in Martin County after raccoon tests positive in Stuart    WPEC
entry.article_text: A rabid raccoon found in Stuart prompted the Florida Department of Health in Martin County to issue a 60-day alert Wednesday. The raccoon was captured Sunday off South Kanner Highway and later tested positive for rabies , according to the department. The alert covered an area bounded by Southeast Tressler Drive to the south, Southeast Federal Highway to the east and South Kanner Highway to the west. Health officials said rabies was present among wild animals in the area and urged residents and visitors to avoid contact with raccoons, bats, foxes, skunks, otters, bobcats, coyotes and other wildlife. Rabies is a deadly viral disease most commonly transmitted through the bite or scratch of an infected animal. An animal with rabies may appear healthy and can behave unusually friendly or aggressively. People who are bitten or scratched by a wild or domestic animal should wash the wound with soap and water, seek medical attention and report the incident to the Department of Health in Martin County at 772-221-4030 . Treatment administered after an exposure can prevent the disease. Officials recommended that residents take several precautions: Keep pets and livestock current on rabies vaccinations. Keep pets leashed and under direct supervision. Avoid handling or feeding wild and stray animals. Do not leave pet food or unsecured garbage outdoors. Prevent bats and other wildlife from entering homes, schools and other occupied buildings. Contact a licensed wildlife rehabilitator rather than bringing a wild animal into a home. See also: Florida mother leaves 4 children home alone while on Carnival cruise to Bahamas: Police Anyone whose pet or livestock is bitten should immediately contact a veterinarian and Martin County Animal Control at 772-463-3211 . Residents can also call animal control to report stray animals in their neighborhoods. More information is available at FloridaHealth.gov/Rabies .

entry.summary: As Buc-ee's nears construction, development interest builds in northern St. Lucie County    cw34.com
entry.article_text: Buc-ee’s may be best known for its massive travel centers, barbecue sandwiches and loyal fan base, but on the Treasure Coast, county leaders say the proposed development could signal something even bigger: a wave of growth along the Indrio Road corridor in northern St. After years of planning and review, the proposed Buc-ee’s at Interstate 95 and Indrio Road has completed the county’s planning process, bringing the long-discussed project one step closer to reality. The proposed 76,000-square-foot travel center would feature approximately 120 fuel pumps and could become the largest Buc-ee’s location in Florida. Buc-ee’s Nearing Construction Phase According to St. Lucie County Planning and Development Services Director Benjamin Balcer, the project has cleared its local planning hurdles. "They are completely 100% finished with the planning process," Balcer said. "Our board will not see this again." Balcer said the company is now awaiting final approvals from the Florida Department of Transportation and the Florida Department of Environmental Protection before construction can begin. "As far as the county is concerned, their building permit and their site development permit is pretty much at the tail end and ready to go," Balcer said. "It's really just pulling the trigger on Buc-ee's end to start the process." Buc-ee's has previously targeted a 2028 opening date. Development Interest Growing Along Indrio Road While the travel center itself would bring jobs and tax revenue, county officials say its presence also shines a spotlight on a corridor already attracting significant development interest. For now, much of the area remains undeveloped, with cattle grazing across wide stretches of rural land. But Balcer said developers are increasingly looking at opportunities along Indrio Road. "It's kind of an untapped resource," he said. "At the moment, we're seeing a lot of development interest, whether that's pre-application meetings, developers coming in and talking about concept plans, or actual formal applications." Balcer stopped short of calling Buc-ee's the direct catalyst for that interest, but acknowledged that a major national company can influence future investment decisions. "I don't know if Buc-ee's is a catalyst that actually drives development," he said. "But whenever you have a large national commercial entity like Buc-ee's, it does move the needle whenever people see that type of investment." Why the Corridor Is Attracting Attention The area has benefited from recent road and utility improvements, making it increasingly attractive for future residential and commercial projects. County officials say they are already seeing proposals emerge throughout the area. "But all through that Indrio Road corridor, we do see more retail, mixed-use residential projects that are starting to come in and gain traction," Balcer said. Several large developments are either proposed or moving through the review process near the future Buc-ee's site. The proposed Club at Indrio Creek , located south of Indrio Road, could bring hundreds of new homes to the area. Another proposal, Indrio Town Center , would transform approximately 85 acres near Indrio Road and Emerson Avenue into a mixed-use development featuring retail, office space and residential uses. Perhaps the most controversial proposal was Indrio Groves , a development planned near Spanish Lakes Fairways that could add more than 3,000 homes to the area. The size of that proposal has raised concerns among nearby residents who worry about traffic and infrastructure demands. The discussion was tabled over the summer. Residents Voice Infrastructure Concerns But as development proposals continue to stack up, some residents worry infrastructure isn't keeping pace. "That's what people are concerned about," said Jeff Bourassa, president of the Spanish Lakes Fairways Homeowners Association. If they put another 3,000 homes, we're in trouble." Bourassa said residents are worried local roads are not equipped to handle the level of growth being proposed. They're cowpaths," Bourassa said. "There's nothing that was put in for infrastructure." County officials say they understand those concerns. "People are concerned," Balcer said. "Traffic impacts, changing their lifestyle. This is a historical agricultural kind of community." Looking Ahead Whether Buc-ee's ultimately becomes a transformational project remains to be seen. County leaders say the larger story is what comes next for the surrounding area. If Buc-ee's opens and several proposed developments move forward, the character of the Indrio Road corridor could change dramatically over the next decade. "If Buc-ee's does come online, and the projects that are in the pipeline do develop," Balcer said, "you'll see a big difference in the Indrio Road corridor."

entry.title: Port St. Lucie lowers property tax rate for 11th straight year - WPTV
entry.summary: Port St. Lucie lowers property tax rate for 11th straight year    WPTV
entry.article_text: Lucie City Council unanimously approved a reduction in the city's property tax rate for the 11th consecutive year, lowering the millage rate from 4.9750 to 4.8750 for the fiscal year beginning Oct. 1.The decision, made during the formal adoption of the city's $971.6 million budget on Monday, continues a trend of tax relief that officials said has saved the average homeowner nearly $2,000 over the past decade.WATCH BELOW: Port St. Lucie property tax rate going downSince 2016, Port St. Lucie has reduced its millage rate by 25%, giving the city the third-lowest municipal tax rate among Florida's 20 largest cities. The millage rate represents the amount of tax charged per $1,000 of taxable property value.Officials said the tax cuts come despite the city's rapid population growth. More than 60,000 new residents have moved to Port St. Lucie since 2020, requiring substantial investments in infrastructure including roads, drainage systems, utilities and public safety services."Our goal is to provide the services our residents value most while being good stewards of taxpayer dollars," said Mayor Shannon M. "By taking a measured approach to lowering property tax rates, we have been able to continue meeting the needs of our growing community while remaining fiscally responsible."The city's ability to maintain services while reducing taxes reflects what officials describe as smart financial planning designed to support the rapidly expanding community without burdening existing property owners.The fiscal year 2026-27 budget totals $971.6 million across the city's operating and capital funds, supporting services for a population that has grown substantially in recent years while maintaining the city's commitment to keeping property tax rates low.The new millage rate takes effect Thursday.
