entry.title: 'Not knowing where he is': Family searches for missing Port St. Lucie father - cbs12.com
entry.summary: 'Not knowing where he is': Family searches for missing Port St. Lucie father    cbs12.com
entry.article_text: Eight months after a Port St. Lucie father vanished, his family says they are still searching for answers and living with the painful uncertainty of not knowing where he is. "I'm stuck in this cycle of not knowing where he is," said Aubrey Finley, whose brother, Robert La Polla , disappeared Jan. 8 after being released from a hospital in Fort Pierce. The 47-year-old father has not been seen or heard from since, according to his family. Detectives have no confirmed sightings, and the case remains unsolved. Finley said La Polla struggled with depression following the deaths of their parents, but the siblings remained close and talked often. "Everything kind of fell apart," she said. "But we still managed to communicate a lot. We were still there for each other all the time." Because of that bond, Finley said her brother's disappearance is completely out of character. In the months since he vanished, family members and friends have organized search efforts across Fort Pierce, checking wooded areas and busy corridors near HCA Florida Lawnwood Hospital. "We've gone through woods, under bridges, talking to people everywhere in Fort Pierce, trying to find anything that brings us to him," Finley said. The search has also taken an emotional toll on La Polla's young daughter, who continues to wait for her father to come home. She misses him," Finley said. "He's got a family that love him." The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office (SLCSO) said La Polla has been entered into a national missing persons database. Investigators have also collected DNA from family members in case it is needed for identification and continue to follow up on leads. Anyone with information about La Polla's whereabouts is asked to contact Detective Cpl. Drawdy at 772-462-3230 or call 911.

entry.title: Returning Stuart city manager Michael Mortell vows to improve city structure, restore public trust
entry.summary: Stuart's returning city manager says he has unfinished business and a plan to bring more structure to City Hall. Michael Mortell is back in his role as Stuart city manager. In his first interview since officially returning to the role Friday, Mortell told me he still has more to give the city. WATCH BELOW: Returning Stuart city manager vows to restore public trust Returning Stuart city manager Michael Mortell vows to improve city structure 'There's something drawing me. I feel the need to go back and finish the unwritten book or the unwritten chapter,' Mortell said. 'I felt like there was things that were left that needed to be corrected and needed to be finished.' After his dismissal last October, Mortell worked for the 19th Judicial Circuit, where he says he learned practices that could help the city run more efficiently. 'We need to really focus on defining administration defining whatwho are the policymakers, who the administrators, who is the chain of command, and how we need to disseminate information,' Mortell said. 'Implementing more structure and defining it will help all of us make the city a better place and I think residents will know exactly what to expect.' Over the past year, a divided Stuart Commission and leadership turnover have left some residents questioning their confidence in city government. Resident David Kelman voiced those concerns at a previous city commission meeting. 'You all represent this city. You need to step back and unite because what you're doing ain't going to work. It's three versus two here,' Kelman said. I asked Mortell how he plans to restore the community's faith in the city. He says it starts with teamwork. 'We really identify everybody's strengths ... and find ways to work more as a team so that everybody feels like they're contributing to the outcome and that everybody has the common goal of what's best for Stuart in mind and rather than being divisive at all to try to find ways to work together,' Mortell said. A city manager with a long history working for the city, Mortell is returning to the job with a fresh approach. entry.title: 'Who put it up?' Unpermitted license plate readers found in St. Lucie County
entry.summary: WPTV learned there are 13 license plate reader cameras in St. Lucie County that don't have permits, according to county staff. Wednesday, Sept. 30, was the deadline the Florida Department of Transportation gave municipalities to remove the license plate readers from state-controlled roads. WATCH BELOW: Unpermitted license plate readers found in St. Lucie County Unpermitted license plate readers found in St. Lucie County Now WPTV is pressing city leaders about why the cameras are there, who they belong to, and what is happening to the cameras now. On Thursday, WPTV spoke to Ricky Mathura, who works at a gas station off Orange Avenue and 25 th Street in Fort Pierce, where one of the unpermitted license plate readers was found. 'I don't know why it's there,' said Mathura. 'Who put it up?' St. Lucie County Communications Director Erick Gill said they're trying to find that out. 'We don't know who they belong to,' Gill said. 'They were just put in our right-of-way.' The county says there's 53 permitted license plate readers on their right-of-ways and gave WPTV a list with all the locations of the unpermitted license plate readers staff found. RELATED: FDOT revokes permits for automated license plate readers FDOT revokes permits for automated license plate readers 'We were surprised, you know, that were that many out there, said Gill. The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office told WPTV they claimed three of them but are working to find out why they weren't permitted. Gill said county staff is actively working to identify the owners of the other readers and taped notices on the cameras for the owners to take them down within 30 days. Once the 30 days are up, Gill said staff will remove the readers safely. 'We'll begin the process of either removing them if we feel like we can safely remove them without damaging the equipment and endangering our staff, or at least covering up so the cameras can't capture any surveillance,' Gill said.

entry.title: Two men arrested in separate Port St. Lucie hit-and-run cases - cbs12.com
entry.summary: Two men arrested in separate Port St. Lucie hit-and-run cases    cbs12.com
entry.article_text: Two men are out of jail on bond after being arrested in two separate hit-and-run cases in Port St. Lucie this week, according to the Port St. According to an arrest affidavit, 23-year-old Giovanny Barthelemy was driving a silver Toyota Highlander around 8:40 p.m. Tuesday when it collided with a 16-year-old riding an electric motorcycle on Southwest Roma Way near Southwest Lorenzo Way. A security camera at the community clubhouse recorded the crash. The officer wrote that the video shows the SUV turning into the community entrance as the teen crossed in front of it. The teen was thrown from the motorcycle. The affidavit says the SUV then backed up and drove away while the injured teen lay on the ground waving his arms. The teen was taken to Tradition Medical Center and then flown to HCA Florida Lawnwood Hospital. Police said he broke his left femur and hurt his left ankle, and he was listed in serious but stable condition. See also: Rapper Rick Ross arrested in Florida on domestic violence charges, enters not guilty plea One witness told police the electric motorcycle had no headlights. Two witnesses said both vehicles were going fast. The SUV's owner, the father of Barthelemy's girlfriend, called 911. He told police Barthelemy said he had hit someone on a bike and then driven home. Officers found Barthelemy at his home on Southwest Ridgecrest Drive. According to the affidavit, after being read his rights, Barthelemy told police he felt and heard the crash and knew right away he had hit a person. He told police he should have stopped but didn't, and said his phone was dead, according to the affidavit. Barthelemy is charged with leaving the scene of a crash involving injuries, which is a felony. He was also given a traffic citation. He was released on a $7,500 bond. The second case happened earlier that afternoon. Lucie officer clocked a silver Toyota going 85 mph in a 40-mph zone, according to an arrest affidavit. The officer turned around and tried to stop the car. The affidavit says the driver went over a concrete median into the opposite lanes, ran a red light, and hit a traffic sign at Southwest Becker Road and Southwest Hallmark Street before getting on northbound Interstate 95. The officer turned off his lights and siren but kept the car in sight. Police said the car later broke down on the side of I-95. Officers said the driver, 19-year-old Christian Johnson, got out and ran toward the back of the car. Lucie detective, a Florida Highway Patrol trooper, and the officer surrounded the car, and Johnson was taken into custody. According to the affidavit, Johnson's license had been suspended three times in St. Johnson is charged with leaving the scene of a crash involving property damage, reckless driving and driving with a suspended or revoked license. All three charges are misdemeanors. He was released on a $12,500 bond. In a statement about both arrests, the Port St. Lucie Police Department said drivers are legally required to stop, whether it's for a traffic stop or after a crash. "Fleeing from law enforcement or leaving the scene of a crash can have serious consequences," the department said.

entry.title: As Buc-ee's nears construction, development interest builds in northern St. Lucie County - cbs12.com
entry.summary: As Buc-ee's nears construction, development interest builds in northern St. Lucie County    cbs12.com
entry.article_text: Buc-ee’s may be best known for its massive travel centers, barbecue sandwiches and loyal fan base, but on the Treasure Coast, county leaders say the proposed development could signal something even bigger: a wave of growth along the Indrio Road corridor in northern St. After years of planning and review, the proposed Buc-ee’s at Interstate 95 and Indrio Road has completed the county’s planning process, bringing the long-discussed project one step closer to reality. The proposed 76,000-square-foot travel center would feature approximately 120 fuel pumps and could become the largest Buc-ee’s location in Florida. Buc-ee’s Nearing Construction Phase According to St. Lucie County Planning and Development Services Director Benjamin Balcer, the project has cleared its local planning hurdles. "They are completely 100% finished with the planning process," Balcer said. "Our board will not see this again." Balcer said the company is now awaiting final approvals from the Florida Department of Transportation and the Florida Department of Environmental Protection before construction can begin. "As far as the county is concerned, their building permit and their site development permit is pretty much at the tail end and ready to go," Balcer said. "It's really just pulling the trigger on Buc-ee's end to start the process." Buc-ee's has previously targeted a 2028 opening date. Development Interest Growing Along Indrio Road While the travel center itself would bring jobs and tax revenue, county officials say its presence also shines a spotlight on a corridor already attracting significant development interest. For now, much of the area remains undeveloped, with cattle grazing across wide stretches of rural land. But Balcer said developers are increasingly looking at opportunities along Indrio Road. "It's kind of an untapped resource," he said. "At the moment, we're seeing a lot of development interest, whether that's pre-application meetings, developers coming in and talking about concept plans, or actual formal applications." Balcer stopped short of calling Buc-ee's the direct catalyst for that interest, but acknowledged that a major national company can influence future investment decisions. "I don't know if Buc-ee's is a catalyst that actually drives development," he said. "But whenever you have a large national commercial entity like Buc-ee's, it does move the needle whenever people see that type of investment." Why the Corridor Is Attracting Attention The area has benefited from recent road and utility improvements, making it increasingly attractive for future residential and commercial projects. County officials say they are already seeing proposals emerge throughout the area. "But all through that Indrio Road corridor, we do see more retail, mixed-use residential projects that are starting to come in and gain traction," Balcer said. Several large developments are either proposed or moving through the review process near the future Buc-ee's site. The proposed Club at Indrio Creek , located south of Indrio Road, could bring hundreds of new homes to the area. Another proposal, Indrio Town Center , would transform approximately 85 acres near Indrio Road and Emerson Avenue into a mixed-use development featuring retail, office space and residential uses. Perhaps the most controversial proposal was Indrio Groves , a development planned near Spanish Lakes Fairways that could add more than 3,000 homes to the area. The size of that proposal has raised concerns among nearby residents who worry about traffic and infrastructure demands. The discussion was tabled over the summer. Residents Voice Infrastructure Concerns But as development proposals continue to stack up, some residents worry infrastructure isn't keeping pace. "That's what people are concerned about," said Jeff Bourassa, president of the Spanish Lakes Fairways Homeowners Association. If they put another 3,000 homes, we're in trouble." Bourassa said residents are worried local roads are not equipped to handle the level of growth being proposed. They're cowpaths," Bourassa said. "There's nothing that was put in for infrastructure." County officials say they understand those concerns. "People are concerned," Balcer said. "Traffic impacts, changing their lifestyle. This is a historical agricultural kind of community." Looking Ahead Whether Buc-ee's ultimately becomes a transformational project remains to be seen. County leaders say the larger story is what comes next for the surrounding area. entry.title: Rabies alert issued in Martin County after raccoon tests positive in Stuart - cbs12.com
entry.summary: Rabies alert issued in Martin County after raccoon tests positive in Stuart    cbs12.com
entry.article_text: A rabid raccoon found in Stuart prompted the Florida Department of Health in Martin County to issue a 60-day alert Wednesday. The raccoon was captured Sunday off South Kanner Highway and later tested positive for rabies , according to the department. The alert covered an area bounded by Southeast Tressler Drive to the south, Southeast Federal Highway to the east and South Kanner Highway to the west. Health officials said rabies was present among wild animals in the area and urged residents and visitors to avoid contact with raccoons, bats, foxes, skunks, otters, bobcats, coyotes and other wildlife. Rabies is a deadly viral disease most commonly transmitted through the bite or scratch of an infected animal. An animal with rabies may appear healthy and can behave unusually friendly or aggressively. People who are bitten or scratched by a wild or domestic animal should wash the wound with soap and water, seek medical attention and report the incident to the Department of Health in Martin County at 772-221-4030 . Treatment administered after an exposure can prevent the disease. Officials recommended that residents take several precautions: Keep pets and livestock current on rabies vaccinations. Keep pets leashed and under direct supervision. Avoid handling or feeding wild and stray animals. Do not leave pet food or unsecured garbage outdoors. Prevent bats and other wildlife from entering homes, schools and other occupied buildings. Contact a licensed wildlife rehabilitator rather than bringing a wild animal into a home. See also: Florida mother leaves 4 children home alone while on Carnival cruise to Bahamas: Police Anyone whose pet or livestock is bitten should immediately contact a veterinarian and Martin County Animal Control at 772-463-3211 . Residents can also call animal control to report stray animals in their neighborhoods. More information is available at FloridaHealth.gov/Rabies .

She is the subject of several complaints stemming from allegations that she and Fire Chief Jeff Lee improperly handled internal investigations.WATCH BELOW: St. Lucie County fire district attorney resigns amid hazing falloutNearly a dozen people spoke at the special meeting, which was called to address what board members described as a major gap in district policy: who investigates complaints against the district's own leaders."Since this district's inception, we have not had a policy on how they handle complaints against themselves," St. Lucie County Commissioner and Fire District Board Member Jamie Fowler said. "They — being those positions— have essentially been able to investigate themselves." Those contract positions include the Fire Chief, District Attorney, Clerk Treasurer and Medical Director.The issue stems from an alleged hazing incident we reported on earlier this year. A third-party investigator concluded that videos showing firefighters using a modified bug zapper to shock probationary firefighters depicted hazing. Three veteran firefighters — Doug Boudrias, Jordan Hutchinson and Christopher Baldwin — were fired as a result."It was just us in our downtime, joking around, having fun," Hutchinson said."We're all still friends," Boudrias said. "Us and the victims, there was no ill intent." Months before the incident came to light, Baldwin and Hutchinson filed a complaint against Fire Chief Jeff Lee and Sabol in September 2025. District officials ultimately denied it. Baldwin and Hutchinson then filed additional complaints, including an amended complaint to investigators alleging the hazing investigation — and their subsequent termination — were part of a broader pattern of retaliation."That's not a good process," Fowler said. The board is now asking two outside law firms to help draft a new complaint policy. Meanwhile, firefighters are casting ballots in a no-confidence vote regarding Lee."It basically says whether or not they trust and believe in him to lead this district," Fowler said. "So that is a huge thing if you have the majority of the men and women underneath you saying they can no longer serve under you, that's a pretty impactful message." Lee acknowledged the district lacks a clear complaint process. He told Investigative Reporter Kate Hussey: "I'm glad this board is finally taking this as a serious issue," adding he "welcomes any investigation from any agency."Per Sabol's resignation, Lee said it's a "sad day." "She's been a tremendous attorney for the district," Lee said of Sabol. As for the vote of no confidence, Lee said he didn't have much to say until it's over with "We'll see what the men and women decide," Lee told Hussey. "I came up on the labor side; I've always fought for our men and women on the line." Tension inside district headquarters was evident throughout Wednesday's meeting."This system is so broken," one attendee said."Everybody is fed up. They want action," said retired fire captain Mike Jenkins.As the union's legal fight to reinstate the three firefighters continues, calls are growing for the fire board to bypass arbitration and bring them back to work. When asked whether the board has that authority, Fowler said, "I think we might actually," adding, "The chief wants them back. The union is saying they want to come back. I'm going to ask the board in a week from now — what do we want to do? What's the process?" Firefighters are still casting ballots in the no-confidence vote. entry.title: Dolphins rule out rookie WR Caleb Douglas for second straight week with ankle injury
entry.summary: The Miami Dolphins will be without rookie receiver Caleb Douglas for a second straight game as he continues nursing an ankle injury suffered in Week 2. Dolphins coach Jeff Hafley said Friday that Douglas and defensive end Robert Beal Jr. (hamstring) will miss Sunday's game at Minnesota, but Miami will have veteran center Aaron Brewer, who appeared on Thursday's injury report with a hand issue. 'He's in every meeting, and hes got to stay locked in, and hes got to watch practice, watch the practice tape, and stay on top of it,' Hafley said of Douglas missing what could be valuable reps early in the season, 'because what we dont want to have happen is when he gets back and hopefully thats soon that he takes a step back mentally. Hes doing a good job, hes a mature guy. Douglas, who has seven receptions for 117 yards in two games, has not practiced the past two weeks after suffering the injury in the second half of a loss at San Francisco. He was one of the standouts in the preseason and was expected to emerge as one of the top targets for quarterback Malik Willis. With Douglas sidelined, fellow rookie Chris Bell, who has still been ramping up from a knee injury suffered last year, had four receptions for 64 yards in last week's loss to Kansas City . Receiver Malik Washington had five catches for 56 yards, and tight end Greg Dulcich added five catches for 55 yards. Hafley said he wants to see improvement in the timing and rhythm with Willis' connection with his young receiving corps. For this team, right now where were at with the youth, with guys playing together, its Can I trust the guy next to me to do his job precisely and be where hes supposed to be every single play over and over again,'' Hafley said. 'And weve seen glimpses of that. And then weve seen where were just a little bit off here and a little bit off here.' Running back Jaylen Wright is expected to return after missing last week with a stinger and foot injury. The Dolphins will lean on the third-year running back a lot more going forward after losing Pro Bowler De'Von Achane to a season-ending ACL tear . Wright and third-stringer Ollie Gordon will see increased roles, and the Dolphins will elevate one of their practice squad running backs, either Carlos Washington Jr. or Jarquez Hunter, for Sunday's game. Also Friday, Hafley said second-year defensive tackle Kenneth Grant could return to practice next week after beginning the season on injured reserve because of a lower-body injury.

Joshua Gibbs was sentenced to 37 1/2 years in Florida state prison, followed by 10 years of probation, according to the Stuart Police Department. The sentence stems from the Jan. 25, 2025, shooting at Miller’s Vapory, 1596 SE Federal Highway. Police said Gibbs, then 19, entered the business wearing a ski mask and carrying a handgun before firing at a store clerk. The clerk fired back, and no one was injured. Detectives identified Gibbs as the suspect following an extensive investigation, police said. Authorities arrested him in Douglasville, Georgia, with help from the U.S. Marshals Fugitive Task Force. See also: Ag Reserve meeting draws overflow crowd, tense atmosphere in Delray Beach Police previously said Gibbs had confronted the clerk in December 2024 after he was denied service because he was underage. Gibbs was initially accused of attempted robbery with a firearm, aggravated assault with a firearm and robbery without a firearm in connection with the earlier theft.

entry.title: FDLE testimony focuses on RFP process in ex-Fort Pierce manager Nick Mimms' trial - cbs12.com
entry.summary: FDLE testimony focuses on RFP process in ex-Fort Pierce manager Nick Mimms' trial    cbs12.com
entry.article_text: Former Fort Pierce City Manager Nick Mimms is on trial over allegations that he improperly influenced a city bidding process involving two vacant lots in Fort Pierce's Lincoln Park area. Mimms faces charges of bid tampering and official misconduct. He has pleaded not guilty. Prosecutors allege he steered the process toward Lincoln Park Young Professionals, a nonprofit whose board included Mimms' niece and another city employee. On Thursday, much of the testimony focused on who controlled the RFP process and how closely Mimms remained involved after it was turned over to the city's purchasing department. FDLE Agent Derek Brisky testified about emails and other records collected during the investigation. One focus was the nearby Lincoln Theater and its need for parking. Brisky testified Mimms had told the Fort Pierce Redevelopment Agency that the RFP would include language addressing the theater's parking needs. But that language was not included in the request Mimms sent to the purchasing department. Brisky also testified investigators found no evidence Mimms filed a 2019 memorandum concerning the parking plans in the relevant city records. The defense questioned the significance of that omission and emphasized that the purchasing department was responsible for putting together and publishing the RFP after receiving the project's specifications. See also: NTSB report clarifies Amazon plane crash timeline that killed 5 on Sept. 6 Defense attorneys also challenged the state's characterization of the process as a sole-source arrangement. Brisky acknowledged the RFP was not technically a sole-source contract. The state, meanwhile, pointed to emails showing Mimms continued to communicate with city employees about the RFP, including its evaluation criteria and the evaluation committee. Other emails showed city employees knew there had been one submission after the RFP was posted. An LPYP email address was copied on one of those communications. The defense also questioned the investigation's treatment of other city employees involved in the process, including a purchasing official who was not charged. Later, former Fort Pierce employee Kalita Scott testified about LPYP and its efforts to develop the Lincoln Park properties. She described the organization as a group of young professionals focused on community development and said the need for parking near the Lincoln Theater was known in the community. Prosecutors allege Mimms manipulated the city's process to ensure LPYP received the lease. The defense has argued Mimms did not improperly favor the organization and that the evidence does not establish a criminal conspiracy. The trial is continuing in St.

entry.title: As Buc-ee's nears construction, development interest builds in northern St. Lucie County - WPEC
entry.summary: As Buc-ee's nears construction, development interest builds in northern St. Lucie County    WPEC
entry.article_text: Buc-ee’s may be best known for its massive travel centers, barbecue sandwiches and loyal fan base, but on the Treasure Coast, county leaders say the proposed development could signal something even bigger: a wave of growth along the Indrio Road corridor in northern St. After years of planning and review, the proposed Buc-ee’s at Interstate 95 and Indrio Road has completed the county’s planning process, bringing the long-discussed project one step closer to reality. The proposed 76,000-square-foot travel center would feature approximately 120 fuel pumps and could become the largest Buc-ee’s location in Florida. Buc-ee’s Nearing Construction Phase According to St. Lucie County Planning and Development Services Director Benjamin Balcer, the project has cleared its local planning hurdles. "They are completely 100% finished with the planning process," Balcer said. "Our board will not see this again." Balcer said the company is now awaiting final approvals from the Florida Department of Transportation and the Florida Department of Environmental Protection before construction can begin. "As far as the county is concerned, their building permit and their site development permit is pretty much at the tail end and ready to go," Balcer said. "It's really just pulling the trigger on Buc-ee's end to start the process." Buc-ee's has previously targeted a 2028 opening date. Development Interest Growing Along Indrio Road While the travel center itself would bring jobs and tax revenue, county officials say its presence also shines a spotlight on a corridor already attracting significant development interest. For now, much of the area remains undeveloped, with cattle grazing across wide stretches of rural land. But Balcer said developers are increasingly looking at opportunities along Indrio Road. "It's kind of an untapped resource," he said. "At the moment, we're seeing a lot of development interest, whether that's pre-application meetings, developers coming in and talking about concept plans, or actual formal applications." Balcer stopped short of calling Buc-ee's the direct catalyst for that interest, but acknowledged that a major national company can influence future investment decisions. "I don't know if Buc-ee's is a catalyst that actually drives development," he said. "But whenever you have a large national commercial entity like Buc-ee's, it does move the needle whenever people see that type of investment." Why the Corridor Is Attracting Attention The area has benefited from recent road and utility improvements, making it increasingly attractive for future residential and commercial projects. County officials say they are already seeing proposals emerge throughout the area. "But all through that Indrio Road corridor, we do see more retail, mixed-use residential projects that are starting to come in and gain traction," Balcer said. Several large developments are either proposed or moving through the review process near the future Buc-ee's site. The proposed Club at Indrio Creek , located south of Indrio Road, could bring hundreds of new homes to the area. Another proposal, Indrio Town Center , would transform approximately 85 acres near Indrio Road and Emerson Avenue into a mixed-use development featuring retail, office space and residential uses. Perhaps the most controversial proposal was Indrio Groves , a development planned near Spanish Lakes Fairways that could add more than 3,000 homes to the area. The size of that proposal has raised concerns among nearby residents who worry about traffic and infrastructure demands. The discussion was tabled over the summer. Residents Voice Infrastructure Concerns But as development proposals continue to stack up, some residents worry infrastructure isn't keeping pace. "That's what people are concerned about," said Jeff Bourassa, president of the Spanish Lakes Fairways Homeowners Association. If they put another 3,000 homes, we're in trouble." Bourassa said residents are worried local roads are not equipped to handle the level of growth being proposed. They're cowpaths," Bourassa said. "There's nothing that was put in for infrastructure." County officials say they understand those concerns. "People are concerned," Balcer said. "Traffic impacts, changing their lifestyle. This is a historical agricultural kind of community." Looking Ahead Whether Buc-ee's ultimately becomes a transformational project remains to be seen. County leaders say the larger story is what comes next for the surrounding area. If Buc-ee's opens and several proposed developments move forward, the character of the Indrio Road corridor could change dramatically over the next decade. "If Buc-ee's does come online, and the projects that are in the pipeline do develop," Balcer said, "you'll see a big difference in the Indrio Road corridor."

entry.title: 'Not knowing where he is': Family searches for missing Port St. Lucie father - WPEC
entry.summary: 'Not knowing where he is': Family searches for missing Port St. Lucie father    WPEC
entry.article_text: Eight months after a Port St. Lucie father vanished, his family says they are still searching for answers and living with the painful uncertainty of not knowing where he is. "I'm stuck in this cycle of not knowing where he is," said Aubrey Finley, whose brother, Robert La Polla , disappeared Jan. 8 after being released from a hospital in Fort Pierce. The 47-year-old father has not been seen or heard from since, according to his family. Detectives have no confirmed sightings, and the case remains unsolved. Finley said La Polla struggled with depression following the deaths of their parents, but the siblings remained close and talked often. "Everything kind of fell apart," she said. "But we still managed to communicate a lot. We were still there for each other all the time." Also read: Search underway for missing autistic man last seen at Jensen Beach home Thursday morning Because of that bond, Finley said her brother's disappearance is completely out of character. In the months since he vanished, family members and friends have organized search efforts across Fort Pierce, checking wooded areas and busy corridors near HCA Florida Lawnwood Hospital. "We've gone through woods, under bridges, talking to people everywhere in Fort Pierce, trying to find anything that brings us to him," Finley said. The search has also taken an emotional toll on La Polla's young daughter, who continues to wait for her father to come home. She misses him," Finley said. "He's got a family that love him." The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office (SLCSO) said La Polla has been entered into a national missing persons database. Investigators have also collected DNA from family members in case it is needed for identification and continue to follow up on leads. Anyone with information about La Polla's whereabouts is asked to contact Detective Cpl. Drawdy at 772-462-3230 or call 911.

entry.title: Case reopened: Port St. Lucie TikTok creator jailed on computer-access charge - cw34.com
entry.summary: Case reopened: Port St. Lucie TikTok creator jailed on computer-access charge    cw34.com
entry.article_text: Lucie man whose TikTok and Twich bios identify him as a cybersecurity engineer was jailed Wednesday after police reopened an investigation that had been closed in May. Mark Stephen Asea, 36, was booked into the St. Lucie County Jail on Sept. on one pending count of offense against computer users, according to jail records. His bond was set at $35,000. An earlier stalking charge appears to have been dropped. The charge stems from an earlier investigation in which detectives accused Asea of gaining access to women’s electronic devices and using TikTok posts to discuss information they said was private. In a warrant affidavit, a detective described reviewing videos from an account linked to Asea. The profile’s bio identifies its user as a narcissistic abuse survivor, former satanist, empath, cybersecurity engineer and woodsman. Police said one video included references to a woman’s password, device information, banking activity, license plate number and possible location tracking. The woman told investigators the password had been shared only in a closed TikTok group chat and that she had not given Asea permission to share it. Another woman told police Asea previously had remote access to her computer to help with an application. She became concerned, investigators said, after an image from a private Telegram message appeared in one of his TikTok posts. See also: Florida Education Department eyes dress code to ban head coverings, Crocs, short skirts The earlier affidavit alleged Asea posted more than 100 TikTok videos mentioning one of the women, including as many as six in a day. Detectives also cited videos that appeared to show computer equipment and coding as they investigated whether he had accessed devices without authorization. Asea’s booking photo shows him with long dark hair and prominent geometric tattoos across his face.

entry.summary: Altercation at tow yard leads to shooting, Martin County Sheriff's Office says    WPBF
entry.article_text: The Martin County Sheriff’s Office is actively investigating after a shooting Friday afternoon at Gary's Towing and Recovery near Stuart. At 1 p.m., deputies responded to Southeast Cove Road at 4405 SE Cove Road. A woman from Miami arrived at the tow yard to claim a vehicle that had been towed there earlier in the day. Then, people in another vehicle arrived at the facility, and the two parties became involved in an altercation, according to the sheriff's office. https://www.facebook.com/MartinCountySheriffsOffice/posts/pfbid0enPBfuxCWxva9Ce6vmU7hGP3nKdhfidsLzp1e7zxkZ58uSYxB3KhHPTdVi9kagZnl The Miami woman then retrieved a firearm and fired multiple shots at the other individuals before getting into a vehicle and fleeing the area, the agency said. Because the tow yard is about a half-mile from Murray Middle School, the sheriff’s office activated an active-shooter response and placed the school on lockout as deputies responded to the scene. Road Patrol deputies, aviation, detectives and other available units began searching for the suspect vehicle. Deputies located the vehicle traveling on Cove Road near U.S. 1 and attempted a traffic stop. The driver fled, and deputies subsequently performed a PIT maneuver, bringing the vehicle to a stop, MCSO said. Additional units moved in and successfully immobilized the vehicle before the driver could flee again. The individuals targeted by the gunfire had left the area before deputies arrived. At this time, it is unclear whether any of them were struck by gunfire, the agency said. The woman was taken into custody and taken to the Sheriff’s Office, where detectives are currently questioning her. entry.title: Port St. Lucie man sentenced to 37 1/2 years in Stuart vape shop shooting - WPEC
entry.summary: Port St. Lucie man sentenced to 37 1/2 years in Stuart vape shop shooting    WPEC
entry.article_text: Lucie man convicted in connection with a shooting inside a Stuart vape shop has been sentenced to decades in prison, police said Friday. Joshua Gibbs was sentenced to 37 1/2 years in Florida state prison, followed by 10 years of probation, according to the Stuart Police Department. The sentence stems from the Jan. 25, 2025, shooting at Miller’s Vapory, 1596 SE Federal Highway. Police said Gibbs, then 19, entered the business wearing a ski mask and carrying a handgun before firing at a store clerk. The clerk fired back, and no one was injured. Detectives identified Gibbs as the suspect following an extensive investigation, police said. Authorities arrested him in Douglasville, Georgia, with help from the U.S. Marshals Fugitive Task Force. See also: Ag Reserve meeting draws overflow crowd, tense atmosphere in Delray Beach Police previously said Gibbs had confronted the clerk in December 2024 after he was denied service because he was underage. Investigators said he threatened the clerk and stole more than $300 in vape products. Gibbs was initially accused of attempted robbery with a firearm, aggravated assault with a firearm and robbery without a firearm in connection with the earlier theft.

entry.article_text: The Boys Girls Clubs of America has named a St. Lucie County teen the 2026-27 National Youth of the Year, the organization's highest honor for a club member. Stay up to date: The latest headlines and weather from WPBF 25 Enrique Rosario Liz received the award during a national ceremony in New York City on Thursday night after representing Florida and the Southeast Region in the competition. According to the Boys Girls Clubs of St. Lucie County, Enrique first won local and state Youth of the Year titles before advancing to the national level. Enrique moved to the United States from the Dominican Republic when he was 8 years old. Club leaders said he later created a Spanish class for younger members, graduated as valedictorian from Port St. Lucie High School and is now studying elementary education at the University of Florida. Youth of the Year recognizes Boys Girls Club members for leadership, service, academic success and commitment to their communities. A welcome-home celebration for Enrique is planned for 7 p.m. Friday at the President Donald J. Trump International Airport. Get the latest news updates with the WPBF 25 News app.

entry.title: Miami woman in custody after shooting at tow yard near Murray Middle School in Martin County
entry.summary: A shooting at a tow yard Friday afternoon near a middle school in Martin County triggered a lockout and led to a chase and a Miami woman in custody. The woman opened fire at a tow yard on Southeast Cove Road shortly after 1 p.m., the Martin County Sheriff's Office said. According to deputies, the woman arrived at the towing facility to claim a car that had been towed there earlier in the day. Shortly after, individuals in another car arrived at the facility, and the two parties became involved in an altercation, deputies said. The woman got a gun and fired multiple shots at the other individuals before getting into a car and leaving the area. Since the tow yard is located near Murray Middle School, the sheriff's office said it immediately activated an active-shooter response and placed the school on lockout as deputies responded to the scene. Road patrol deputies, aviation, detectives and other available units quickly began searching for the woman's car, deputies said, and located the car traveling on Cove Road near U.S. 1 Deputies said they attempted a traffic stop but the driver fled, forcing deputies to perform a PIT maneuver, bringing the car to a stop. The individuals who were shot at left the area before deputies arrived, the sheriff's office said. It is unclear whether any of them were struck by gunfire. The woman was taken into custody and transported to the sheriff's office, where detectives are currently questioning her. Deputies said additional information will be provided as it becomes available.

entry.title: Rabies alert issued in Indian River County after rabid bat found near apartment complex
entry.summary: The Florida Department of Health in Indian River County has issued a 60-day rabies alert after a bat captured near the Sonrise Apartments tested positive for the virus. Health officials said the bat was captured in the Sonrise Apartments area off Sonrise Place in Fellsmere on Sept. 24. Anyone who may have had contact with or touched the bat is urged to contact the Department of Health in Indian River County at 772-794-7472. WATCH BELOW: Rabid bat prompts alert in Indian River County Rabid bat prompts alert in Indian River County The alert comes as health officials monitor rabies activity among wild animals in the area and warn residents that the disease is present in the local wildlife population. Rabies is a viral disease that affects the nervous system of mammals, including humans. Health officials say people who are exposed to rabies can protect themselves by seeking prompt medical treatment after exposure. The Department of Health is reminding residents and visitors to avoid contact with wild animals such as raccoons, bats, foxes, skunks, otters, bobcats and coyotes, which are more likely to carry the disease. Officials also recommend taking several precautions to reduce the risk of exposure, including: Keeping pets vaccinated against rabies Supervising pets and keeping them on a leash Securing livestock on private property Avoiding contact with wild or stray animals, including cats Not feeding or handling wildlife Preventing bats and other wildlife from entering homes, schools and other occupied buildings Anyone bitten or scratched by a wild or domestic animal should seek medical attention and report the incident to the Department of Health in Indian River County at 772-794-7472. If a pet or livestock animal is bitten by another animal, owners should contact a veterinarian immediately and notify Indian River County Animal Control at 772-226-4799. Visit the Florida Department of Health website for more information on rabies.

entry.article_text: Lucie man was arrested after police said a 16-year-old relative accused him of sexually assaulting her multiple times inside their shared home. Jean Emile Revange faces three felony counts of sexual battery on a person between the ages of 12 and 17 without physical force likely to cause serious injury, according to a Port St. Lucie Police Department arrest affidavit. The investigation began Sept. 26 after police were notified about allegations involving a teen receiving treatment at Lawnwood Regional Medical Center . According to the affidavit, the teen’s family had taken her to a hospital after she complained of severe abdominal and pelvic pain. During treatment, she disclosed that Revange, who is her father’s cousin, had sexually assaulted her, investigators said. Police said Revange, his wife, the teen and several other relatives lived together in the same Port St. During an interview at the hospital and a subsequent forensic interview at the Children’s Advocacy Center , the teen repeatedly identified Revange as the person who assaulted her, according to the affidavit. Investigators said the teen had cognitive and developmental limitations that affected how she communicated. Police ended their initial detailed questioning so a specially trained forensic interviewer could speak with her. The teen described multiple alleged assaults in different parts of the home. She could not provide exact dates but believed at least one occurred Sept. 23, according to the affidavit. Police said he admitted during the call to having sexual intercourse with her but claimed he could not remember when it began or when it most recently occurred. After Revange was taken into custody, however, he denied the allegations during an interview conducted in Creole, the affidavit said. entry.article_text: A woman is in custody after deputies say an altercation at a Martin County towing facility escalated into gunfire, triggering a law enforcement response, a school lockout and a pursuit Friday afternoon. According to the Martin County Sheriff's Office , the shooting happened shortly after 1 p.m. at a towing facility on Southeast Cove Road. Investigators said a woman from Miami arrived at the tow yard to retrieve a vehicle that had been towed there earlier in the day. Shortly afterward, people in another vehicle arrived at the facility and became involved in an altercation with the woman, according to MCSO. The sheriff's office said the woman retrieved a firearm and fired multiple shots at the other individuals before getting into a vehicle and fleeing the area. Because the tow yard is about a half-mile from Murray Middle School , the sheriff's office activated an active-shooter response and placed the school on lockout while deputies responded. See also: Woman arrested at Mar-a-Lago after claiming Sen. Tom Cotton invited her Road patrol deputies, aviation units, detectives and other available units began searching for the suspect vehicle. Deputies located the vehicle traveling on Cove Road near U.S. 1 and attempted a traffic stop, according to MCSO. The sheriff's office said the driver fled, prompting deputies to perform a PIT maneuver to stop the vehicle. Additional units moved in and immobilized the vehicle before the driver could flee again, according to MCSO. The woman was taken into custody and transported to the Martin County Sheriff's Office, where detectives were questioning her. The people who were allegedly targeted by the gunfire left the towing facility before deputies arrived. As of the sheriff's office's latest update, investigators did not know whether anyone had been struck by gunfire. Murray Middle School sent out the following message to families: "Good afternoon, Lions! Please note that we have heavy police presence in the area for an incident unrelated to Murray. We are following Martin County Sheriffs Office guidance and are on a lock out. We will remain in close contact with them and provide additional information as it becomes available. Thank you, Principal Roth" The sheriff's office has not released the woman's identity or announced any charges. The investigation remains active.

entry.title: As Buc-ee's nears construction, development interest builds in northern St. Lucie County - cw34.com
entry.summary: As Buc-ee's nears construction, development interest builds in northern St. Lucie County    cw34.com
entry.article_text: Buc-ee’s may be best known for its massive travel centers, barbecue sandwiches and loyal fan base, but on the Treasure Coast, county leaders say the proposed development could signal something even bigger: a wave of growth along the Indrio Road corridor in northern St. After years of planning and review, the proposed Buc-ee’s at Interstate 95 and Indrio Road has completed the county’s planning process, bringing the long-discussed project one step closer to reality. The proposed 76,000-square-foot travel center would feature approximately 120 fuel pumps and could become the largest Buc-ee’s location in Florida. Buc-ee’s Nearing Construction Phase According to St. Lucie County Planning and Development Services Director Benjamin Balcer, the project has cleared its local planning hurdles. "They are completely 100% finished with the planning process," Balcer said. "Our board will not see this again." Balcer said the company is now awaiting final approvals from the Florida Department of Transportation and the Florida Department of Environmental Protection before construction can begin. "As far as the county is concerned, their building permit and their site development permit is pretty much at the tail end and ready to go," Balcer said. "It's really just pulling the trigger on Buc-ee's end to start the process." Buc-ee's has previously targeted a 2028 opening date. Development Interest Growing Along Indrio Road While the travel center itself would bring jobs and tax revenue, county officials say its presence also shines a spotlight on a corridor already attracting significant development interest. For now, much of the area remains undeveloped, with cattle grazing across wide stretches of rural land. But Balcer said developers are increasingly looking at opportunities along Indrio Road. "It's kind of an untapped resource," he said. "At the moment, we're seeing a lot of development interest, whether that's pre-application meetings, developers coming in and talking about concept plans, or actual formal applications." Balcer stopped short of calling Buc-ee's the direct catalyst for that interest, but acknowledged that a major national company can influence future investment decisions. "I don't know if Buc-ee's is a catalyst that actually drives development," he said. "But whenever you have a large national commercial entity like Buc-ee's, it does move the needle whenever people see that type of investment." Why the Corridor Is Attracting Attention The area has benefited from recent road and utility improvements, making it increasingly attractive for future residential and commercial projects. County officials say they are already seeing proposals emerge throughout the area. "But all through that Indrio Road corridor, we do see more retail, mixed-use residential projects that are starting to come in and gain traction," Balcer said. Several large developments are either proposed or moving through the review process near the future Buc-ee's site. The proposed Club at Indrio Creek , located south of Indrio Road, could bring hundreds of new homes to the area. Another proposal, Indrio Town Center , would transform approximately 85 acres near Indrio Road and Emerson Avenue into a mixed-use development featuring retail, office space and residential uses. Perhaps the most controversial proposal was Indrio Groves , a development planned near Spanish Lakes Fairways that could add more than 3,000 homes to the area. The size of that proposal has raised concerns among nearby residents who worry about traffic and infrastructure demands. The discussion was tabled over the summer. Residents Voice Infrastructure Concerns But as development proposals continue to stack up, some residents worry infrastructure isn't keeping pace. "That's what people are concerned about," said Jeff Bourassa, president of the Spanish Lakes Fairways Homeowners Association. If they put another 3,000 homes, we're in trouble." Bourassa said residents are worried local roads are not equipped to handle the level of growth being proposed. They're cowpaths," Bourassa said. "There's nothing that was put in for infrastructure." County officials say they understand those concerns. "People are concerned," Balcer said. "Traffic impacts, changing their lifestyle. This is a historical agricultural kind of community." Looking Ahead Whether Buc-ee's ultimately becomes a transformational project remains to be seen. County leaders say the larger story is what comes next for the surrounding area. If Buc-ee's opens and several proposed developments move forward, the character of the Indrio Road corridor could change dramatically over the next decade. "If Buc-ee's does come online, and the projects that are in the pipeline do develop," Balcer said, "you'll see a big difference in the Indrio Road corridor."

entry.summary: A Port St. Lucie teenager has earned the highest honor awarded by the Boys Girls Clubs of America. Enrique Rosario Liz has been named the organizations 2026-27 National Youth of the Year, a recognition that celebrates outstanding leadership, academic achievement and service to others. The honor marks the latest milestone in a remarkable year for Rosario Liz. In April, he was named Florida Youth of the Year. Two months later, he earned the title of Southeast Youth of the Year, advancing to the national level of competition. In July, Rosario Liz received another surprise when the Boys Girls Clubs of America selected him to attend the FIFA World Cup final as a flag bearer. WPTV reporter Tyler Hatfield helped deliver the exciting news during a special presentation. Now, Rosario Liz is being recognized on the national stage as a standout young leader who exemplifies dedication in the classroom, strong personal values and a commitment to serving his community. The National Youth of the Year program honors exceptional teens from Boys Girls Clubs across the country who inspire others through their leadership, character and achievements. Rosario Liz's journey from local club member to national honoree highlights the impact of mentorship, perseverance and community involvement.

entry.title: Overflow crowd, heated debate mark Palm Beach County Ag Reserve development meeting
entry.summary: Hundreds of residents packed the South County Civic Center on Friday, while many more were turned away, as concerns over development in Palm Beach County's Agricultural Reserve sparked a heated public meeting that at times became contentious. The meeting, hosted by Palm Beach County Commissioner Maria Sachs, focused on approved projects planned for the area, including a DMV office, a nursing home and an Islamic center. Residents raised concerns about traffic, development impacts and whether enough public notice was given before the projects moved forward. entry.article_text: Hundreds of residents packed the South County Civic Center on Friday, while many more were turned away, as concerns over development in Palm Beach County's Agricultural Reserve sparked a heated public meeting that at times became contentious.The meeting, hosted by Palm Beach County Commissioner Maria Sachs, focused on approved projects planned for the area, including a DMV office, a nursing home and an Islamic center. Residents raised concerns about traffic, development impacts and whether enough public notice was given before the projects moved forward.WATCH BELOW: Overflow crowd, heated debate mark Ag Reserve development meetingBefore the meeting even began, tensions were already running high.More than 1,000 people RSVP'd for the event, despite the venue having space for only about 300 attendees. As crowds gathered outside, many said they were frustrated they could not get inside.Faith Kohn, who traveled from Parkland, said she RSVP'd but never received a response."We all want to be part of this meeting, and they won't let us in," said Kohn. Others outside voiced frustration as they waited outside."We have all these elderly people sweltering in the heat; we're not getting any information, we the people have no respect, they won't let us in to talk or even see the proceedings," said a man standing near the locked front doors as security guarded the entrance.When WPTV reporter Joel Lopez made it inside, there were still chairs available. We learned county officials shut the doors promptly at 9:30 a.m. so the meeting could begin, with Sachs noting she only had until 11 a.m. to get through the discussion.Earlier in the week, WPTV reporter Zitlali Solache reported the meeting had already reached its capacity for RSVPs on Wednesday, and encouraged residents who couldn't secure a seat to watch the meeting online via livestream.Inside the meeting, Sachs found herself fielding concerns from residents who say they want the Agricultural Reserve to remain focused on farming and preservation rather than additional development.When Sachs asked how many people wanted more farming and less housing and school development in the Ag Reserve, the crowd responded overwhelmingly.The discussion quickly turned to concerns over traffic, growth and public notification requirements.Pamela Higer-Polani, an attorney who lives in the Ag Reserve and helped organize residents to attend the meeting.She told WPTV residents have always been vocal about defending the ag reserve, and the fact that many weren't present during the approval process should have been a red flag. "If they did not receive notice, how would they have known that there was supposed to be a commissioner vote or anything of that?" said Pamela Higer-Polani.Higer-Polani said she believes residents living within 1,000 feet of the proposed projects should have been notified, rather than only those within 500 feet."I'm not here how to tell people how to have their religion, how to practice it, that is not my purpose. My purpose is I am extremely concerned that we have had our due process rights violated," said Higer-Polani.At one point during the meeting, Higer-Polani was asked to sit down and was escorted back to her seat by PBSO security after repeatedly attempting to continue her remarks while Sachs worked to restore order.It was one of several moments during the meeting where audience members shouted, stood up and chanted, nearly causing the event to end early as Sachs struggled to regain control.Following the meeting, Sachs told WPTV that residents have every right to express concerns and hold elected officials accountable."People need to be able to voice their opinion on who their neighbors are or aren't, and whether their elected representative listens to them; they can vote them out of office," said Sachs.She also noted she has consistently voted against every development project in the Agricultural Reserve but is only one of seven commissioners.Sachs encouraged residents to contact all county commissioners about their concerns. She explained that the projects residents were protesting were approved through an administrative review process that has existed for years and allows certain government entities and houses of worship to move forward without direct approval from county commissioners."I think for the most part people had their voices heard, but what they said is they want to have a voice in what comes to development in this county. I respect that I hear them," Sachs said.She is now working on a proposal that would require future development applications to come before elected county commissioners for approval."Do you think there's anything that can be done for the developments that have already been approved in the area?" asked Lopez."That's up to the lawyers," said Sachs, adding that she supports looking into it, and that legal action would likely be required to revisit previous approvals.Another major point of contention centered on an Islamic center planned for the Agricultural Reserve.The project was approved in 2022 and was repeatedly discussed during Friday's meeting, calling for stricter background checks and more information about applicants seeking approval for places of worship.Outside the venue, some attendees held signs agaisnt the site and during the meeting, Sachs directed questions regarding the applicant and project funding to attorney Brian Seymour of the Gunster law firm.In response to growing concerns and rhetoric surrounding the project, the Boca Raton Interfaith Clergy Association released the following statement urging respect and tolerance:"As faith leaders in Boca Raton, we believe we live our best lives in a pluralistic, respectful democracy where faith communities live side by side in peace. For decades we have worked together in partnership and mutual respect to build a vibrant, diverse religious community. We write today to urge everyone to seek the peace and welfare of our city and to protect what we have built together.We know some in our community are concerned about plans for expansion, including a new house of worship, in the Agricultural Reserve. Questions about how that area will be developed are before the Palm Beach County Commission and we trust our commissioners to act in the community's best interests.Over the past week we have seen painful and at times hateful remarks about various faith traditions in online conversations about this issue. We condemn unreservedly any expressions of hatred, bigotry, and the vitriol we have seen. We cannot tolerate this level of intolerance.We always encourage residents to bring their concerns to elected officials. We ask that they do so with respect and gratitude for the blessing of a diverse religious community.We stand together in defending every faith community's right to gather and to build houses of worship and community centers. This is a fundamental freedom of our American democracy, and it is essential to living out our commitments to our faiths."-Boca Raton Interfaith Clergy AssociationSachs told WPTV she plans to hold a second public meeting to further discuss the issues raised Friday.A date and location have not been finalized, but Sachs indicated a much larger venue will likely be needed given the turnout.This story was reported on-air by a journalist and has been converted to this platform with the assistance of AI. Our editorial team verifies all reporting on all platforms for fairness and accuracy.

entry.title: 21-year-old Okeechobee woman killed in car crash involving tractor-trailer on State Road 710
entry.summary: The Florida Highway Patrol is investigating a car crash involving a tractor-trailer that killed a 21-year-old Okeechobee woman Thursday afternoon. The deadly accident happened at around 1 p.m. at the T-intersection of State Road 710 and Southeast 86th Boulevard. FHP said the woman was at a stop sign at Southeast 86th Boulevard turning left onto State Road 710, when her car was struck by a man driving a tractor-trailer. The woman failed to yield the right of way, traveling into the tractor-trailers lane of travel, causing the tractor-trailer to collide with the drivers side of the womans car. The woman was taken to HCA Florida Lawnwood Hospital where she died from her injuries. The man was not injured. FHP said the investigation is ongoing.

entry.title: 'I'm forced to live in this filth': Jensen Beach residents frustrated by recurring septic backups after storms
entry.summary: WPTV is looking into drainage and septic issues on the Treasure Coast. Neighbor Daniel Fletchall reached out to our news team about septic issues in his community on Northwest Sunset Boulevard in Jensen Beach. WATCH BELOW: 'I'm forced to live in this filth': Neighbors demand septic solution Neighbors deal with septic back-ups following heavy rainfall Fletchall said after a heavy rain, he and his neighbors' septic backs up and comes up into their yards 'The sewage water from the septic tank will actually make its way up out of the tank and into my yard,' said Fletchall. 'It smells back here, and I can't let my dog out.' Fletchall said they can't even flush their toilets for days. 'I got to go down to Home Depot or go to the mall to use the bathroom,' said Fletchall. Fletchall added he can't shower or wash his clothes. 'Thankfully, my parents live nearby, so I can go take a shower,' said Fletchall. 'But it's just not happening here. Fletchall isn't the only one affected by this issue. Neighbors like Christie Berger are also having septic issues every time there's heavy rain. 'I go to McDonald's to use the bathroom if I have to,' Berger said. Neighbor Rachelle Kukan said it's becoming unacceptable. 'I wish I could just kind of pick up and move because this is such a problem and it's so serious to me that I would leave if I could,' said Kukan. Fletchall said he had septic companies come out to fix the drainage in his yard. Elevating the septic tank, Fletchall said, would be costly, and even then he's been told it might not solve the problem. Fletchall said he'd like the Martin County staff to extend the sewer lines into his neighborhood. 'I'm forced to live in this filth, and I still pay the taxes every year to have things done around the county, but Im not getting any help here,' said Fletchall. WPTV reached out to Martin County about any solutions. Staff said the neighborhood on Northwest Sunset Boulevard is on the list to get septic-to-sewer conversions, but no date has been set yet. Staff said they're looking at ways to potentially move the neighborhood up on the list of systems to convert.

entry.title: Rising dating costs push Gen Z, millennials toward cheaper date nights
entry.summary: The price of dating is going up, and younger adults are looking for less expensive ways to enjoy a date night, according to new data. Payment app Zelle did some research and found 84% of Gen Z and Millennial daters say rising costs have led them to date less, choose less expensive activities or just stop dating. WATCH BELOW: Gen Z, Millennials seek cheaper date nights, study says Higher Prices Impacts Date Night for Gen Z and Millennials Over half also say they value being thoughtful, honest and transparent with money and prefer planning a budget-friendly date. A few adults in their 20s told me a night with a TV movie and ordering food is usually preferred. Not anything extravagant,' said Nia Pierre. 'I like something that's casual or activity-filled, but it usually starts off like a coffee date or something.' And when it comes to paying for the date, 52% say they don't want to make the situation awkward. 'I would say usually the guy pays, but yeah, it's like a 50-50 thing when deciding if its the guy or girl,' Pierre said.

entry.title: Indiantown flooding remains a problem despite millions spent on drainage - WPEC
entry.summary: Indiantown flooding remains a problem despite millions spent on drainage    WPEC
entry.article_text: Flooding continues to be a problem across Indiantown, leaving some residents questioning why the issue persists despite years of efforts to improve drainage. Large areas of the village saw flooding this week including Booker Park despite spending more than $2 million on drainage improvements in the area in recent years. Residents have seen some improvements over the years but believe more need to be done. I’ve been here almost 60 years and it hasn’t gotten right, Brown said. It is better than it was at some point, but in 60 years you would think it would be far greater than what it is now. The latest round of flooding has affected other parts of Indiantown as well. Oak River saw significant flooding this week, while floodwater also surrounded Indian River Middle School. For residents whose homes take on water, the problem can quickly become a financial burden. Flood insurance can help cover some flood-related damage, but it can also come with a significant cost. For homeowners without a flood policy, recovery can become more difficult. Brian Christensen, president of Coast to Coast Adjuster, said homeowners facing a flood claim without coverage may have to look for other ways to pay for repairs. See also: GALLERY: Ag Reserve meeting draws overflow crowd, tense atmosphere in Delray Beach If you don’t have a flood policy and it is a flood claim and your homeowners policy won’t cut it, I start looking for a loan, Christensen said. Start looking for something a second mortgage, friends, family, churches anything that can assist you. Indiantown Councilman Anthony Dowling said the village is working with Martin County on the flooding problem. The village is also considering a municipal bond that could help address broken pipes and other infrastructure issues. Dowling said the village is repairing pipes that are already damaged and clearing debris from drainage systems. He acknowledged that addressing the flooding problem will not happen overnight and urged residents to take precautions when floodwater is present. I would encourage no kids to play in the water, Dowling said. Village officials say they are continuing to look for ways to address flooding throughout Indiantown. But after years of flooding and millions of dollars spent on drainage improvements residents say they want to know when they will finally see a significant difference.

entry.title: Miami woman in custody after shooting at tow yard near Murray Middle School in Martin County - WFLX
entry.summary: Miami woman in custody after shooting at tow yard near Murray Middle School in Martin County    WFLX
entry.article_text: A shooting at a tow yard Friday afternoon near a middle school in Martin County triggered a lockout and led to a chase and a Miami woman in custody. The woman opened fire at a tow yard on Southeast Cove Road shortly after 1 p.m., the Martin County Sheriff’s Office said. According to deputies, the woman arrived at the towing facility to claim a car that had been towed there earlier in the day. Shortly after, individuals in another car arrived at the facility, and the two parties became involved in an altercation, deputies said. The woman got a gun and fired multiple shots at the other individuals before getting into a car and leaving the area. Since the tow yard is located near Murray Middle School, the sheriff’s office said it immediately activated an active-shooter response and placed the school on lockout as deputies responded to the scene. Road patrol deputies, aviation, detectives and other available units quickly began searching for the woman’s car, deputies said, and located the car traveling on Cove Road near U.S. 1 Deputies said they attempted a traffic stop but the driver fled, forcing deputies to perform a PIT maneuver, bringing the car to a stop. The individuals who were shot at left the area before deputies arrived, the sheriff’s office said. It is unclear whether any of them were struck by gunfire. The woman was taken into custody and transported to the sheriff’s office, where detectives are currently questioning her. Deputies said additional information will be provided as it becomes available.

entry.title: Woman in custody after Martin County tow yard shooting leads to pursuit, PIT maneuver - WPEC
entry.summary: Woman in custody after Martin County tow yard shooting leads to pursuit, PIT maneuver    WPEC
entry.article_text: A second woman has been arrested following a chaotic chain of events that began with a shooting at a Martin County tow yard, triggered a nearby school lockout and ended with multiple crashes and a police pursuit. According to the Martin County Sheriff's Office , the incident unfolded shortly after 1 p.m. Friday at Gary's Towing and Recovery on Southeast Cove Road. Investigators said 23-year-old Jade Ely Rondon, of Miami, arrived at the tow yard to retrieve a BMW that had been towed earlier in the day. Deputies said another group arrived shortly afterward, leading to an altercation. According to the sheriff's office, Rondon retrieved a firearm and fired multiple shots at the other individuals before fleeing the scene in a vehicle. Because the business is located about a half-mile from Murray Middle School, deputies activated an active-shooter response and placed the school on lockout while officers searched for the suspect. Deputies later located Rondon's vehicle near U.S. 1 and attempted a traffic stop. Investigators said she refused to stop, prompting deputies to perform a PIT maneuver and take her into custody. Rondon was arrested and charged with two counts of aggravated assault with firearm, discharging a firearm in public, aggravated fleeing and eluding, driving while license suspended, and felony criminal mischief. See also: Woman arrested at Mar-a-Lago after claiming Sen. Tom Cotton invited her According to the sheriff's office, Valerie Valdes, 24, had accompanied Rondon to the tow yard to retrieve the BMW. After the shooting, deputies said Valdes fled in the vehicle they originally arrived in and drove recklessly while attempting to leave the area. Investigators said Valdes ultimately crashed at the intersection of Constitutional Boulevard and U.S. She was taken to Cleveland Clinic Martin South Hospital for treatment of her injuries before being arrested. Valdes is charged with operating an unregistered motor vehicle, and four counts of reckless driving with injuries. The people who were allegedly targeted by the gunfire left the towing facility before deputies arrived. CBS12 News spoke with Gary Reed, owner of Gary's Towing and Recovery, who said he's grateful no one was hurt during the incident. Murray Middle School sent out the following message to families: "Good afternoon, Lions! Please note that we have heavy police presence in the area for an incident unrelated to Murray. We are following Martin County Sheriff's Office guidance and are on a lock out. We will remain in close contact with them and provide additional information as it becomes available. Thank you, Principal Roth" The Martin County Sheriff's Office said the investigation remains active and additional charges are possible.

entry.title: Martin County border collie hoarding case moves forward as 30 rescued dogs find new homes
entry.summary: A criminal case involving 36 rescued border collies in Martin County is moving forward. Paige O'Donnell faces 72 criminal charges two for each dog rescued from her home. She was not present at her docket sounding Thursday afternoon in the Martin County courthouse, but I spoke with her attorney, Russell Ferraro. WATCH BELOW: Rescued dogs find new homes in animal hoarding case Dogs rescued in suspected animal cruelty case find new homes 'At this point I can't really say anything on her behalf for or against her,' Ferraro said. 'We just got the discovery in the case yesterday. We're organizing it, going through it, and we'll take it from there.' It has been just under two months since Martin County deputies took 36 dogs out of O'Donnell's feces-filled home on Aug. 10. The county condemned it days after the Border Collies were rescued. Ferraro said O'Donnell is staying elsewhere while the house is under repair. O'Donnell faces an animal cruelty and improper confinement charge for each dog and has pleaded not guilty. 'Everybody's got a right to a fair trial and to due process,' Ferraro said. The next hearing in O'Donnell's case is scheduled for Dec. 1. While the outcome of the case remains uncertain, most of O'Donnell's former dogs have found loving homes. According to the Humane Society of the Treasure Coast, 30 of the dogs have been adopted, five have gone or are about to go to animal rescues, and one remains up for adoption. Alan Cale in Port St. Lucie and Colleen Tilley near Deltona each adopted one of the rescued border collies. Both say their new family members now named Nadia and Leila have had little trouble adjusting to their new lives. 'She's just has an endless amount of energy and just wants to expend it at all times,' Cale said. Cale said Nadia, named after a character from the show 'New Girl,' goes to work with him every day and usually warms up to new people after they offer her a treat. 'She's just has an endless amount of energy and just wants to expend it at all times,' Cale said. 'When I saw where they came from, I expected a lot more of a challenge,' he added. 'She's curious. She wants to be out there and interacting with the world.' 'There's no off switch; it's all go, go, go,' Tilley said, as Leila raced back and forth behind her in her backyard during a Zoom interview. entry.title: Florida Election 2026: Voter Registration, Vote-by-Mail and Early Voting deadlines you need to know
entry.summary: Floridians who want to cast a ballot in the 2026 General Election have until Monday, Oct. 5, to register to vote or update their voter registration information. Voters are encouraged to verify that their registration details, including their name, address and party affiliation, are accurate before the deadline. Voters are also urged to confirm their Election Day polling location. Voter registration deadline is Oct. 5 for November election Election Day is scheduled for Tuesday, Nov. 3, with polls open from 7 a.m. to 7 p.m. Residents can register to vote or update their registration online through Florida's voter registration website , by mail or in person using a Florida Voter Registration Application. Applications are also available at Supervisor of Elections Offices and other designated voter registration agencies. Key election deadlines Voter registration deadline: Monday, Oct. 5, 2026 Vote-by-mail request deadline: Thursday, Oct. 22, 2026, by 5 p.m. Early voting dates, locations Palm Beach County: Oct. 19-Nov. 1 from 7 a.m. to 7 p.m. Voters can cast their ballot at any of the 28 locations during this time. Vote-by-mail return deadline is Nov. 3, 2026, by 7 p.m. at the Main Office or by 5 p.m. at a Branch Office or Secure Ballot Intake Station Martin County: Oct. 21-31 from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. each day at six locations across the county. St. Lucie County: Oct. 1931 from 10 a.m. to 6 p.m. daily, including Sunday, Oct. 25. The county will have eight early-voting locations across the county. Indian River County: Oct. 19-31 from 8 a.m. to 4 p.m. with extended hours on Thursdays from 8 a.m. to 6 p.m. Four early-voting locations will be available throughout the county. Vote-by-mail ballots must be received by the Supervisor of Elections office by 7 p.m. Election Day to be counted and may be returned to a secure ballot intake station located at each early voting location during early voting hours, or in person to the Supervisor of Elections office. Okeechobee County: Oct. 24-31 from 8:30 a.m. to 6 p.m. at one location: 307 NW 5th Avenue in Okeechobee Election Day: Tuesday, Nov. 3, 2026, from 7 a.m. to 7 p.m. Voters must cast their ballot at their assigned precinct.
