entry.title: Altercation at tow yard leads to shooting, Martin County Sheriff's Office says - WPBF
entry.summary: Altercation at tow yard leads to shooting, Martin County Sheriff's Office says    WPBF
entry.article_text: Two women are in custody in Martin County after a shooting at a tow yard led to a police chase and a violent crash Friday afternoon. “I have more questions than I have answers,” Martin County Sheriff John Budensiek said. Budensiek said the incident began around 1 p.m. when two women arrived at Gary’s Towing and Recovery, 4405 SE Cove Road, near Stuart, to retrieve a car that had been towed earlier that morning. While they were there, two other individuals showed up to claim the same vehicle. “They got into some type of argument about the belongings in the car, which, by the way, the only thing in the car really was a couple of guns,” Budensiek said. The sheriff said one of the original women then grabbed a gun and began shooting. No one was injured, but bullets struck trailers in the yard. “It’s just crazy how it went down,” said Gary Reed, the owner of Gary’s Towing and Recovery. Reed, who was not present during the shooting, said his employee called him, screaming for help. And I’m running as fast as I can,” Reed said. https://www.facebook.com/MartinCountySheriffsOffice/posts/pfbid0enPBfuxCWxva9Ce6vmU7hGP3nKdhfidsLzp1e7zxkZ58uSYxB3KhHPTdVi9kagZnl By the time deputies and Reed arrived at the scene, all four individuals involved had fled. The sheriff said the accused shooter had taken the car they were disputing, but deputies located her shortly later on Cove Road near U.S. She attempted to flee but was quickly arrested. Investigators identified her as Jade Rondon, 23, from Miami. The other woman she was with has been identified as Valerie Valdes, 22, also from Miami. Budensiek said she was taken into custody after causing a violent collision on U.S. “Why she was driving at a high rate of speed, why she was weaving out of traffic, we’re not sure. We didn’t even know for sure that that car was involved at that time,” Budensiek said. The sheriff said investigators are working to answer these questions and plan to obtain search warrants for the suspects’ cars and phones. He hopes to have more answers by next week. Rondon already is facing two counts of aggravated assault with a firearm, discharging a firearm in public, aggravated fleeing and eluding, driving while license suspended, felony criminal mischief. Valdes has been cited for operating an unregistered motor vehicle and four counts of reckless driving with injuries. Because the incident was a half-mile from Murray Middle School, MCSO activated an active-shooter response and placed the school on lockout. entry.title: Martin County border collie hoarding case moves forward as 30 rescued dogs find new homes - WFLX
entry.summary: Martin County border collie hoarding case moves forward as 30 rescued dogs find new homes    WFLX
entry.article_text: A criminal case involving 36 rescued border collies in Martin County is moving forward. Paige O’Donnell faces 72 criminal charges — two for each dog rescued from her home. She was not present at her docket sounding Thursday afternoon in the Martin County courthouse, but I spoke with her attorney, Russell Ferraro. “At this point I can’t really say anything on her behalf for or against her,” Ferraro said. “We just got the discovery in the case yesterday. We’re organizing it, going through it, and we’ll take it from there.” It has been just under two months since Martin County deputies took 36 dogs out of O’Donnell’s feces-filled home on Aug. The county condemned it days after the Border Collies were rescued. Ferraro said O’Donnell is staying elsewhere while the house is under repair. O’Donnell faces an animal cruelty and improper confinement charge for each dog and has pleaded not guilty. “Everybody’s got a right to a fair trial and to due process,” Ferraro said. The next hearing in O’Donnell’s case is scheduled for Dec. While the outcome of the case remains uncertain, most of O’Donnell’s former dogs have found loving homes. According to the Humane Society of the Treasure Coast, 30 of the dogs have been adopted, five have gone or are about to go to animal rescues, and one remains up for adoption. Lucie and Colleen Tilley near Deltona each adopted one of the rescued border collies. Both say their new family members — now named Nadia and Leila — have had little trouble adjusting to their new lives. “She’s just has an endless amount of energy and just wants to expend it at all times,” Cale said. Cale said Nadia, named after a character from the show “New Girl,” goes to work with him every day and usually warms up to new people after they offer her a treat. “She’s just has an endless amount of energy and just wants to expend it at all times,” Cale said. “When I saw where they came from, I expected a lot more of a challenge,” he added. She wants to be out there and interacting with the world.” “There’s no off switch; it’s all go, go, go,” Tilley said, as Leila raced back and forth behind her in her backyard during a Zoom interview. “It’s really satisfying to see, actually. Just that she’s— she’s happy.” Tilley recalled how nervous Leila was when she first came home on Sept. “At first — like the first three days — it took her to be able to go out the doors— like when I opened the front door, she would run and hide under the bed,” Tilley said. “Now she just runs straight through the sliding glass door, or into it.” Cale and Tilley both said their new border collies have taken well to training as they work to shed old habits, like jumping onto countertops. “I think that’s how they got their food,” Tilley speculated. When Tilley thinks about the criminal case against Leila’s former owner, she wonders what went wrong. Tilley, who showed dogs with her family during her childhood, said she remembers O’Donnell and her outstanding reputation. Like she had very well-bred dogs, very well-trained dogs, beautiful dogs,” Tilley said. “And so all of us were just like, what happened?” Cale revealed that he’d been grieving the loss of his beloved Border Collie, Jessie, who’d died from cancer a year before he heard about what had happened in Palm City. “You just never know when the right dog is gonna come along, and this was the right dog,” Cale said. “(Jessie) was the ride-or-die that would have gone anywhere with me — roaming the woods and getting into mischief ... And that’s gonna be Nadia now.” “You just never know when the right dog is gonna come along, and this was the right dog,” Cale said. The Humane Society of the Treasure Coast says one Border Collie is still up for adoption. entry.title: 'I get chewed to death': St. Lucie County tackles mosquito breeding after heavy rain - WPBF
entry.summary: 'I get chewed to death': St. Lucie County tackles mosquito breeding after heavy rain    WPBF
entry.article_text: Lucie County mosquito control are working to stop mosquitoes from breeding after recent rain created standing water. In a residential neighborhood near U.S. 1 and Fort Pierce, mosquito control teams treated swales and used a backpack blower to distribute larvicide. Officials said the rain has increased standing water, which allows mosquito eggs to hatch. "So relative to last year, mosquito calls have been pretty reduced, but at any moment’s notice following a lot of rain, we can have a huge strike in population, so it's important to be on top of our game," said Daniel Tuzzolino, senior entomologist at St. Lucie County Mosquito Control. DENGUE FEVER: Dengue fever case in Palm Beach County prompts mosquito control action Kenneth Fusco, a nearby resident, shared his experience with the mosquito problem. "If I go out in my front yard and start to do anything, you get bit. I have an island behind me with some cats. If I go over there, I have to wear long pants because I get chewed to death," Fusco said. He added, "Park the truck and leave it for 20 minutes and leave it in front of my house, please!" Crews are also monitoring reports of dengue fever and West Nile virus in surrounding counties. They are asking residents to empty or remove containers holding water to prevent mosquito breeding. Deep Dive: WPBF 25 News Investigates "We are really doubling down and making sure that the people of St. Lucie County know the importance of tipping and tossing because anything that you do to remove potential environment for those dangerous mosquitoes really helps reduce the likelihood that we have transmission in this county," Tuzzolino said. Thursday's heavy rain also caused erosion and a washout along Indian River Drive, where crews were completing a shoulder repair project designed to protect the roadway during heavy rain events. More rain is expected, which could lead to additional standing water and, Tuzzolino said, "A lot more mosquitoes! A lot more mosquitoes!" If you are dealing with a mosquito problem near your home, contact St. Lucie County mosquito control at 772-462-1962 or email mosquito@stlucieco.org. entry.title: 17-year-old dies after shooting near Garcia's Boat Ramp in Indian River County
entry.summary: A 17-year-old died after being shot near a boat ramp in Indian River County late Friday night, according to the Indian River County Sheriff's Office. Deputies responded to reports of a juvenile shot in the 3700 block of County Road 512, near Garcia's Boat Ramp, at approximately 11:24 p.m. The sheriff's office said deputies found the 17-year-old and began lifesaving measures until Indian River County Fire Rescue arrived. The teen was taken to Sebastian River Medical Center before being flown to Holmes Regional Medical Center, where he died from his injuries. Detectives with the sheriff's office's Criminal Investigations Division and crime scene personnel are processing the scene and interviewing multiple witnesses. Investigators said the shooting appears to be an isolated incident and there is no threat to the public. No information about a possible suspect or what led up to the shooting has been released. Anyone with information is asked to call the Indian River County Sheriff's Office at 772-569-6700 or Treasure Coast Crime Stoppers at 1-800-273-TIPS. The investigation remains active.

entry.title: Teen dies after shooting near Garcia's Boat Ramp in Indian River County - WPBF
entry.summary: Teen dies after shooting near Garcia's Boat Ramp in Indian River County    WPBF
entry.article_text: A 17-year-old male died after a shooting late Friday close to a boat ramp near Fellsmere and Vero Beach, the Indian River County Sheriff's Office said Saturday. At 11:24 p.m., deputies responded to reports of a juvenile shot in the area of Garcia's Boat Ramp in the 3700 block of County Road 512 and near the Fort Drum Marsh Conservation Area. Deputies located the 17-year-old and began lifesaving measures until Indian River County Fire Rescue arrived. The teen was taken to Sebastian River Medical Center and later flown to Holmes Regional Medical Center in Melbourne, where he died from his injuries, the sheriff's office said. The person has not been identified. Kevin Jaworski told WPBF the victim was not registered as a student with the Indian River County School District. "At this time, this appears to be an isolated incident, and there is no threat to the public," Jaworski said in an alert to the media. "This is an active investigation." Anyone with information about this incident is asked to call the Indian River County Sheriff’s Office (772-569-6700) or Treasure Coast Crime Stoppers (1-800-273-TIPS). Detectives from the Criminal Investigations Division and crime scene personnel were processing the scene and interviewing multiple witnesses. The area remains open to the public. entry.title: Port St. Lucie man sentenced to 37 1/2 years in Stuart vape shop shooting - WPEC
entry.summary: Port St. Lucie man sentenced to 37 1/2 years in Stuart vape shop shooting    WPEC
entry.article_text: Lucie man convicted in connection with a shooting inside a Stuart vape shop has been sentenced to decades in prison, police said Friday. Joshua Gibbs was sentenced to 37 1/2 years in Florida state prison, followed by 10 years of probation, according to the Stuart Police Department. The sentence stems from the Jan. 25, 2025, shooting at Miller’s Vapory, 1596 SE Federal Highway. Police said Gibbs, then 19, entered the business wearing a ski mask and carrying a handgun before firing at a store clerk. The clerk fired back, and no one was injured. Detectives identified Gibbs as the suspect following an extensive investigation, police said. Authorities arrested him in Douglasville, Georgia, with help from the U.S. Marshals Fugitive Task Force. See also: Ag Reserve meeting draws overflow crowd, tense atmosphere in Delray Beach Police previously said Gibbs had confronted the clerk in December 2024 after he was denied service because he was underage. Investigators said he threatened the clerk and stole more than $300 in vape products. Gibbs was initially accused of attempted robbery with a firearm, aggravated assault with a firearm and robbery without a firearm in connection with the earlier theft.

The Indian River School District said the unnamed teen had recently withdrawn from Sebastian River High School to homeschool and was not enrolled in the district at the time of the shooting. "We are deeply saddened by the loss of this young person, and our hearts are with his family, friends, and the Sebastian River High School community," district spokeswoman Kyra Schafte said in a statement to WPBF. In a follow-up email she wrote: "This remains an active investigation, and we are in constant communication with the Indian River County Sheriff’s Office. Please direct questions about the investigation to IRCSO. Our primary focus is supporting our students, staff, families, and community during this difficult time." At 11:24 p.m., deputies responded to reports of a juvenile shot in the area of Garcia's Boat Ramp in the 3700 block of County Road 512 and near the Fort Drum Marsh Conservation Area. Deputies located the teen and began lifesaving measures until Indian River County Fire Rescue arrived. He was taken to Sebastian River Medical Center and later flown to Holmes Regional Medical Center in Melbourne, where he died from his injuries, the sheriff's office said. "At this time, this appears to be an isolated incident, and there is no threat to the public," Lt. Kevin Jaworski wrote in an alert to the media. "This is an active investigation." He told WPBF that investigators have interviewed all parties involved in the case. Anyone with information about this incident is asked to call the Indian River County Sheriff’s Office (772-569-6700) or Treasure Coast Crime Stoppers (1-800-273-TIPS). entry.title: Tow yard shooting leads to two arrests, multiple crashes in Martin County - cw34.com
entry.summary: Tow yard shooting leads to two arrests, multiple crashes in Martin County    cw34.com
entry.article_text: A second woman has been arrested following a chaotic chain of events that began with a shooting at a Martin County tow yard, triggered a nearby school lockout and ended with multiple crashes and a police pursuit. According to the Martin County Sheriff's Office , the incident unfolded shortly after 1 p.m. Friday at Gary's Towing and Recovery on Southeast Cove Road. 23-year-old Jade Ely Rondon, of Miami, arrived at the tow yard to retrieve a BMW that had been towed earlier in the day. Deputies said another group arrived shortly afterward, leading to an altercation. According to the sheriff's office, Rondon retrieved a firearm and fired multiple shots at the other individuals before fleeing the scene in a vehicle. Because the business is located about a half-mile from Murray Middle School, deputies activated an active-shooter response and placed the school on lockout while officers searched for the suspect. Deputies later located Rondon's vehicle near U.S. 1 and attempted a traffic stop. Investigators said she refused to stop, prompting deputies to perform a PIT maneuver and take her into custody. Rondon was arrested and charged with two counts of aggravated assault with firearm, discharging a firearm in public, aggravated fleeing and eluding, driving while license suspended, and felony criminal mischief. See also: Woman arrested at Mar-a-Lago after claiming Sen. Tom Cotton invited her According to the sheriff's office, Valerie Valdes, 24, had accompanied Rondon to the tow yard to retrieve the BMW. After the shooting, deputies said Valdes fled in the vehicle they originally arrived in. "The other female was driving erratically, passing cars, and ended up losing control, going over into the oncoming lane down U.S. 1 and having a significant crash," sheriff John Budensiek said. Investigators said Valdes ultimately crashed at the intersection of Constitutional Boulevard and U.S. She was taken to Cleveland Clinic Martin South Hospital for treatment of her injuries before being arrested. Valdes is charged with operating an unregistered motor vehicle, and four counts of reckless driving with injuries. The people who were allegedly targeted by the gunfire left the towing facility before deputies arrived. CBS12 News spoke with Gary Reed, owner of Gary's Towing and Recovery, who said he's grateful no one at the business was injured. I love all the people around me. Even the people next door," Reed said. Murray Middle School sent out the following message to families: "Good afternoon, Lions! Please note that we have heavy police presence in the area for an incident unrelated to Murray. We are following Martin County Sheriff's Office guidance and are on a lock out. We will remain in close contact with them and provide additional information as it becomes available. Thank you, Principal Roth" The Martin County Sheriff's Office said the investigation remains active and additional charges are possible.

entry.article_text: Two women are in custody in Martin County after a shooting at a tow yard led to a police chase and a violent crash Friday afternoon. “I have more questions than I have answers,” Martin County Sheriff John Budensiek said. Budensiek said the incident began around 1 p.m. when two women arrived at Gary’s Towing and Recovery, 4405 SE Cove Road, near Stuart, to retrieve a car that had been towed earlier that morning. While they were there, two other individuals showed up to claim the same vehicle. “They got into some type of argument about the belongings in the car, which, by the way, the only thing in the car really was a couple of guns,” Budensiek said. The sheriff said one of the original women then grabbed a gun and began shooting. No one was injured, but bullets struck trailers in the yard. “It’s just crazy how it went down,” said Gary Reed, the owner of Gary’s Towing and Recovery. Reed, who was not present during the shooting, said his employee called him, screaming for help. And I’m running as fast as I can,” Reed said. https://www.facebook.com/MartinCountySheriffsOffice/posts/pfbid0enPBfuxCWxva9Ce6vmU7hGP3nKdhfidsLzp1e7zxkZ58uSYxB3KhHPTdVi9kagZnl By the time deputies and Reed arrived at the scene, all four individuals involved had fled. The sheriff said the accused shooter had taken the car they were disputing, but deputies located her shortly later on Cove Road near U.S. She attempted to flee but was quickly arrested. Investigators identified her as Jade Rondon, 23, from Miami. The other woman she was with has been identified as Valerie Valdes, 22, also from Miami. Budensiek said she was taken into custody after causing a violent collision on U.S. “Why she was driving at a high rate of speed, why she was weaving out of traffic, we’re not sure. We didn’t even know for sure that that car was involved at that time,” Budensiek said. The sheriff said investigators are working to answer these questions and plan to obtain search warrants for the suspects’ cars and phones. He hopes to have more answers by next week. Rondon already is facing two counts of aggravated assault with a firearm, discharging a firearm in public, aggravated fleeing and eluding, driving while license suspended, felony criminal mischief. Valdes has been cited for operating an unregistered motor vehicle and four counts of reckless driving with injuries. Because the incident was a half-mile from Murray Middle School, MCSO activated an active-shooter response and placed the school on lockout. entry.title: 'I get chewed to death': St. Lucie County tackles mosquito breeding after heavy rain - wpbf.com
entry.summary: 'I get chewed to death': St. Lucie County tackles mosquito breeding after heavy rain    wpbf.com
entry.article_text: Lucie County mosquito control are working to stop mosquitoes from breeding after recent rain created standing water. In a residential neighborhood near U.S. 1 and Fort Pierce, mosquito control teams treated swales and used a backpack blower to distribute larvicide. Officials said the rain has increased standing water, which allows mosquito eggs to hatch. "So relative to last year, mosquito calls have been pretty reduced, but at any moment’s notice following a lot of rain, we can have a huge strike in population, so it's important to be on top of our game," said Daniel Tuzzolino, senior entomologist at St. Lucie County Mosquito Control. DENGUE FEVER: Dengue fever case in Palm Beach County prompts mosquito control action Kenneth Fusco, a nearby resident, shared his experience with the mosquito problem. "If I go out in my front yard and start to do anything, you get bit. I have an island behind me with some cats. If I go over there, I have to wear long pants because I get chewed to death," Fusco said. He added, "Park the truck and leave it for 20 minutes and leave it in front of my house, please!" Crews are also monitoring reports of dengue fever and West Nile virus in surrounding counties. They are asking residents to empty or remove containers holding water to prevent mosquito breeding. Deep Dive: WPBF 25 News Investigates "We are really doubling down and making sure that the people of St. Lucie County know the importance of tipping and tossing because anything that you do to remove potential environment for those dangerous mosquitoes really helps reduce the likelihood that we have transmission in this county," Tuzzolino said. Thursday's heavy rain also caused erosion and a washout along Indian River Drive, where crews were completing a shoulder repair project designed to protect the roadway during heavy rain events. More rain is expected, which could lead to additional standing water and, Tuzzolino said, "A lot more mosquitoes! A lot more mosquitoes!" If you are dealing with a mosquito problem near your home, contact St. Lucie County mosquito control at 772-462-1962 or email mosquito@stlucieco.org. According to the sheriff's office, Rondon retrieved a firearm and fired multiple shots at the other individuals before fleeing the scene in a vehicle. Because the business is located about a half-mile from Murray Middle School, deputies activated an active-shooter response and placed the school on lockout while officers searched for the suspect. Deputies later located Rondon's vehicle near U.S. 1 and attempted a traffic stop. Investigators said she refused to stop, prompting deputies to perform a PIT maneuver and take her into custody. After the shooting, deputies said Valdes fled in the vehicle they originally arrived in. "The other female was driving erratically, passing cars, and ended up losing control, going over into the oncoming lane down U.S. 1 and having a significant crash," sheriff John Budensiek said. Investigators said Valdes ultimately crashed at the intersection of Constitutional Boulevard and U.S. She was taken to Cleveland Clinic Martin South Hospital for treatment of her injuries before being arrested. Valdes is charged with operating an unregistered motor vehicle, and four counts of reckless driving with injuries. The people who were allegedly targeted by the gunfire left the towing facility before deputies arrived. entry.summary: The Florida Department of Health in Indian River County has issued a 60-day rabies alert after a bat captured near the Sonrise Apartments tested positive for the virus. Rabies is a viral disease that affects the nervous system of mammals, including humans. Health officials say people who are exposed to rabies can protect themselves by seeking prompt medical treatment after exposure. The Department of Health is reminding residents and visitors to avoid contact with wild animals such as raccoons, bats, foxes, skunks, otters, bobcats and coyotes, which are more likely to carry the disease. Officials also recommend taking several precautions to reduce the risk of exposure, including: Keeping pets vaccinated against rabies Supervising pets and keeping them on a leash Securing livestock on private property Avoiding contact with wild or stray animals, including cats Not feeding or handling wildlife Preventing bats and other wildlife from entering homes, schools and other occupied buildings Anyone bitten or scratched by a wild or domestic animal should seek medical attention and report the incident to the Department of Health in Indian River County at 772-794-7472. If a pet or livestock animal is bitten by another animal, owners should contact a veterinarian immediately and notify Indian River County Animal Control at 772-226-4799. Visit the Florida Department of Health website for more information on rabies.

entry.summary: 'Not knowing where he is': Family searches for missing Port St. Lucie father    cbs12.com
entry.article_text: Eight months after a Port St. Lucie father vanished, his family says they are still searching for answers and living with the painful uncertainty of not knowing where he is. "I'm stuck in this cycle of not knowing where he is," said Aubrey Finley, whose brother, Robert La Polla , disappeared Jan. 8 after being released from a hospital in Fort Pierce. The 47-year-old father has not been seen or heard from since, according to his family. Detectives have no confirmed sightings, and the case remains unsolved. Finley said La Polla struggled with depression following the deaths of their parents, but the siblings remained close and talked often. "Everything kind of fell apart," she said. "But we still managed to communicate a lot. We were still there for each other all the time." Because of that bond, Finley said her brother's disappearance is completely out of character. In the months since he vanished, family members and friends have organized search efforts across Fort Pierce, checking wooded areas and busy corridors near HCA Florida Lawnwood Hospital. "We've gone through woods, under bridges, talking to people everywhere in Fort Pierce, trying to find anything that brings us to him," Finley said. The search has also taken an emotional toll on La Polla's young daughter, who continues to wait for her father to come home. She misses him," Finley said. "He's got a family that love him." The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office (SLCSO) said La Polla has been entered into a national missing persons database. Investigators have also collected DNA from family members in case it is needed for identification and continue to follow up on leads. Anyone with information about La Polla's whereabouts is asked to contact Detective Cpl. Drawdy at 772-462-3230 or call 911.

entry.title: As Buc-ee's nears construction, development interest builds in northern St. Lucie County - cbs12.com
entry.summary: As Buc-ee's nears construction, development interest builds in northern St. Lucie County    cbs12.com
entry.article_text: Buc-ee’s may be best known for its massive travel centers, barbecue sandwiches and loyal fan base, but on the Treasure Coast, county leaders say the proposed development could signal something even bigger: a wave of growth along the Indrio Road corridor in northern St. After years of planning and review, the proposed Buc-ee’s at Interstate 95 and Indrio Road has completed the county’s planning process, bringing the long-discussed project one step closer to reality. The proposed 76,000-square-foot travel center would feature approximately 120 fuel pumps and could become the largest Buc-ee’s location in Florida. Buc-ee’s Nearing Construction Phase According to St. Lucie County Planning and Development Services Director Benjamin Balcer, the project has cleared its local planning hurdles. "They are completely 100% finished with the planning process," Balcer said. "Our board will not see this again." Balcer said the company is now awaiting final approvals from the Florida Department of Transportation and the Florida Department of Environmental Protection before construction can begin. "As far as the county is concerned, their building permit and their site development permit is pretty much at the tail end and ready to go," Balcer said. "It's really just pulling the trigger on Buc-ee's end to start the process." Buc-ee's has previously targeted a 2028 opening date. Development Interest Growing Along Indrio Road While the travel center itself would bring jobs and tax revenue, county officials say its presence also shines a spotlight on a corridor already attracting significant development interest. For now, much of the area remains undeveloped, with cattle grazing across wide stretches of rural land. But Balcer said developers are increasingly looking at opportunities along Indrio Road. "It's kind of an untapped resource," he said. "At the moment, we're seeing a lot of development interest, whether that's pre-application meetings, developers coming in and talking about concept plans, or actual formal applications." Balcer stopped short of calling Buc-ee's the direct catalyst for that interest, but acknowledged that a major national company can influence future investment decisions. "I don't know if Buc-ee's is a catalyst that actually drives development," he said. "But whenever you have a large national commercial entity like Buc-ee's, it does move the needle whenever people see that type of investment." Why the Corridor Is Attracting Attention The area has benefited from recent road and utility improvements, making it increasingly attractive for future residential and commercial projects. County officials say they are already seeing proposals emerge throughout the area. "But all through that Indrio Road corridor, we do see more retail, mixed-use residential projects that are starting to come in and gain traction," Balcer said. Several large developments are either proposed or moving through the review process near the future Buc-ee's site. The proposed Club at Indrio Creek , located south of Indrio Road, could bring hundreds of new homes to the area. Another proposal, Indrio Town Center , would transform approximately 85 acres near Indrio Road and Emerson Avenue into a mixed-use development featuring retail, office space and residential uses. Perhaps the most controversial proposal was Indrio Groves , a development planned near Spanish Lakes Fairways that could add more than 3,000 homes to the area. The size of that proposal has raised concerns among nearby residents who worry about traffic and infrastructure demands. The discussion was tabled over the summer. Residents Voice Infrastructure Concerns But as development proposals continue to stack up, some residents worry infrastructure isn't keeping pace. "That's what people are concerned about," said Jeff Bourassa, president of the Spanish Lakes Fairways Homeowners Association. If they put another 3,000 homes, we're in trouble." Bourassa said residents are worried local roads are not equipped to handle the level of growth being proposed. They're cowpaths," Bourassa said. "There's nothing that was put in for infrastructure." County officials say they understand those concerns. "People are concerned," Balcer said. "Traffic impacts, changing their lifestyle. This is a historical agricultural kind of community." Looking Ahead Whether Buc-ee's ultimately becomes a transformational project remains to be seen. County leaders say the larger story is what comes next for the surrounding area. If Buc-ee's opens and several proposed developments move forward, the character of the Indrio Road corridor could change dramatically over the next decade. "If Buc-ee's does come online, and the projects that are in the pipeline do develop," Balcer said, "you'll see a big difference in the Indrio Road corridor."

entry.summary: Floridians who want to cast a ballot in the 2026 General Election have until Monday, Oct. 5, to register to vote or update their voter registration information. Voters are encouraged to verify that their registration details, including their name, address and party affiliation, are accurate before the deadline. Voters are also urged to confirm their Election Day polling location. Voter registration deadline is Oct. 5 for November election Election Day is scheduled for Tuesday, Nov. 3, with polls open from 7 a.m. to 7 p.m. Residents can register to vote or update their registration online through Florida's voter registration website , by mail or in person using a Florida Voter Registration Application. Applications are also available at Supervisor of Elections Offices and other designated voter registration agencies. Key election deadlines Voter registration deadline: Monday, Oct. 5, 2026 Vote-by-mail request deadline: Thursday, Oct. 22, 2026, by 5 p.m. Early voting dates, locations Palm Beach County: Oct. 19-Nov. 1 from 7 a.m. to 7 p.m. Voters can cast their ballot at any of the 28 locations during this time. Vote-by-mail return deadline is Nov. 3, 2026, by 7 p.m. at the Main Office or by 5 p.m. at a Branch Office or Secure Ballot Intake Station Martin County: Oct. 21-31 from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. each day at six locations across the county. St. Lucie County: Oct. 1931 from 10 a.m. to 6 p.m. daily, including Sunday, Oct. 25. The county will have eight early-voting locations across the county. Indian River County: Oct. 19-31 from 8 a.m. to 4 p.m. with extended hours on Thursdays from 8 a.m. to 6 p.m. Four early-voting locations will be available throughout the county. Vote-by-mail ballots must be received by the Supervisor of Elections office by 7 p.m. Election Day to be counted and may be returned to a secure ballot intake station located at each early voting location during early voting hours, or in person to the Supervisor of Elections office. Okeechobee County: Oct. 24-31 from 8:30 a.m. to 6 p.m. at one location: 307 NW 5th Avenue in Okeechobee Election Day: Tuesday, Nov. 3, 2026, from 7 a.m. to 7 p.m. Voters must cast their ballot at their assigned precinct.

entry.article_text: An SUV lost control on a Florida’s Turnpike ramp near Bayshore Boulevard, crossed into the opposite lane of traffic and overturned Thursday morning, according to video posted by the SLC Scanner Facebook page. entry.summary: Altercation at tow yard leads to shooting, Martin County Sheriff's Office says    WPBF
entry.article_text: Two women are in custody in Martin County after a shooting at a tow yard led to a police chase and a violent crash Friday afternoon. “I have more questions than I have answers,” Martin County Sheriff John Budensiek said. Budensiek said the incident began around 1 p.m. when two women arrived at Gary’s Towing and Recovery, 4405 SE Cove Road, near Stuart, to retrieve a car that had been towed earlier that morning. While they were there, two other individuals showed up to claim the same vehicle. “They got into some type of argument about the belongings in the car, which, by the way, the only thing in the car really was a couple of guns,” Budensiek said. The sheriff said one of the original women then grabbed a gun and began shooting. No one was injured, but bullets struck trailers in the yard. “It’s just crazy how it went down,” said Gary Reed, the owner of Gary’s Towing and Recovery. Reed, who was not present during the shooting, said his employee called him, screaming for help. And I’m running as fast as I can,” Reed said. https://www.facebook.com/MartinCountySheriffsOffice/posts/pfbid0enPBfuxCWxva9Ce6vmU7hGP3nKdhfidsLzp1e7zxkZ58uSYxB3KhHPTdVi9kagZnl By the time deputies and Reed arrived at the scene, all four individuals involved had fled. The sheriff said the accused shooter had taken the car they were disputing, but deputies located her shortly later on Cove Road near U.S. She attempted to flee but was quickly arrested. Investigators identified her as Jade Rondon, 23, from Miami. The other woman she was with has been identified as Valerie Valdes, 22, also from Miami. Budensiek said she was taken into custody after causing a violent collision on U.S. “Why she was driving at a high rate of speed, why she was weaving out of traffic, we’re not sure. We didn’t even know for sure that that car was involved at that time,” Budensiek said. The sheriff said investigators are working to answer these questions and plan to obtain search warrants for the suspects’ cars and phones. He hopes to have more answers by next week. Rondon already is facing two counts of aggravated assault with a firearm, discharging a firearm in public, aggravated fleeing and eluding, driving while license suspended, felony criminal mischief. Valdes has been cited for operating an unregistered motor vehicle and four counts of reckless driving with injuries. Because the incident was a half-mile from Murray Middle School, MCSO activated an active-shooter response and placed the school on lockout. entry.title: 'Not knowing where he is': Family searches for missing Port St. Lucie father - cw34.com
entry.summary: 'Not knowing where he is': Family searches for missing Port St. Lucie father    cw34.com
entry.article_text: Eight months after a Port St. Lucie father vanished, his family says they are still searching for answers and living with the painful uncertainty of not knowing where he is. "I'm stuck in this cycle of not knowing where he is," said Aubrey Finley, whose brother, Robert La Polla , disappeared Jan. 8 after being released from a hospital in Fort Pierce. The 47-year-old father has not been seen or heard from since, according to his family. Detectives have no confirmed sightings, and the case remains unsolved. Finley said La Polla struggled with depression following the deaths of their parents, but the siblings remained close and talked often. "Everything kind of fell apart," she said. "But we still managed to communicate a lot. We were still there for each other all the time." Because of that bond, Finley said her brother's disappearance is completely out of character. In the months since he vanished, family members and friends have organized search efforts across Fort Pierce, checking wooded areas and busy corridors near HCA Florida Lawnwood Hospital. "We've gone through woods, under bridges, talking to people everywhere in Fort Pierce, trying to find anything that brings us to him," Finley said. The search has also taken an emotional toll on La Polla's young daughter, who continues to wait for her father to come home. She misses him," Finley said. "He's got a family that love him." The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office (SLCSO) said La Polla has been entered into a national missing persons database. Investigators have also collected DNA from family members in case it is needed for identification and continue to follow up on leads. Anyone with information about La Polla's whereabouts is asked to contact Detective Cpl. Drawdy at 772-462-3230 or call 911.

entry.title: Indiantown flooding remains a problem despite millions spent on drainage - cw34.com
entry.summary: Indiantown flooding remains a problem despite millions spent on drainage    cw34.com
entry.article_text: Flooding continues to be a problem across Indiantown, leaving some residents questioning why the issue persists despite years of efforts to improve drainage. Large areas of the village saw flooding this week including Booker Park despite spending more than $2 million on drainage improvements in the area in recent years. Residents have seen some improvements over the years but believe more need to be done. I’ve been here almost 60 years and it hasn’t gotten right, Brown said. It is better than it was at some point, but in 60 years you would think it would be far greater than what it is now. The latest round of flooding has affected other parts of Indiantown as well. Oak River saw significant flooding this week, while floodwater also surrounded Indian River Middle School. For residents whose homes take on water, the problem can quickly become a financial burden. Flood insurance can help cover some flood-related damage, but it can also come with a significant cost. For homeowners without a flood policy, recovery can become more difficult. Brian Christensen, president of Coast to Coast Adjuster, said homeowners facing a flood claim without coverage may have to look for other ways to pay for repairs. See also: GALLERY: Ag Reserve meeting draws overflow crowd, tense atmosphere in Delray Beach If you don’t have a flood policy and it is a flood claim and your homeowners policy won’t cut it, I start looking for a loan, Christensen said. Start looking for something a second mortgage, friends, family, churches anything that can assist you. Indiantown Councilman Anthony Dowling said the village is working with Martin County on the flooding problem. The village is also considering a municipal bond that could help address broken pipes and other infrastructure issues. Dowling said the village is repairing pipes that are already damaged and clearing debris from drainage systems. He acknowledged that addressing the flooding problem will not happen overnight and urged residents to take precautions when floodwater is present. I would encourage no kids to play in the water, Dowling said. Village officials say they are continuing to look for ways to address flooding throughout Indiantown. But after years of flooding and millions of dollars spent on drainage improvements residents say they want to know when they will finally see a significant difference.

entry.summary: St. Lucie County teen earns Boys & Girls Clubs' top national honor    wpbf.com
entry.article_text: The Boys Girls Clubs of America has named a St. Lucie County teen the 2026-27 National Youth of the Year, the organization's highest honor for a club member. Stay up to date: The latest headlines and weather from WPBF 25 Enrique Rosario Liz received the award during a national ceremony in New York City on Thursday night after representing Florida and the Southeast Region in the competition. According to the Boys Girls Clubs of St. Lucie County, Enrique first won local and state Youth of the Year titles before advancing to the national level. Enrique moved to the United States from the Dominican Republic when he was 8 years old. Club leaders said he later created a Spanish class for younger members, graduated as valedictorian from Port St. Lucie High School and is now studying elementary education at the University of Florida. Youth of the Year recognizes Boys Girls Club members for leadership, service, academic success and commitment to their communities. entry.title: Teen dies after shooting near Garcia's Boat Ramp in Indian River County - WPBF
entry.summary: Teen dies after shooting near Garcia's Boat Ramp in Indian River County    WPBF
entry.article_text: A 17-year-old boy died after a shooting late Friday close to a boat ramp near Fellsmere and Vero Beach, the Indian River County Sheriff's Office said Saturday. The Indian River School District said the unnamed teen recently withdrew from Sebastian River High School to homeschool and was not enrolled in the district at the time of the shooting. "We are deeply saddened by the loss of this young person, and our hearts are with his family, friends, and the Sebastian River High School community," district spokeswoman Kyra Schafte said in a statement to WPBF. In a follow-up email she wrote: "This remains an active investigation, and we are in constant communication with the Indian River County Sheriff’s Office. Please direct questions about the investigation to IRCSO. Our primary focus is supporting our students, staff, families, and community during this difficult time." A dance is scheduled for 7 p.m. Saturday at Sebastian River High. Read more at: https://www.miamiherald.com/news/article317482082.html#storylink=cpy At 11:24 p.m., deputies responded to reports of a juvenile shot in the area of Garcia's Boat Ramp in the 3700 block of County Road 512 and near the Fort Drum Marsh Conservation Area. Deputies located the teen and began lifesaving measures until Indian River County Fire Rescue arrived. He was taken to Sebastian River Medical Center and later flown to Holmes Regional Medical Center in Melbourne, where he died from his injuries, the sheriff's office said. "At this time, this appears to be an isolated incident, and there is no threat to the public," Lt. Kevin Jaworski wrote in an alert to the media. "This is an active investigation." He told WPBF that investigators have interviewed all parties involved in the case. Anyone with information about this incident is asked to call the Indian River County Sheriff’s Office (772-569-6700) or Treasure Coast Crime Stoppers (1-800-273-TIPS). Detectives from the Criminal Investigations Division and crime scene personnel were processing the scene and interviewing multiple witnesses. The area remains open to the public. entry.title: Manatee safely returns to ocean after washing ashore in Palm Beach while escaping mating males
entry.summary: A female manatee that washed ashore in Palm Beach Saturday morning has safely returned to the ocean, authorities said. The Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission and West Palm Beach police responded after the manatee was found out of the water. Officials at the scene said the female manatee came ashore while trying to get away from male manatees attempting to mate with her. FWC and police remained at the scene and monitored the manatee while waiting for her to return to the water on her own. The manatee eventually made her way off the beach and back into the ocean.

entry.title: Trump holds Ohio midterm rally, urging voters to consider him on the ballot during 32-day campaign tour
entry.summary: President Donald Trump rallied supporters at Butler High School in Ohio on Saturday, urging them to consider him as a key factor as he continued his midterm campaign push. 'We win when I'm on the ballot,' Trump said. The rally is part of what Trump calls a 32-day tour ahead of the election to help boost Republicans amid a number of competitive races across the country. RELATED STORY | New midterm polling gives Democrats an edge in battleground states Ohio is home to several closely watched races. Former Democratic Senator Sherrod Brown is seeking to unseat incumbent Republican Senator Jon Husted in a race that could determine who controls the Senate. Republican Vivek Ramaswamy is also running against Democrat Amy Acton. 'On election night Ohio is going to prove America does not belong to those who hate it, America belongs to those who love it,' Trump said. Trump touted both Republican candidates and his administration to the crowd. His message included promoting investments, tariffs and action against Iran, defending data centers which have divided some Republicans and promising they would ensure the centers benefit communities, while warning against Democratic leadership. A short distance from the rally, 1,400 people at a Navistar truck factory were laid off, according to the Associated Press. The campaign push comes as polls show persistent voter concerns about the economy. A recent AP/NORC poll found only 17% of adults approved of his handling of the cost of living. More broadly, a number of polls show the president's approval rating generally under 40%. IN CASE YOU MISSED IT | Trump claims Iran is waiting until after midterm elections to strike deal Trump dismissed the surveys to the crowd, contending they do not account for his campaigning. 'They don't account that Trump is out campaigning,' he said. He spoke to a high school stadium filled with supporters donning MAGA gear, many touting support for Trump some for all three campaigns. One protestor was drowned out by the crowd. 'I think we're gonna have a surprise,' Trump said. 'Just get out and vote and if you do that we're gonna win big,' Trump said. Trump has acknowledged concern over messaging and races in some states in recent days. His focus in the final weeks ahead of the election has centered on red states to thank supporters including Texas, Oklahoma and Alabama with a visit to Nebraska ahead.

entry.title: 17-year-old dies after shooting near Garcia's Boat Ramp in Indian River County
entry.summary: A 17-year-old died after being shot near a boat ramp in Indian River County late Friday night, according to the Indian River County Sheriff's Office. Deputies responded to reports of a juvenile shot in the 3700 block of County Road 512, near Garcia's Boat Ramp, at approximately 11:24 p.m. 17-year-old dies after shooting near Garcia's Boat Ramp in Indian River County The sheriff's office said deputies found the 17-year-old and began lifesaving measures until Indian River County Fire Rescue arrived. The teen was taken to Sebastian River Medical Center before being flown to Holmes Regional Medical Center, where he died from his injuries. Detectives with the sheriff's office's Criminal Investigations Division and crime scene personnel are processing the scene and interviewing multiple witnesses. Investigators said the shooting appears to be an isolated incident and there is no threat to the public. No information about a possible suspect or what led up to the shooting has been released. Anyone with information is asked to call the Indian River County Sheriff's Office at 772-569-6700 or Treasure Coast Crime Stoppers at 1-800-273-TIPS. The investigation remains active.

entry.title: Port St. Lucie teen named National Youth of the Year by Boys & Girls Clubs of America
entry.summary: A Port St. Lucie teenager has earned the highest honor awarded by the Boys Girls Clubs of America. Enrique Rosario Liz has been named the organizations 2026-27 National Youth of the Year, a recognition that celebrates outstanding leadership, academic achievement and service to others. The honor marks the latest milestone in a remarkable year for Rosario Liz. In April, he was named Florida Youth of the Year. Two months later, he earned the title of Southeast Youth of the Year, advancing to the national level of competition. In July, Rosario Liz received another surprise when the Boys Girls Clubs of America selected him to attend the FIFA World Cup final as a flag bearer. WPTV reporter Tyler Hatfield helped deliver the exciting news during a special presentation. Now, Rosario Liz is being recognized on the national stage as a standout young leader who exemplifies dedication in the classroom, strong personal values and a commitment to serving his community. The National Youth of the Year program honors exceptional teens from Boys Girls Clubs across the country who inspire others through their leadership, character and achievements. Rosario Liz's journey from local club member to national honoree highlights the impact of mentorship, perseverance and community involvement.

entry.title: 'I'm forced to live in this filth': Jensen Beach residents frustrated by recurring septic backups after storms
entry.summary: WPTV is looking into drainage and septic issues on the Treasure Coast. Neighbor Daniel Fletchall reached out to our news team about septic issues in his community on Northwest Sunset Boulevard in Jensen Beach. WATCH BELOW: 'I'm forced to live in this filth': Neighbors demand septic solution Neighbors deal with septic back-ups following heavy rainfall Fletchall said after a heavy rain, he and his neighbors' septic backs up and comes up into their yards 'The sewage water from the septic tank will actually make its way up out of the tank and into my yard,' said Fletchall. 'It smells back here, and I can't let my dog out.' Fletchall said they can't even flush their toilets for days. 'I got to go down to Home Depot or go to the mall to use the bathroom,' said Fletchall. Fletchall added he can't shower or wash his clothes. 'Thankfully, my parents live nearby, so I can go take a shower,' said Fletchall. 'But it's just not happening here. Fletchall isn't the only one affected by this issue. Neighbors like Christie Berger are also having septic issues every time there's heavy rain. 'I go to McDonald's to use the bathroom if I have to,' Berger said. Neighbor Rachelle Kukan said it's becoming unacceptable. 'I wish I could just kind of pick up and move because this is such a problem and it's so serious to me that I would leave if I could,' said Kukan. Fletchall said he had septic companies come out to fix the drainage in his yard. Elevating the septic tank, Fletchall said, would be costly, and even then he's been told it might not solve the problem. Fletchall said he'd like the Martin County staff to extend the sewer lines into his neighborhood. 'I'm forced to live in this filth, and I still pay the taxes every year to have things done around the county, but Im not getting any help here,' said Fletchall. WPTV reached out to Martin County about any solutions. Staff said the neighborhood on Northwest Sunset Boulevard is on the list to get septic-to-sewer conversions, but no date has been set yet. Staff said they're looking at ways to potentially move the neighborhood up on the list of systems to convert.

entry.title: Port St. Lucie man sentenced to 37 1/2 years in Stuart vape shop shooting - cw34.com
entry.summary: Port St. Lucie man sentenced to 37 1/2 years in Stuart vape shop shooting    cw34.com
entry.article_text: Lucie man convicted in connection with a shooting inside a Stuart vape shop has been sentenced to decades in prison, police said Friday. Joshua Gibbs was sentenced to 37 1/2 years in Florida state prison, followed by 10 years of probation, according to the Stuart Police Department. The sentence stems from the Jan. 25, 2025, shooting at Miller’s Vapory, 1596 SE Federal Highway. Police said Gibbs, then 19, entered the business wearing a ski mask and carrying a handgun before firing at a store clerk. The clerk fired back, and no one was injured. Detectives identified Gibbs as the suspect following an extensive investigation, police said. Authorities arrested him in Douglasville, Georgia, with help from the U.S. Marshals Fugitive Task Force. See also: Ag Reserve meeting draws overflow crowd, tense atmosphere in Delray Beach Police previously said Gibbs had confronted the clerk in December 2024 after he was denied service because he was underage. Investigators said he threatened the clerk and stole more than $300 in vape products. Gibbs was initially accused of attempted robbery with a firearm, aggravated assault with a firearm and robbery without a firearm in connection with the earlier theft.

entry.title: 2 women arrested after shooting at Martin County tow yard sparked a chase and crash, more charges possible - wptv.com
entry.summary: 2 women arrested after shooting at Martin County tow yard sparked a chase and crash, more charges possible    wptv.com
entry.article_text: Two women are under arrest after a shooting at Garry's Towing and Recovery in Martin County triggered a school lockout, a police chase and a separate crash. The Martin County Sheriff's Office says more charges could be coming.Jade Rondon, a Miami resident, opened fire in the tow yard on Southeast Cove Road shortly after 1 p.m.WATCH BELOW: Tow yard shooting leads to arrests; more charges possibleThe sheriff's office says the car she came to retrieve had been involved in criminal activity Thursday evening, then reported stolen. Detectives recovered it Friday morning.Around 1 p.m., Rondon arrived at the tow yard accompanied by another woman, Valerie Valdes. Shortly after, individuals in another car arrived at the facility, and the two parties became involved in an altercation, deputies said."They got into some type of argument about the belongings in the car which by the way the only thing really in the car was a couple guns," Sheriff John Budensiek said.Rondon got a gun and fired multiple shots at the other individuals before getting into the car and leaving the area. The individuals who were shot at also left the scene before deputies arrived.Garry Reed, the owner of Garry's Towing and Recovery, said his employee was left shaken by the ordeal."Young lady who works in my office — she was terrorized," Reed said.Reed told me they had helped the Martin County Sheriff's Office recover the car Friday morning, but when the owner came to pick it up this afternoon, things turned dangerous."The young lady went to see what was going on and all of a sudden she heard gunfire," Reed said."[It’s] scary. I'm racing — my heart is racing," Reed said.Because the tow yard is located near Murray Middle School, the sheriff's office immediately activated an active-shooter response and placed the school on lockout.Road patrol deputies, aviation, detectives and other available units quickly began searching for Rondon's car and located it traveling on Cove Road near US-1. Deputies attempted a traffic stop, but she fled, forcing deputies to perform a PIT maneuver to bring the car to a stop.Later, Valdes was reportedly driving recklessly, lost control and caused a significant crash near Osprey Street and US-1. No one was seriously hurt.The Sheriff's Office is still conducting search warrants and reviewing data and video evidence to figure out what happened at the tow yard."We're honestly not sure what we have," Budensiek said. "We're sure that shots are fired. We're sure that she fled from our deputies. Something happened with that vehicle the night before. There was a reason why everyone had interest in that car."Rondon faces two counts of aggravated assault with a firearm, discharging a firearm in public, aggravated fleeing and eluding, driving with a suspended license and felony criminal mischief. Valdes faces charges for operating an unregistered motor vehicle and four counts of reckless driving with injuries. The sheriff says more charges are likely as investigators piece together what happened.Despite the chaos, Reed said he is counting his blessings."Thank God that everybody was okay," Reed said.This story was reported on-air by a journalist and has been converted to this platform with the assistance of AI. Our editorial team verifies all reporting on all platforms for fairness and accuracy.

entry.summary: Port St. Lucie man sentenced to 37 1/2 years in Stuart vape shop shooting    cw34.com
entry.article_text: Lucie man convicted in connection with a shooting inside a Stuart vape shop has been sentenced to decades in prison, police said Friday. Joshua Gibbs was sentenced to 37 1/2 years in Florida state prison, followed by 10 years of probation, according to the Stuart Police Department. The sentence stems from the Jan. 25, 2025, shooting at Miller’s Vapory, 1596 SE Federal Highway. Police said Gibbs, then 19, entered the business wearing a ski mask and carrying a handgun before firing at a store clerk. The clerk fired back, and no one was injured. Detectives identified Gibbs as the suspect following an extensive investigation, police said. Authorities arrested him in Douglasville, Georgia, with help from the U.S. Marshals Fugitive Task Force. See also: Ag Reserve meeting draws overflow crowd, tense atmosphere in Delray Beach Police previously said Gibbs had confronted the clerk in December 2024 after he was denied service because he was underage. Investigators said he threatened the clerk and stole more than $300 in vape products. Gibbs was initially accused of attempted robbery with a firearm, aggravated assault with a firearm and robbery without a firearm in connection with the earlier theft.

entry.summary: Miami woman in custody after shooting at tow yard near Murray Middle School in Martin County    wflx.com
entry.article_text: A shooting at a tow yard Friday afternoon near a middle school in Martin County triggered a lockout and led to a chase and a Miami woman in custody. The woman opened fire at a tow yard on Southeast Cove Road shortly after 1 p.m., the Martin County Sheriff’s Office said. According to deputies, the woman arrived at the towing facility to claim a car that had been towed there earlier in the day. Shortly after, individuals in another car arrived at the facility, and the two parties became involved in an altercation, deputies said. The woman got a gun and fired multiple shots at the other individuals before getting into a car and leaving the area. Since the tow yard is located near Murray Middle School, the sheriff’s office said it immediately activated an active-shooter response and placed the school on lockout as deputies responded to the scene. Road patrol deputies, aviation, detectives and other available units quickly began searching for the woman’s car, deputies said, and located the car traveling on Cove Road near U.S. 1 Deputies said they attempted a traffic stop but the driver fled, forcing deputies to perform a PIT maneuver, bringing the car to a stop. The individuals who were shot at left the area before deputies arrived, the sheriff’s office said. It is unclear whether any of them were struck by gunfire. The woman was taken into custody and transported to the sheriff’s office, where detectives are currently questioning her. Deputies said additional information will be provided as it becomes available.

entry.title: Rabies alert issued in Indian River County after rabid bat found near apartment complex - wflx.com
entry.summary: Rabies alert issued in Indian River County after rabid bat found near apartment complex    wflx.com
entry.article_text: The Florida Department of Health in Indian River County has issued a 60-day rabies alert after a bat captured near the Sonrise Apartments tested positive for the virus. Health officials said the bat was captured in the Sonrise Apartments area off Sonrise Place in Fellsmere on Sept. Anyone who may have had contact with or touched the bat is urged to contact the Department of Health in Indian River County at 772-794-7472. The alert comes as health officials monitor rabies activity among wild animals in the area and warn residents that the disease is present in the local wildlife population. Rabies is a viral disease that affects the nervous system of mammals, including humans. Health officials say people who are exposed to rabies can protect themselves by seeking prompt medical treatment after exposure. The Department of Health is reminding residents and visitors to avoid contact with wild animals such as raccoons, bats, foxes, skunks, otters, bobcats and coyotes, which are more likely to carry the disease. Officials also recommend taking several precautions to reduce the risk of exposure, including: Anyone bitten or scratched by a wild or domestic animal should seek medical attention and report the incident to the Department of Health in Indian River County at 772-794-7472. If a pet or livestock animal is bitten by another animal, owners should contact a veterinarian immediately and notify Indian River County Animal Control at 772-226-4799. Visit the Florida Department of Health website for more information on rabies.

entry.summary: 17-year-old dies after shooting near Garcia's Boat Ramp in Indian River County    wflx.com
entry.article_text: A 17-year-old died after being shot near a boat ramp in Indian River County late Friday night, according to the Indian River County Sheriff's Office. Deputies responded to reports of a juvenile shot in the 3700 block of County Road 512, near Garcia's Boat Ramp, at approximately 11:24 p.m. The sheriff's office said deputies found the 17-year-old and began lifesaving measures until Indian River County Fire Rescue arrived. The teen was taken to Sebastian River Medical Center before being flown to Holmes Regional Medical Center, where he died from his injuries. Detectives with the sheriff's office's Criminal Investigations Division and crime scene personnel are processing the scene and interviewing multiple witnesses. Investigators said the shooting appears to be an isolated incident and there is no threat to the public. No information about a possible suspect or what led up to the shooting has been released. Anyone with information is asked to call the Indian River County Sheriff's Office at 772-569-6700 or Treasure Coast Crime Stoppers at 1-800-273-TIPS. The investigation remains active.

entry.article_text: Lucie man convicted in connection with a shooting inside a Stuart vape shop has been sentenced to decades in prison, police said Friday. Joshua Gibbs was sentenced to 37 1/2 years in Florida state prison, followed by 10 years of probation, according to the Stuart Police Department. The sentence stems from the Jan. 25, 2025, shooting at Miller’s Vapory, 1596 SE Federal Highway. Police said Gibbs, then 19, entered the business wearing a ski mask and carrying a handgun before firing at a store clerk. The clerk fired back, and no one was injured. Detectives identified Gibbs as the suspect following an extensive investigation, police said. Authorities arrested him in Douglasville, Georgia, with help from the U.S. Marshals Fugitive Task Force. See also: Ag Reserve meeting draws overflow crowd, tense atmosphere in Delray Beach Police previously said Gibbs had confronted the clerk in December 2024 after he was denied service because he was underage. Investigators said he threatened the clerk and stole more than $300 in vape products. Gibbs was initially accused of attempted robbery with a firearm, aggravated assault with a firearm and robbery without a firearm in connection with the earlier theft.

entry.title: SLC seniors demand answers as Fort Pierce center prepares to close
entry.summary: A Fort Pierce senior center is expected to close, leaving some of the older adults who rely on it worried about losing a gathering place in their own community. The Council on Aging of St. Lucie confirmed the senior center at 1505 Orange Avenue in Fort Pierce is expected to close in the near future. The property is currently listed for sale for $2.2 million. The news came as a surprise to some seniors who use the center regularly, including 77-year-old Sandy Pietrewicz. She has relied on the center for nearly a decade. That's the community center that I go to for lunch and friendship and social activities with other elderly women, said Pietrewicz. After hearing the center could be closing, Pietrewicz said she and other seniors were left with questions about what would happen to the services they depend on. We were all talking about who we could contact, and I thought of WPTV immediately, she said. WPTV reporter Brooke Chau went to the center to get answers and hear directly from the seniors who use it. The Council on Aging said the closure will not mean an end to the services provided to seniors. You're going to get the same treatment. You're going to get the same love. You're going to get the same meals, said Trekina Smith with the Council on Aging. Once the property sells, seniors who currently use the Orange Avenue location are expected to transition to the Council on Aging's facility on Bayshore Boulevard in Port St. Lucie. The organization said transportation will be provided to help seniors get to the new location. But some seniors say the location itself is important. That makes us even angrier. We can't have something in our own community, Pietrewicz said. Geneira Lovett, who also uses the center, told WPTV that seniors in Fort Pierce want to be able to access services close to where they live. We live here, we want rights to do thing, besides trouble, Lovett said. The Council on Aging said it understands those concerns, but says change is necessary. For now, the Council on Aging says services at the Orange Avenue center are continuing. There is no finalized timeline for the closure because the transition is tied to the sale of the property. We understand the concerns, it's a change for us too. But hey, change comes, and you got to go with the change, Smith said. The organization said seniors will continue to have access to meals, activities, social opportunities and transportation once services move to the Port St. Lucie location.

entry.title: Wrong-way driver causes deadly 3-vehicle crash on I-95 in West Palm Beach
entry.summary: A wrong-way driver sparked a deadly three-vehicle crash early Sunday morning on I-95 in West Palm Beach, killing one person and seriously injuring two others, according to the Florida Highway Patrol (FHP). The crash happened around 5:30 a.m. Sunday on the northbound lanes of I-95 near Palm Beach Lakes Boulevard. Investigators say a GMC Sierra pickup truck was traveling south in the inside lane of northbound I-95, driving the wrong way as it approached Palm Beach Lakes Boulevard. A Dodge Grand Caravan was traveling north in the inside lane when its driver, a 68-year-old West Palm Beach man, attempted to swerve right to avoid the oncoming pickup, but was unable to avoid collision. Following the initial impact, the pickup rotated and came to rest in the inside northbound lane. The van spun across the roadway from west to east. A Cadillac El Dorado was traveling north behind the van and was unable to avoid the wreckage. The Cadillac then struck the rear of the van, according to FHP. The driver of the Dodge Grand Caravan was pronounced dead at the scene. FHP has not shared the identity of the driver. The wrong-way driver, a 26-year-old West Palm Beach man, and the Cadillac driver suffered serious injuries and were transported to St. Mary's Medical Center for treatment. All northbound lanes of I-95 at Palm Beach Lakes Boulevard remained closed while the crash was being investigated, but have since reopened.

entry.title: 3 Ag Reserve projects fuel growth concerns among western Delray Beach residents
entry.summary: Western Delray Beach residents are voicing concerns about growth and development in the Agricultural Reserve as three major projects move forward along Lyons Road, including a new driver's license office, a nursing home and an Islamic school and daycare. The debate intensified Friday after a public meeting hosted by Palm Beach County Commissioner Maria Sachs that drew hundreds of residents seeking answers about traffic, zoning and public notification. WATCH BELOW: 3 Ag Reserve projects spark debate in western Delray 3 Ag Reserve projects spark growth debate in Western Delray Beach The projects are already at various stages of approval and construction, but some neighbors say they were not adequately informed about developments that could significantly change the character of the area. As Palm Beach County continues to experience rapid population growth, development in the Ag Reserve has become a recurring issue for residents concerned about traffic congestion, infrastructure demands and preservation of open land. The latest projects have reignited that debate in western Delray Beach. Public meeting draws large crowd Hundreds of residents attended a public meeting Friday hosted by Commissioner Sachs to discuss development activity in the Agricultural Reserve. Residents raised concerns about traffic, density and transparency in the approval process. One resident, Michelle, said she believes nearby homeowners should have received more notice before projects advanced. 'We were not notified,' Michelle said. 'This is a natural reserve and if you're going to destroy the natural reserve you need to notify residents who live in the neighborhood.' Others questioned whether development should continue in the area at all, arguing the Agricultural Reserve should remain protected from additional growth. Three projects moving forward 1. New DMV under construction One of the projects is a new Palm Beach County Tax Collector's Office facility , which WPTV previously reported on. According to county officials, Palm Beach County Tax Collector Anne Gannon purchased the property for approximately $4.3 million. The facility will replace the current office on Congress Avenue. Construction is already underway on the 4.2-acre site, with the new location expected to open in 2027. 2. Nursing home planned Another proposal moving forward is All Seasons, a nursing home development planned on nearly 9 acres. Project documents show the facility will include more than 150 units. entry.title: Arya Tea Bar makes GreenMarket debut as one of this season's new vendors
entry.summary: The West Palm Beach GreenMarket is known for bringing together local farmers, makers and small businesses, and this season, five new vendors are joining the lineup. On Saturday, WPTV reporter Christy Waite showcased one of them. WATCH Arya Tea Bar Makes GreenMarket Debut as One of This Season's New Vendors Small Business Saturday at the GreenMarket Arya Tea Bar, a downtown West Palm Beach tea shop, specializes in matcha drinks, loose-leaf teas and fruit refreshers made with clean, high-quality ingredients. Owner Sophie DeWaal says tea has always been a part of her life. 'I have drunk tea my whole life. I have only ever had coffee literally three times,' DeWaal said. At her Clematis Street storefront, customers can find classic teas, specialty matcha drinks and loose-leaf teas sourced from around the world. DeWaal said she carefully selected teas she believes are the best representation of their type, including hibiscus, black tea, Earl Grey and Japanese floral teas she discovered while visiting Japan. Arya Tea Bar also offers fruit refreshers that can be made with either tea or lemonade. The drinks feature house-made fruit purees and freshly diced fruit. 'When matcha became a thing, I was like, this is amazing. There is so much cool stuff you can do with it. If you use high-quality tea, you can use clean ingredients and not fill it with a bunch of sugar and still get a really nice drink.' Popular menu items include strawberry, mango and lavender matchas, along with the shop's bestselling salted date matcha. 'The salted date matcha is one of our most popular,' DeWaal said. Arya Tea Bar opened its Clematis Street storefront in January, but DeWaal's connection to the GreenMarket began long before she became a vendor. She said the GreenMarket was one of the reasons she decided to move to West Palm Beach and was thrilled when she learned Arya Tea Bar had been selected as a vendor this season. 'I feel like I got into the Harvard of farmers' markets,' DeWaal said. 'I moved to West Palm because of the GreenMarket.' Now, she's excited to introduce her products to a whole new audience. 'I am so excited to meet everyone and meet the people who are interested in what we have to offer. I think it's really unique,' she said. The business also carries a personal connection for DeWaal. Arya Tea Bar is named after her horse, Arya, a nod to the years she spent horseback riding and show jumping in Wellington. As one of five new vendors joining the West Palm Beach GreenMarket

Rosario Liz's journey from local club member to national honoree highlights the impact of mentorship, perseverance and community involvement.

entry.title: Panthers place Aleksander Barkov on long-term injured reserve with injury to left leg
entry.summary: Florida center Aleksander Barkov has been placed on long-term injured reserve by the Panthers, meaning the injury to his left leg will keep him sidelined for at least the next 10 games and quite possibly beyond. The Panthers are still unclear on the extent of Barkov's injury , coach Paul Maurice said, adding that Barkov will see Florida team physicians on Monday. RELATED: More Panthers news 'We know its going to be 10 (games) anyway,' Maurice said after the Panthers practiced in Irvine, California. 'Well see what they say Monday. ... Im not the doctor here. So, well see. Whatever they say.' Florida made a pair of roster additions after placing Barkov on the injured list Saturday, bringing up center Sam Lafferty and defenseman Alexander Petrovic. Barkov was hurt midway through the second period of Florida's 4-3 overtime loss to the San Jose Sharks on Thursday night. He was jostling for the puck along the boards, got pushed by the Sharks' Darnell Nurse and awkwardly fell to the ice with his left leg at an unnatural angle. It appeared his knee buckled on the play. Barkov remained down for a few moments, then got up and headed toward the tunnel leading to the Florida dressing room. He walked with a bit of a limp and appeared to angrily try to throw off his gloves as he moved toward the room. Barkov Florida's captain and a huge part of the Panthers' runs to Stanley Cup championships in 2024 and 2025 missed the entire 2025-26 season with torn ligaments in his right knee. He went scoreless in his first two appearance of this season for Florida, which plays Sunday at Anaheim. There was some good injury news Saturday, with Maurice saying that forward Brad Marchand is getting closer to making his season debut 'real close,' Maurice said and that defenseman Gustav Forsling, who had the overtime goal in the opener at Carolina but was a last-minute scratch at San Jose with an upper body issue, is a game-time decision for Sunday.

entry.title: Vikings defeat Dolphins 15-10 as Miami still searches for first win of season
entry.summary: Kyler Murray and the Minnesota Vikings' offense would've appreciated a touchdown for their progress down the stretch, but there was only one way to truly secure this victory. T.J. Hockenson fittingly took the winning slide. The Vikings stayed undefeated with more dominance by their defense and five field goals from Will Reichard, sidestepping their early passing game problems to beat the winless Miami Dolphins 15-10 on Sunday. Hockenson tied a career high with 13 receptions for 119 yards on 13 targets from Murray, including the game-sealing 8-yard catch on third-and-5 from the 10. The eighth-year tight end was wide open and could've coasted into the end zone, but he wisely slid in front of the goal line to drain the clock to the two-minute warning. 'Once you get the first down, you've got to get down,' said Hockenson, who had his highest yardage total since Week 10 of the 2023 season. 'It was tough. I saw that goal line and I wanted it, but it's for the betterment of the team that we ended on offense.' With the Dolphins out of timeouts, the Vikings had Murray take three straight kneel-downs to move to 4-0 for the second time in three years despite going without a touchdown in two games. 'If we want to score, we should do it earlier,' Vikings coach Kevin O'Connell said. Murray finished 27 for 37 for 247 yards without a turnover, but he took four sacks for 34 yards against a Dolphins defense that had none in the first three games and was often tentative and unsteady in the pocket until Hockenson helped him open up the field with a handful of clutch and difficult catches. The Dolphins, who are 0-4 for the first time since starting 0-7 in 2019 in their first season under then-coach Brian Flores, were crushed by a combination of unforced mistakes including nine penalties for 55 yards. New Dolphins quarterback Malik Willis went just 9 for 17 for 85 yards, losing a fumble during one of the two sacks by Dallas Turner. The four teams the Dolphins have faced in coach Jeff Hafley's first year are 15-1. 'You hate the feeling of continuing to get better without actually gaining wins on the win column, but as we see, we're going out there and competing,' Willis said.
