entry.title: Teen identified after deadly Fellsmere shooting involving 100-plus teens - WPEC
entry.summary: Teen identified after deadly Fellsmere shooting involving 100-plus teens    WPEC
entry.article_text: A 17-year-old was killed in a Fellsmere shooting Friday night after a meetup of more than 100 teens turned violent, according to the sheriff. The shooting happened around 11:24 p.m. at Garcia’s Boat Ramp , where a large crowd had gathered. Sheriff Eric Flowers said the group included teens ages 14 to 19, with drinking and fighting reported. These have been happening since before I was in high school, since before many of you were in high school. This has been going on for a long time. But now we're adding guns into the mix, and we're adding social media into the mix. CBS12 confirmed with the family that the slain 17-year-old was Sulliman Bah, a senior at Sebastian River High School. He and a group of friends approached a pickup truck with two 18-year-olds inside. Detectives say Bah opened the door and attempted to punch someone inside when the passenger fired a single shot at Bah. See also: What Florida voters need to know about the 3 constitutional amendments on the Nov. ballot Bah was taken by friends toward Fellsmere. Deputies and EMS met them at Fellsmere City Hall and performed CPR before he was taken to Sebastian River Medical Center and later transported to Holmes Regional Medical Center in Melbourne, where he succumbed to his injuries. No arrests have been made. Flowers said the driver and passenger inside the truck have cooperated with investigators and turned over the truck and firearm. The sheriff said the preliminary investigation indicates a self-defense claim may apply. We will be submitting a warrant in the case, but at this time it looks as though there will be a self-defense claim as a result, Flowers said. The sheriff said the state will ultimately decide whether charges are filed. Investigators used Flock technology to identify people connected to the truck and shooting. Deputies also recovered additional guns and multiple shell casings. Flowers said investigators believe the meetup was part of a growing trend of teens gathering at remote locations arranged through Snapchat , where fights are recorded and shared online. "We got kids out here losing their lives chasing likes and shares on social media," he said. "We've got kids out here losing their lives trying to go viral on social media." He said there may have been as many as four fights at the boat ramp that night, and investigators are still working to identify people who were there. "They had a history of fighting," Flowers said. "This has been an ongoing thing." The sheriff urged parents to ask their children whether they attended the meetup and encouraged anyone who witnessed the shooting or recorded it to contact investigators. "It's not safe," Flowers said. There's guns, and those two just don't mix. And now add in the fuel of the fire of social media, and now we have a 17-year-old dead." In a statement, the Indian River School District gave its condolences to the teen's family: The School District of Indian River County is heartbroken by this young person’s death. Our hearts are with his family, friends, and the students and staff who knew and cared about him. Grief support was in place over the weekend, including counselors at Sebastian River High School’s Homecoming Dance, and continues today as students and staff return to school. Our teams will remain available in the days ahead, offering care and responding to the needs of those affected. A spokesperson for SDIRC said the student had recently withdrawn from Sebastian River High School to be home schooled.

entry.title: I-Team investigates Florida rules for seatbelts on school buses after fatal crash in Winter Haven
entry.summary: A deadly school bus crash in Polk County is raising new questions about how students are protected inside Florida school buses and why state law still falls short of federal safety recommendations. One student, a 10th grader on her way to Winter Haven High School, was killed Monday morning when a school bus carrying 39 people was involved in a crash. The circumstances surrounding the crash remain under investigation, including what happened outside the bus and what took place inside it. Watch report from Katie Lagrone School bus seatbelts 'We have one fatality of a beautiful high school girl. It's just heartbreaking,' Polk County Sheriff Grady Judd said during a morning news briefing. Investigators have not released details about how many students were wearing seat belts, what type of restraints were in use, or whether the belts played a role in the outcome of the crash. Florida requires seat belts, but not the type federal investigators recommend Florida law requires school buses built since 2001 to be equipped with seat belts. However, students are not required to wear them, and state law does not require the more protective lap-and-shoulder belts recommended by federal safety investigators. Instead, many Florida school buses continue to use standard lap belts. The federal recommendation followed an investigation by investigative reporter Katie LaGrone more than a decade ago. In 2012, a St. Lucie County school bus collided with a semi-truck, killing 9-year-old Aaron Beauchamp. Aaron was wearing the bus's standard lap belt at the time of the crash. Several years later, investigators with the National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) examined that crash and studied how different types of seat belts affect student safety. The agency's testing showed significant differences between standard lap belts and lap-and-shoulder restraints. Simulations demonstrated that lap-and-shoulder belts provide greater protection by better controlling a passenger's movement during a crash. As a result, the NTSB recommended that all school buses nationwide be equipped with lap-and-shoulder belts. Federal recommendation to Florida went unanswered The NTSB specifically urged Florida to change state law to require lap-and-shoulder belts on new large school buses. That recommendation was never adopted. Today, it remains unclear how many Florida school districts have voluntarily upgraded their fleets to meet the federal recommendation. Simulations demonstrated that lap-and-shoulder belts provide greater protection by better controlling a passenger's movement during a crash.As a result, the NTSB recommended that all school buses nationwide be equipped with lap-and-shoulder belts.The NTSB specifically urged Florida to change state law to require lap-and-shoulder belts on new large school buses.That recommendation was never adopted.Today, it remains unclear how many Florida school districts have voluntarily upgraded their fleets to meet the federal recommendation.In St. Lucie County, nearly 15 years after Aaron's death, about 20% of district school buses still use only standard lap belts.In Polk County, a district spokesperson confirmed on Monday that all the district’s school buses are equipped with just lap belts.The latest crash has renewed questions about whether stronger seat belt requirements could better protect students who are traveling to and from school on a school bus.Despite the concerns raised by this tragedy, transportation safety experts continue to emphasize that deadly school bus crashes are extremely rare, and that school buses remain the safest form of transportation for students traveling to and from school.For families in Polk County and across Florida, the crash could prompt renewed scrutiny of whether the state's school bus safety standards should be updated to reflect federal recommendations."No one will ever understand how heavy this weighs on our hearts," Polk County Schools Superintendent Fred Heid said following the crash.

entry.title: No arrests after 17-year-old shot, killed at meetup in Indian River County, self-defense claim expected - WPTV
entry.summary: No arrests after 17-year-old shot, killed at meetup in Indian River County, self-defense claim expected    WPTV
entry.article_text: No arrests have been made in the shooting death of a 17-year-old at a teen meetup near Garcia's Boat Ramp in Indian River County, with a self-defense claim expected in the case, Indian River County Sheriff Eric Flowers announced Monday.WATCH BELOW: Sheriff Eric Flowers give update on shooting death of teen"We got kids out here losing their lives chasing likes and shares on social media," Flowers said.The shooting occurred late Friday night when approximately 100 teens, ranging in age from 14 to 19, gathered at Garcia's Boat Ramp in the 3700 block of County Road 512, the sheriff said. Deputies had broken up a similar group earlier that evening before the crowd moved to the boat ramp."The 17-year-old, and a group of his friends, are approaching a truck, and there are two people, both 18 years old, inside of that truck. The 17-year-old opens the door, and he starts to punch," Flowers said. "He's going to punch on the people that are inside of that truck. That shot is the shot that ultimately killed 17-year-old in this case."The teen's friends drove him away from the scene, east on County Road 512, while calling 911 and a dispatcher told them to stop at Fellsmere City Hall, where emergency crews performed CPR, the sheriff said. He was taken to Sebastian River Medical Center and later flown to Holmes Regional Medical Center in Melbourne, where he died from his injuries.The two individuals in the truck were identified using the sheriff's office's Flock technology, the sheriff said. Flowers said both have been cooperative with investigators, surrendering the weapon used in the shooting and the truck. Additional individuals involved in the incident have also been identified through Flock, though some remain unidentified. Investigators also recovered other weapons from the vehicle in which the 17-year-old was transported from the scene.WATCH: 17-year-old dies after shooting near Garcia's Boat RampFlowers said a warrant will be submitted in the case, but it will be up to the state to determine whether charges are filed."There have been no arrests on this case at this time, because the preliminary investigation shows that the 17-year-old was opening the door to attempt to fight with the two that were inside of the vehicle. They had a history of fighting," Flowers said. "Self defense plays a part in these, and when these kids go out and videotape these fights, and now guns are involved, there's going to be more of this." Names of those involved are not being released as the investigation continues, the sheriff said.Investigators believe at least four fights occurred at the boat ramp on the night of the shooting. Multiple shell casings and rounds were recovered from the scene.During Monday's news conference, Flowers released video of the shooting, noting the footage had already circulated widely on social media and that the victim's mother had seen it. One of the 18-year-olds involved in the shooting attends Vero Beach High School.The sheriff said teen meetups like the one at Garcia's Boat Ramp are coordinated through Snapchat, making them difficult for law enforcement to track in advance."When it's Snapchat, it's basically a private conversation," Flowers said. "But it quickly can escalate to over 100, 150, 200 people there."Flowers said the meetups, which have included alcohol, fighting, and firearms, have been taking place for years across Indian River County, Okeechobee, and surrounding areas, but that social media has intensified the danger."Now we're adding guns and alcohol into the mix, and we're adding social media into the mix, and so what we're seeing is an escalation of each one of these," Flowers said. There's guns, and those two just don't mix. And now add in the fuel of the fire of social media, and now we have a 17-year-old dead."The sheriff said teens at these gatherings are motivated in part by a desire for online attention."The kids like to fight, and they like to videotape it, and they like to get their likes and shares because of that," Flowers said. Parents, you see these videos. You do not want your teens out at these meetups."With Vero Beach High School's homecoming game scheduled for Friday and the dance on Saturday, Flowers said additional deputies will be on duty. Meanwhile, the sheriff urged parents to monitor their children's whereabouts and report any information about planned meetups to the sheriff's office."Parents, if your kids are telling you that they're headed out to one of these meetups, ask them where they're going. Ask, find out the details. Share that with us," Flowers said.He recommended parents use location-sharing apps such as Life360 to track their children and said a child appearing to be in a remote or unusual location can be an indicator that a meetup is taking place.The investigation remains active. Flowers said anyone who witnessed any of the events that night, including the shooting itself, and has not yet spoken to investigators is urged to come forward."I can tell you, our investigation is not even remotely over, and if we are able to identify people that were involved in this, from underage drinking to fighting, hurting other people," Flowers said. " If they did something wrong, they're going to have to be accountable for that."Anyone with information is asked to call the Indian River County Sheriff's Office at 772-569-6700 or Treasure Coast Crime Stoppers at 1-800-273-TIPS.

entry.title: Gov. Ron DeSantis announces removal of 220 Medicaid providers amid fraud, abuse investigation
entry.summary: Governor Ron DeSantis announced Tuesday that Florida's intensified effort to root out fraud, waste and abuse in the state's Medicaid program has resulted in more than $1 billion in projected savings and the removal of hundreds of providers from the system. Speaking at the Healthcare District of Palm Beach County alongside Agency for Health Care Administration (AHCA) Secretary Shevaun Harris, DeSantis said the state has expanded oversight and enforcement measures to identify fraudulent billing and improper Medicaid payments. 'We want to make sure that what is being spent is being spent well,' DeSantis said. 'Medicaid dollars must go to healthcare for eligible Floridians, not to people who are gaming the system.' According to state officials, AHCA has conducted more than 400 provider site visits since January and increased the use of data analytics, claims monitoring and background screening to uncover suspicious activity. As part of the crackdown, the state said more than 150 fraud-related referrals have been made to the Florida Attorney General's Office over the past year, more than 250 providers have been placed on payment restrictions or had payments suspended, and more than 220 providers have been terminated from Florida Medicaid due to fraud, waste or abuse. State officials said those terminated providers accounted for more than $230 million in Medicaid billing in 2025. A major focus of the effort has been Applied Behavioral Analysis (ABA) services, commonly used to help children with autism. According to Harris, Florida Medicaid spent approximately $6.57 billion on ABA services between 2023 and 2025, nearly four times more than any other state's Medicaid program. "Medicaid dollars must go to healthcare for eligible Floridians, not to people who are gaming the system."According to state officials, AHCA has conducted more than 400 provider site visits since January and increased the use of data analytics, claims monitoring and background screening to uncover suspicious activity.As part of the crackdown, the state said more than 150 fraud-related referrals have been made to the Florida Attorney General's Office over the past year, more than 250 providers have been placed on payment restrictions or had payments suspended, and more than 220 providers have been terminated from Florida Medicaid due to fraud, waste or abuse.State officials said those terminated providers accounted for more than $230 million in Medicaid billing in 2025.A major focus of the effort has been Applied Behavioral Analysis (ABA) services, commonly used to help children with autism. According to Harris, Florida Medicaid spent approximately $6.57 billion on ABA services between 2023 and 2025, nearly four times more than any other state's Medicaid program. At one point, spending was projected to grow by 30% annually.The state moved ABA services into managed care in 2025, a change officials say has improved oversight and slowed spending growth to less than 10% annually. As a result, the state now projects ABA-related expenditures at roughly $2.8 billion, more than $1 billion lower than previous forecasts."That is where we want our funding going," Harris said. "Not in the pockets of crooks."Investigators uncovered instances in which providers billed Medicaid for impossible service schedules, including claims for more than 24 hours of care in a single day and services allegedly provided continuously through weekends and holidays.To strengthen provider screening, AHCA also partnered with identity verification company SentiLink to help identify synthetic identities, suspicious ownership structures and other potential fraud indicators before providers enter the Medicaid system.Despite the enforcement actions, DeSantis and Harris emphasized that the effort is aimed at fraudulent providers and not families who rely on Medicaid services.When WPTV Investigative Reporter Jamie Ostroff asked about concerns from families struggling to access ABA therapy, particularly in Palm Beach County, Harris said managed care plans are working with affected recipients to connect them with new providers when a provider is removed from the program."If there is a parent watching and they're having any issues, they can contact the agency and we will help them ourselves or connect them with their managed care plan," Harris said.DeSantis said the Medicaid initiative is part of a broader effort to ensure taxpayer dollars are spent responsibly while maintaining Florida's fiscal position. The governor highlighted the state's recent budget reductions, debt repayment efforts and tax relief measures as examples of what he described as responsible financial management.State officials said AHCA will continue conducting site visits, monitoring claims and referring suspected fraud cases for further investigation."This is kind of just the opening salvo," DeSantis said. "I would anticipate you will see more results coming in the weeks, months and years ahead."

entry.article_text: Five years after the shooting death of a 20-year-old woman, the Port St. Lucie Police Department is still seeking answers. Lucie police responded to reports of multiple gunshots near Southeast Green River Parkway and Southeast Charleston Drive. Police said Gabriella Gina Hanley was driving south on Southeast Green River Parkway in a black Kia Forte with her boyfriend, Darrick Mincey Jr., when another vehicle pulled alongside them and fired multiple rounds into their car. Officers and rescue personnel began life-saving measures after finding Hanley with multiple gunshot wounds. She was pronounced dead Oct. Mincey was also struck by gunfire but survived. See also: Teen identified after deadly Fellsmere shooting involving 100-plus teens Investigators found the Kia had 37 bullet impacts. Numerous 9mm cartridge casings were recovered, and forensic evidence indicated the bullets were fired from two separate rifles, police said. Five years later, detectives are continuing to conduct interviews and examine forensic and digital evidence. At the time of her death, Hanley left behind a 20-month-old baby. CBS12 reported in 2022 that investigators had identified three people of interest, but no charges were filed against them. Anyone with information is asked to call the Port St. Lucie Police Department at 772-871-5000 or Treasure Coast Crime Stoppers at 1-800-273-TIPS (8477) .

entry.title: Potential 2028 Democratic contenders set to discuss party’s future at post-midterms meeting
entry.summary: A group of potential 2028 Democratic presidential candidates is heading to Denver days after the midterms to discuss the partys future, in one of the partys first major gatherings following the election. Attendees will include former Transportation Secretary Pete Buttigieg and former US Ambassador to Japan Rahm Emanuel, as well as Sens. Ruben Gallego of Arizona, Chris Murphy of Connecticut, Raphael Warnock of Georgia and Elissa Slotkin of Michigan, according to an initial lineup shared first with CNN. The group of speakers also includes Govs. Mikie Sherrill of New Jersey and Abigail Spanberger of Virginia, plus several additional members of Congress. The Whats Next summit is being hosted from November 12-14 by Majority Democrats, an organization that launched last year to help Democrats win in more places. entry.title: Florida Election 2026: Vote-by-Mail and Early Voting deadlines you need to know
entry.summary: Floridians who want to cast a ballot in the 2026 General Election are encouraged to verify that their registration details, including their name, address and party affiliation, are accurate. Voters are also urged to confirm their Election Day polling location. Voter registration deadline is Oct. 5 for November election Election Day is scheduled for Tuesday, Nov. 3, with polls open from 7 a.m. to 7 p.m. Residents can update their registration online through Florida's voter registration website , by mail or in person using a Florida Voter Registration Application. Applications are also available at Supervisor of Elections Offices and other designated voter registration agencies. The deadline to register to vote for the November election was on Monday, Oct. 5. The deadline to register for an upcoming election is 29 days before that election. Key election deadlines Vote-by-mail request deadline: Thursday, Oct. 22, 2026, by 5 p.m. Early voting dates, locations Palm Beach County: Oct. 19-Nov. 1 from 7 a.m. to 7 p.m. Voters can cast their ballot at any of the 28 locations during this time. Vote-by-mail return deadline is Nov. 3, 2026, by 7 p.m. at the Main Office or by 5 p.m. at a Branch Office or Secure Ballot Intake Station Martin County: Oct. 21-31 from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. each day at six locations across the county. St. Lucie County: Oct. 1931 from 10 a.m. to 6 p.m. daily, including Sunday, Oct. 25. The county will have eight early-voting locations across the county. Indian River County: Oct. 19-31 from 8 a.m. to 4 p.m. with extended hours on Thursdays from 8 a.m. to 6 p.m. Four early-voting locations will be available throughout the county. Vote-by-mail ballots must be received by the Supervisor of Elections office by 7 p.m. Election Day to be counted and may be returned to a secure ballot intake station located at each early voting location during early voting hours, or in person to the Supervisor of Elections office. Okeechobee County: Oct. 24-31 from 8:30 a.m. to 6 p.m. at one location: 307 NW 5th Avenue in Okeechobee Election Day: Tuesday, Nov. 3, 2026, from 7 a.m. to 7 p.m. Voters must cast their ballot at their assigned precinct.

entry.title: Gov. Ron DeSantis announces removal of 220 Medicaid providers amid fraud, abuse investigation
entry.summary: Gov. Ron DeSantis announced Tuesday that Florida's intensified effort to root out fraud, waste and abuse in the state's Medicaid program has resulted in more than $1 billion in projected savings and the removal of hundreds of providers from the system. Speaking at the Healthcare District of Palm Beach County alongside Agency for Health Care Administration (AHCA) Secretary Shevaun Harris, DeSantis said the state has expanded oversight and enforcement measures to identify fraudulent billing and improper Medicaid payments. 'We want to make sure that what is being spent is being spent well,' DeSantis said. 'Medicaid dollars must go to healthcare for eligible Floridians, not to people who are gaming the system.' According to state officials, AHCA has conducted more than 400 provider site visits since January and increased the use of data analytics, claims monitoring and background screening to uncover suspicious activity. As part of the crackdown, the state said more than 150 fraud-related referrals have been made to the Florida Attorney General's Office over the past year, more than 250 providers have been placed on payment restrictions or had payments suspended, and more than 220 providers have been terminated from Florida Medicaid due to fraud, waste or abuse. State officials said those terminated providers accounted for more than $230 million in Medicaid billing in 2025. A major focus of the effort has been Applied Behavioral Analysis (ABA) services, commonly used to help children with autism. According to Harris, Florida Medicaid spent approximately $6.57 billion on ABA services between 2023 and 2025, nearly four times more than any other state's Medicaid program. At one point, spending was projected to grow by 30% annually. The state moved ABA services into managed care in 2025, a change officials say has improved oversight and slowed spending growth to less than 10% annually. "Medicaid dollars must go to healthcare for eligible Floridians, not to people who are gaming the system."According to state officials, AHCA has conducted more than 400 provider site visits since January and increased the use of data analytics, claims monitoring and background screening to uncover suspicious activity.As part of the crackdown, the state said more than 150 fraud-related referrals have been made to the Florida Attorney General's Office over the past year, more than 250 providers have been placed on payment restrictions or had payments suspended, and more than 220 providers have been terminated from Florida Medicaid due to fraud, waste or abuse.State officials said those terminated providers accounted for more than $230 million in Medicaid billing in 2025.A major focus of the effort has been Applied Behavioral Analysis (ABA) services, commonly used to help children with autism. According to Harris, Florida Medicaid spent approximately $6.57 billion on ABA services between 2023 and 2025, nearly four times more than any other state's Medicaid program. At one point, spending was projected to grow by 30% annually.The state moved ABA services into managed care in 2025, a change officials say has improved oversight and slowed spending growth to less than 10% annually. As a result, the state now projects ABA-related expenditures at roughly $2.8 billion, more than $1 billion lower than previous forecasts."That is where we want our funding going," Harris said. "Not in the pockets of crooks."Investigators uncovered instances in which providers billed Medicaid for impossible service schedules, including claims for more than 24 hours of care in a single day and services allegedly provided continuously through weekends and holidays.To strengthen provider screening, AHCA also partnered with identity verification company SentiLink to help identify synthetic identities, suspicious ownership structures and other potential fraud indicators before providers enter the Medicaid system.Despite the enforcement actions, DeSantis and Harris emphasized that the effort is aimed at fraudulent providers and not families who rely on Medicaid services.When WPTV Investigative Reporter Jamie Ostroff asked about concerns from families struggling to access ABA therapy, particularly in Palm Beach County, Harris said managed care plans are working with affected recipients to connect them with new providers when a provider is removed from the program."If there is a parent watching and they're having any issues, they can contact the agency and we will help them ourselves or connect them with their managed care plan," Harris said.DeSantis said the Medicaid initiative is part of a broader effort to ensure taxpayer dollars are spent responsibly while maintaining Florida's fiscal position. The governor highlighted the state's recent budget reductions, debt repayment efforts and tax relief measures as examples of what he described as responsible financial management.State officials said AHCA will continue conducting site visits, monitoring claims and referring suspected fraud cases for further investigation."This is kind of just the opening salvo," DeSantis said. "I would anticipate you will see more results coming in the weeks, months and years ahead."

Lee Forbes, Curtis Garrison and Kenneth Richter are among the more than 62,000 survivors who have been approved for settlements through the Boy Scouts of America bankruptcy trust. Watch full report from I-Team Investigative reporter Katie LaGrone Boy Scout Settlement Fees For Forbes, the settlement represents justice for abuse, he said, that lasted nearly two years while he was a teen scout in the Explorer program. entry.title: Toddler drowns in pond on family's property in Martin County
entry.summary: A 23-month-old boy died Tuesday evening after being found floating in a pond on his family's property, according to the Martin County Sheriff's Office. The child was playing outside in the yard along Darling Street with family members shortly after 5 p.m. when he slipped out of sight for a brief period. When the child's mother and aunt realized he was missing, they began searching for him and found him in a pond on the property. The family immediately rushed the toddler to Cleveland Clinic South, where medical staff performed lifesaving efforts. Despite their attempts, he was pronounced dead in the emergency room. Family members told investigators the child was out of their sight for no more than 10 minutes. Martin County Sheriff's Office criminal investigators interviewed everyone present at the scene and are reviewing the circumstances surrounding the tragedy. The investigation remains ongoing.

entry.title: Pratt Whitney and Bridge roads intersection causes daily delays for Martin County commuters
entry.summary: Drivers face significant delays at the intersection of Pratt Whitney and Bridge roads in Martin County during the morning and afternoon commutes. The rural four-way stop backs up with commuters, particularly when accidents occur. Many of those drivers travel from places like Lake Okeechobee and Pahokee workers who live far from their jobs in search of affordable housing. WATCH Pratt Whitney and Bridge Roads intersection causes daily delays for commuters Pratt Whitney and Bridge Roads intersection causes daily delays for Martin County commuters The area has seen upgrades to support growth and freight movement, but this intersection has received only upgraded signs, rumble strips, and advanced warning signs. Installing a full traffic light requires meeting state thresholds for high traffic volumes or crash data. The county has studied widening the road in phases. WPTV connected with the Martin County Board of County Commissioners and will keep track of any plans to add a traffic light in the future. entry.title: Decision not to charge parent in Indiantown bus stop gun incident sparks heated community debate
entry.summary: Outrage and frustration boiled over at a community meeting in Indiantown, as residents packed a room to demand answers from the Martin County Sheriff's Office after a parent who pulled a gun on two students at a bus stop was not charged with a crime. The tense Monday night meeting, led by the Martin County NAACP and the sheriff, centered on the sheriff's determination that the father acted in self-defense. However, many residents argued that the man should have been arrested for the separate crime of possessing a firearm at a school bus stop. He said it began with a student being bullied and struck by another student on a school bus. The victim's father went to the bus stop to report the bullying to the driver. The situation escalated, Budensiek said, when the alleged bully and a friend 'pushed past the bus driver and tried to confront the dad.' 'He puts his hand up and backs up, backs up, says 'stay away, stay away,' and they don't,' Budensiek explained. 'In fact, theyre yelling that theyre going to whoop his hind end... He pulls out a gun and all of a sudden theyre backing up, because they dont want to get shot.' A debate over Florida law The sheriff defended the lack of charges against the father, citing the state's self-defense laws. 'In the state of Florida, youre allowed to defend yourself against someone coming after you,' he said. But residents at the meeting were furious, arguing that the father was committing a misdemeanor by possessing a gun at a bus stop, which they believe should negate his 'Stand Your Ground' defense. 'Stand Your Ground cannot come into play because at the time you were committing a crime by being at that bus stop with a gun,' one resident yelled. The sheriff countered that the law does not provide a clear legal definition of what constitutes a 'bus stop,' making that specific charge unenforceable in this case. The father also declined to press battery charges against the two students. "They — being those positions— have essentially been able to investigate themselves." Those contract positions include the Fire Chief, District Attorney, Clerk Treasurer and Medical Director.The issue stems from an alleged hazing incident we reported on earlier this year. A third-party investigator concluded that videos showing firefighters using a modified bug zapper to shock probationary firefighters depicted hazing. Three veteran firefighters — Doug Boudrias, Jordan Hutchinson and Christopher Baldwin — were fired as a result."It was just us in our downtime, joking around, having fun," Hutchinson said."We're all still friends," Boudrias said. "Us and the victims, there was no ill intent." Months before the incident came to light, Baldwin and Hutchinson filed a complaint against Fire Chief Jeff Lee and Sabol in September 2025. District officials ultimately denied it. Baldwin and Hutchinson then filed additional complaints, including an amended complaint to investigators alleging the hazing investigation — and their subsequent termination — were part of a broader pattern of retaliation."That's not a good process," Fowler said. The board is now asking two outside law firms to help draft a new complaint policy. Meanwhile, firefighters are casting ballots in a no-confidence vote regarding Lee."It basically says whether or not they trust and believe in him to lead this district," Fowler said. "So that is a huge thing if you have the majority of the men and women underneath you saying they can no longer serve under you, that's a pretty impactful message." Lee acknowledged the district lacks a clear complaint process. He told Investigative Reporter Kate Hussey: "I'm glad this board is finally taking this as a serious issue," adding he "welcomes any investigation from any agency."Per Sabol's resignation, Lee said it's a "sad day." "She's been a tremendous attorney for the district," Lee said of Sabol. As for the vote of no confidence, Lee said he didn't have much to say until it's over with "We'll see what the men and women decide," Lee told Hussey. "I came up on the labor side; I've always fought for our men and women on the line." Tension inside district headquarters was evident throughout Wednesday's meeting."This system is so broken," one attendee said."Everybody is fed up. They want action," said retired fire captain Mike Jenkins.As the union's legal fight to reinstate the three firefighters continues, calls are growing for the fire board to bypass arbitration and bring them back to work. When asked whether the board has that authority, Fowler said, "I think we might actually," adding, "The chief wants them back. The union is saying they want to come back. I'm going to ask the board in a week from now — what do we want to do? What's the process?" Firefighters are still casting ballots in the no-confidence vote. entry.title: Nick Mimms trial: Prosecutor says former Fort Pierce city manager 'got caught with his hand in the cookie jar'
entry.summary: The trial of former Fort Pierce City Manager Nick Mimms entered its second day Tuesday with opening statements and witness testimony. Mimms was arrested in 2024 on charges of bid tampering and official misconduct. WATCH BELOW: Opening statements begin in trial of former city manager Former Fort Pierce city manager faces day two of trial During opening statements, the State Attorney's Office said Mimms knowingly rigged the bidding process for two vacant parcels of land along Avenue D in favor of a local nonprofit that his niece was on the board of, and kept it from the public. 'The defendant Nicholas Mimms just got caught with his hand in the cookie jar,' Assistant State Prosecutor Jonathan Bridges said. Bridges pointed to a paper trail of city documents, email correspondence, phone records and witness testimony. 'He made sure that the public was not privy to the information he shared with Miss Scott and her group. In doing so, the defendant made sure that the city-owned land would ultimately be leased by LPYP and no one else,' Bridges said. LPYP stands for the Lincoln Park Young Professionals, the local nonprofit involved in the case. The defense countered that Mimms showed no favoritism, and that a $500,000 grant provided by the Alleghany Franciscan Ministries toward the development of the site in Lincoln Park did not involve the city. 'They started work on the project, and it failed, and that's the sad truth. But it wasn't by the fault of any one person. It certainly wasn't a deliberate act by anyone,' defense attorney Donald Murrell said. The first witness called by the state was Ben Masondo, a local real estate broker from the Doyen Company, who also submitted a bid on the two vacant lots. Masondo said he felt the city's decision to move forward with LPYP was unfair. 'You have one that has a city employee involved. I felt that the judging was misguided. At one point, I think I had said clearly one of these people was the Russian judge, just decided not to score me fairly, and I looked at what was around, and yes, I was upset. I thought that was snake. They snaked me,' Masondo said. The trial is expected to last at least a week. If found guilty, Mimms could face a second-degree felony for bid tampering that carries a maximum of 15 years in prison and up to a $10,000 fine. Official misconduct is a third-degree felony that carries a maximum of five years in prison and up to a $5,000 fine.

entry.title: Port St. Lucie lowers property tax rate for 11th straight year
entry.summary: The Port St. Lucie City Council unanimously approved a reduction in the city's property tax rate for the 11th consecutive year, lowering the millage rate from 4.9750 to 4.8750 for the fiscal year beginning Oct. 1. The decision, made during the formal adoption of the city's $971.6 million budget on Monday, continues a trend of tax relief that officials said has saved the average homeowner nearly $2,000 over the past decade. WATCH BELOW: Port St. Lucie property tax rate going down Port St. Lucie lowers property tax rate for 11th straight year Since 2016, Port St. Lucie has reduced its millage rate by 25%, giving the city the third-lowest municipal tax rate among Florida's 20 largest cities. The millage rate represents the amount of tax charged per $1,000 of taxable property value. Officials said the tax cuts come despite the city's rapid population growth. More than 60,000 new residents have moved to Port St. Lucie since 2020, requiring substantial investments in infrastructure including roads, drainage systems, utilities and public safety services. 'Our goal is to provide the services our residents value most while being good stewards of taxpayer dollars,' said Mayor Shannon M. Martin. 'By taking a measured approach to lowering property tax rates, we have been able to continue meeting the needs of our growing community while remaining fiscally responsible.' The city's ability to maintain services while reducing taxes reflects what officials describe as smart financial planning designed to support the rapidly expanding community without burdening existing property owners. The fiscal year 2026-27 budget totals $971.6 million across the city's operating and capital funds, supporting services for a population that has grown substantially in recent years while maintaining the city's commitment to keeping property tax rates low. The new millage rate takes effect Thursday.

Trump International Airport, Olive's reaction was immediate."I would say so. I would say that's a lot," said Olive.The briefing comes as WPTV continues reporting on the impact the restrictions have had on communities below, including concerns about increased aircraft noise in parts of West Palm Beach and Palm Beach.In May, Palm Beach County Commissioner Gregg Weiss told WPTV the rerouted flight paths have impacted approximately 20,000 residents.The restrictions, known as TFRs, are routinely put in place when Trump is staying at Mar-a-Lago. NORAD officials told WPTV they do not create the restrictions. Instead, the restrictions are established by the Federal Aviation Administration and U.S. Secret Service, while NORAD is responsible for enforcing them."We're here to enforce the TFR and to ensure the safety of everyone, to include the individuals on the ground, the airplanes that are flying in the air as well, to make sure nobody violates the TFR, and if they do, to make sure that they're escorted safely out of the TFR as well, basically to keep the airspace clean," Olive said.NORAD officials shared a demonstration video where WPTV was given a close look at the fighter aircraft and personnel responsible for protecting the restricted airspace.Pilots assigned to the mission are not waiting on the ground for a violation to occur.When asked whether they launch after a violation or patrol routinely, one pilot's answer was simple:"Regularly patrol," the pilot replied.Officials said fighter jets are already in position before the restrictions take effect."When the TFR goes active, we're already airborne, and we're there," Olive said.If a pilot enters restricted airspace without authorization, NORAD receives notification through air traffic control."We're already airborne. They'll give us a point out; we'll find it with our radar, we'll go check it out, and basically get their intention, what they're looking to do," Olive said. "If they're just a person who doesn't know they're not supposed to be there, then we'll help escort them out of the TFR safely."Despite the number of interceptions, officials said the overwhelming majority involve pilots making mistakes, not people attempting to threaten the restricted airspace."I would say the majority, that is correct," Olive said. "There's also a majority of it where they have the proper code, they have the proper clearance, they just forget to squawk the right code, so they take off, they have a clearance, they're good to go, but they haven't punched in that clearance in their airplane, and then they do so on departure, but we still have to scramble on them because we don't know their intention because they're not squawking the right code."Asked whether any of the interceptions he has handled involved bad intentions, Olive said: "Not, I don't, no, not from my experience, no, they're just people who forget or who have not done the proper flight planning."Officials say most of the aircraft involved are not large commercial jets."The majority would be smaller Cessnas, single-engine planes for sure," said Olive.Palm Beach presents unique challenges, according to NORAD, because of the large amount of general aviation traffic in the area."I'd say Mar-a-Lago is interesting. It's different from up north," one pilot said. "There's more general aviation down here due to the nice weather, the amount of flight schools that are around here, people want to fly up and down the coast, the banner towers, so we get more general aviation traffic down here for sure."The restricted airspace itself consists of two zones."It's a temporary flight restriction," a pilot explained. "It encompasses a 10-mile ring centered at the airfield here, and then there's a 30-mile ring as well that extends beyond that. The 10-mile ring is essentially a no-fly zone."Pilots operating inside the larger ring must follow special FAA procedures."You have to be on a flight plan. You have to be squawking a discrete code, and in comms with ATC."Officials emphasized that while most violations are innocent mistakes, every response is treated seriously."We're always training to take it all the way to the conclusion that, hey, this is a person with bad intentions," Olive said. "Obviously that is a last, last resort. We're not there to hand down the judgment or the punishment; we're just there to enforce the TFR and escort them safely either to land or outside of the TFR."Any penalties are handled by the FAA once the aircraft lands."We'll safely escort them out. We'll make sure that they land. We'll monitor them until they land at their destination," Olive said. "Upon landing, they'll be notified that they have a phone number to call that'll be a phone number that leads them to the FAA and then the FAA will deal with that."Officials also stressed how closely NORAD and the FAA work together."It's imperative. We're completely intertwined," Olive said. "The FAA, they can't do their job without us. We can't do our job without them."For residents wondering why military aircraft may be overhead during presidential visits, officials say the mission comes down to safety."Any time you have the president of the United States travel anywhere, that's a very high visibility movement, and it attracts a lot of attention not only within the United States but nationally as well," one pilot said.And for pilots flying near Palm Beach, NORAD had a straightforward message:"If you're going to fly, if you're an avid flyer, check your NOTAMs before you fly, just so everybody's safe, and you're not where you're not supposed to be."When asked whether he had a message for Trump himself, the pilot smiled."Yeah, sir, we'll be above you, keeping you safe in the sky."This story was reported on-air by a journalist and has been converted to this platform with the assistance of AI. entry.title: Shooting death of Gabriella Hanley remains unsolved 5 years later, police seeking tips
entry.summary: Five years have passed, but the shooting death of 20-year-old Gabriella Hanley remains unsolved. No one has been charged with her death, and Port St. Lucie police are asking anyone with information to come forward. WATCH BELOW: Port St. Lucie police investigating deadly shooting Mystery gunman fires shots into car in Port St. Lucie, killing woman On Oct. 5, 2021, at around 11:45 p.m., Port St. Lucie police said they responded to reports of multiple gunshots near Southeast Green River Parkway and Southeast Charleston Drive. Hanley was driving southbound on Southeast Green River Parkway in a black Kia Forte with her boyfriend, 21-year-old Darrick Mincey Jr., when another vehicle pulled alongside them and fired multiple rounds into their car, police said. Hanley was shot multiple times, police said. Officers and rescue personnel immediately attempted lifesaving measures, but she later died in the early morning hours on Oct. 6, 2021. Mincey was also struck by gunfire but survived. Investigators said they determined the Kia sustained 37 bullet impacts during the shooting. Numerous 9mm cartridge casings were recovered from the scene, and subsequent forensic examination determined they had been fired from two different firearms, police said. The suspect vehicle was described as a silver four-door sedan that fled southbound on Southeast Green River Parkway. In the years since Hanley's death, Port St. Lucie Police Department detectives have continued to investigate her death, conducting numerous interviews, examining forensic and digital evidence, and following up on investigative leads. As of Tuesday, no one has been charged with Hanley's death, and police continue to search for answers. If you know something about what happened to Hanley that night, no matter how insignificant you may think it is, Port St. Lucie police are asking you to come forward. You can call Port St. Lucie Police Department Major Crimes Division at 772-871-5000 or Treasure Coast Crime Stoppers at 1-800-273-TIPS (8477). Tips provided can remain anonymous.

entry.title: Gov. Ron DeSantis announces removal of 220 Medicaid providers amid fraud, abuse investigation

Ron DeSantis announced Tuesday that Florida's intensified effort to root out fraud, waste and abuse in the state's Medicaid program has resulted in more than $1 billion in projected savings and the removal of hundreds of providers from the system. Speaking at the Healthcare District of Palm Beach County alongside Agency for Health Care Administration (AHCA) Secretary Shevaun Harris, DeSantis said the state has expanded oversight and enforcement measures to identify fraudulent billing and improper Medicaid payments. entry.article_text: Ron DeSantis announced Tuesday that Florida's intensified effort to root out fraud, waste and abuse in the state's Medicaid program has resulted in more than $1 billion in projected savings and the removal of hundreds of providers from the system.Speaking at the Healthcare District of Palm Beach County alongside Agency for Health Care Administration (AHCA) Secretary Shevaun Harris, DeSantis said the state has expanded oversight and enforcement measures to identify fraudulent billing and improper Medicaid payments.WATCH BELOW: State targets Medicaid fraud, removes hundreds of providers"We want to make sure that what is being spent is being spent well," DeSantis said. "Medicaid dollars must go to healthcare for eligible Floridians, not to people who are gaming the system."According to state officials, AHCA has conducted more than 400 provider site visits since January and increased the use of data analytics, claims monitoring and background screening to uncover suspicious activity.As part of the crackdown, the state said more than 150 fraud-related referrals have been made to the Florida Attorney General's Office over the past year, more than 250 providers have been placed on payment restrictions or had payments suspended, and more than 220 providers have been terminated from Florida Medicaid due to fraud, waste or abuse.State officials said those terminated providers accounted for more than $230 million in Medicaid billing in 2025.A major focus of the effort has been Applied Behavioral Analysis (ABA) services, commonly used to help children with autism. According to Harris, Florida Medicaid spent approximately $6.57 billion on ABA services between 2023 and 2025, nearly four times more than any other state's Medicaid program. At one point, spending was projected to grow by 30% annually.The state moved ABA services into managed care in 2025, a change officials say has improved oversight and slowed spending growth to less than 10% annually. As a result, the state now projects ABA-related expenditures at roughly $2.8 billion, more than $1 billion lower than previous forecasts."That is where we want our funding going," Harris said. "Not in the pockets of crooks."Investigators uncovered instances in which providers billed Medicaid for impossible service schedules, including claims for more than 24 hours of care in a single day and services allegedly provided continuously through weekends and holidays.To strengthen provider screening, AHCA also partnered with identity verification company SentiLink to help identify synthetic identities, suspicious ownership structures and other potential fraud indicators before providers enter the Medicaid system.In July, WPTV chief investigator Jamie Ostroff spoke with families in Palm Beach County whose access to ABA was abruptly cut off by Medicaid. They told her ABA was a lifeline for their children who were able to learn in school, communicate, use the bathroom and control tantrums thanks to the therapy.Despite the enforcement actions, DeSantis and Harris emphasized that the effort is aimed at fraudulent providers and not families who rely on Medicaid services.When Ostroff asked about concerns from families struggling to access ABA therapy, particularly in Palm Beach County, DeSantis replied, "If you have a provider that is doing some legitimate services and much fraudulent — to the extent that those services get interrupted, that's not AHCA's fault. That's that provider's fault."Harris added that managed care plans are working with affected recipients to connect them with new providers when a provider is removed from the program."If there is a parent watching and they're having any issues, they can contact the agency and we will help them ourselves or connect them with their managed care plan," Harris said.DeSantis said the Medicaid initiative is part of a broader effort to ensure taxpayer dollars are spent responsibly while maintaining Florida's fiscal position. The governor highlighted the state's recent budget reductions, debt repayment efforts and tax relief measures as examples of what he described as responsible financial management.State officials said AHCA will continue conducting site visits, monitoring claims and referring suspected fraud cases for further investigation.Ostroff asked Harris for a list of providers accused of fraud. She said she would provide what she could without jeopardizing any ongoing, potentially criminal, investigations."This is kind of just the opening salvo," DeSantis said. "I would anticipate you will see more results coming in the weeks, months and years ahead."

entry.title: Palm Beach Gardens High School football players excelling on and off the field with a top state GPA
entry.summary: The Palm Beach Gardens High School football team is not only winning on the field the Gators are also setting a high standard in the classroom, carrying a team grade point average between 3.3 and 3.4, one of the best in the state. Following a dominant Monday night football win against Boynton Beach High School, the team is back focused on the game plan, both on the field and in school. WATCH BELOW: Palm Beach Gardens HS football players are excelling on and off the field with a top state GPA Palm Beach Gardens High School football players are excelling on and off the field Two years ago, head coach Phil Norman made academics a central priority when he took over the program. 'One of the first meetings was detailed in the classroom. A lot of these kids do have aspirations to go to college, and the main thing to get there is you have to be accepted into the college programs first,' Norman said. The team's grade point average ranks among the best in not only Palm Beach County, but the entire state. Junior defensive back Ellby Gedeum is one player setting the pace with a near-perfect GPA. 'My GPA is a 3.9 right now,' Gedeum said. Gedeum said he handles the demands of being a student-athlete by staying disciplined after games. 'Just adapting after a long game, I come home, do my homework and stuff,' Gedeum said. Junior running back Rasheen Brooks is also excelling as a student-athlete. 'My GPA is a 3.5 as we speak, and I have 21 credit hours right now as a junior, so I am eligible to graduate as of now, but you know I'm not. I am in a good spot as a student-athlete,' Brooks said. Brooks said he wants to play college football, and he knows academics are the foundation for getting there. 'Without the books there is no college, so you can be the best athlete you are but without books there's nothing,' Brooks said. entry.title: Teen dies after shooting near Garcia's Boat Ramp in Indian River County - WPBF
entry.summary: Teen dies after shooting near Garcia's Boat Ramp in Indian River County    WPBF
entry.article_text: A 17-year-old boy died after a shooting late Friday close to a boat ramp near Fellsmere and Vero Beach, the Indian River County Sheriff's Office said Saturday. The Indian River School District said the unnamed teen recently withdrew from Sebastian River High School to homeschool and was not enrolled in the district at the time of the shooting. "We are deeply saddened by the loss of this young person, and our hearts are with his family, friends, and the Sebastian River High School community," district spokeswoman Kyra Schafte said in a statement to WPBF. In a follow-up email she wrote: "This remains an active investigation, and we are in constant communication with the Indian River County Sheriff’s Office. Please direct questions about the investigation to IRCSO. Our primary focus is supporting our students, staff, families, and community during this difficult time." A dance is scheduled for 7 p.m. Saturday at Sebastian River High. Read more at: https://www.miamiherald.com/news/article317482082.html#storylink=cpy At 11:24 p.m., deputies responded to reports of a juvenile shot in the area of Garcia's Boat Ramp in the 3700 block of County Road 512 and near the Fort Drum Marsh Conservation Area. Deputies located the teen and began lifesaving measures until Indian River County Fire Rescue arrived. He was taken to Sebastian River Medical Center and later flown to Holmes Regional Medical Center in Melbourne, where he died from his injuries, the sheriff's office said. "At this time, this appears to be an isolated incident, and there is no threat to the public," Lt. Kevin Jaworski wrote in an alert to the media. "This is an active investigation." He told WPBF that investigators have interviewed all parties involved in the case. Anyone with information about this incident is asked to call the Indian River County Sheriff’s Office (772-569-6700) or Treasure Coast Crime Stoppers (1-800-273-TIPS). Detectives from the Criminal Investigations Division and crime scene personnel were processing the scene and interviewing multiple witnesses. The area remains open to the public. entry.summary: Flood safety tips shared as Indiantown residents prepare for more rain    WPEC
entry.article_text: Indiantown residents remain concerned about flooding after heavy rain left streets covered in water last week, with more rain and storms in the forecast for this week. CBS12 crews captured video of vehicles driving through standing water on roadways in parts of the village. Residents say flooding can quickly become expensive when water affects homes and property. The sad part is, if you don’t have insurance or anything like that you’re just stuck, your stuck with the bill, said Mary Brown, a Booker Park resident. The flooding has renewed questions about the more than $2 million drainage and roadway project in Booker Park. The project began in 2022 to help reduce flooding, but residents say heavy rain is still leaving some streets underwater. Village leaders have said they are working with Martin County on longer-term drainage solutions, including the possible repair or replacement of broken pipes. The next Indiantown Village Council meeting is Thursday night. With more rain possible this week, Martin County Fire Rescue and the Florida Department of Health in Martin County have tips available online for residents to plan ahead and avoid driving or walking through floodwater. You can CLICK HERE to view the entire list. Officials say water on a roadway may be deeper or more contaminated than it appears. Drivers who encounter a flooded road should turn around rather than attempt to drive through it. Martin County Fire Rescue responds to flooding-related emergencies, including when a vehicle becomes stuck in floodwater. Residents should call 911 during an emergency. For ongoing drainage problems or flooded roadways, residents can submit a report through Martin County’s online Request for Service system . The county asks residents to include the specific address or location and details about the issue, such as standing water, a blockage or a low spot near a drainage structure. CLICK HERE to submit a request. Health officials also advise residents whose wells flood to use bottled or boiled water until the well can be tested.

entry.article_text: Five years after the shooting death of a 20-year-old woman, the Port St. Lucie Police Department is still seeking answers. Lucie police responded to reports of multiple gunshots near Southeast Green River Parkway and Southeast Charleston Drive. Police said Gabriella Gina Hanley was driving south on Southeast Green River Parkway in a black Kia Forte with her boyfriend, Darrick Mincey Jr., when another vehicle pulled alongside them and fired multiple rounds into their car. Officers and rescue personnel began life-saving measures after finding Hanley with multiple gunshot wounds. She was pronounced dead Oct. Mincey was also struck by gunfire but survived. See also: Teen identified after deadly Fellsmere shooting involving 100-plus teens Investigators found the Kia had 37 bullet impacts. Numerous 9mm cartridge casings were recovered, and forensic evidence indicated the bullets were fired from two separate rifles, police said. Five years later, detectives are continuing to conduct interviews and examine forensic and digital evidence. At the time of her death, Hanley left behind a 20-month-old baby. CBS12 reported in 2022 that investigators had identified three people of interest, but no charges were filed against them. Anyone with information is asked to call the Port St. Lucie Police Department at 772-871-5000 or Treasure Coast Crime Stoppers at 1-800-273-TIPS (8477) .

entry.title: DeSantis opens new I-95 interchange in Indian River County, a year early - cw34.com
entry.summary: DeSantis opens new I-95 interchange in Indian River County, a year early    cw34.com
entry.article_text: Ron DeSantis opened the new I-95 interchange at Oslo Road in Indian River County on Monday, calling it a critical connection for drivers, emergency crews and the region’s growing population. The roughly $100 million project opened one year ahead of schedule , according to the governor’s office and the Florida Department of Transportation. This is the first new interchange built in this area in almost 50 years, DeSantis said. It’s going to bring [a] new critical connection [to] I-95 for a part of the state that has changed quite a bit. The new exit is expected to ease congestion at nearby Indrio Road and State Road 60 interchanges, DeSantis said. Drivers traveling from Oslo Road to I-95 can expect their travel times to be cut in half, he added. With the number of daily vehicles on the corridor still expected to grow between now and 2045 significantly, the Oslo Road interchange sets a clear example of how Florida delivers infrastructure that improves quality of life today while building more capacity for the future, DeSantis said. The governor also said the direct interstate connection will help emergency crews respond faster in southern Indian River County. See also: Two killed, including 10th-grade girl, after rollover school bus crash in Polk County We anticipate that just for the local community on a normal basis, for local, like non-hurricane-type emergencies, that the emergency response time will be reduced by up to 56%, DeSantis said. That will ultimately save some lives, of course, because time is of the essence in some of these situations. FDOT Secretary Jared Perdue said the project was completed 400 days early through what the agency calls voluntary acceleration, which lets contractors propose ways to speed construction and share in the savings. This is going to reduce the time it takes for first responders to get to incidents substantially, Perdue said. We’re really excited about that, to include cutting commute time in half and so many other benefits. DeSantis said FDOT also acquired land near the interchange for a dedicated gopher tortoise habitat. He said the site will be the only relocation area of its kind in Southeast Florida. Florida [is] showing that it’s possible to do the projects that we need done while also buttressing environmental stewardship, DeSantis said. Perdue said nearly $1 billion in transportation investment is planned for the Treasure Coast region. Indian River County Commissioner Joseph Flescher recounted his reaction when he first heard about the opening. "When I got the phone call, I said, ' We're not near completion. I had been here just two weeks ago. We were nowhere near where we're at.' This team worked an incredible operation, said Flescher. Flescher also highlighted how important this new entrance ot I-95 is to the growing population across the county. This interchange is very much needed in the development of our county. And I don't mean the future development. I mean the current development, Flescher said.

entry.title: Port St. Lucie streets flood after downpour, stranding vehicles and disrupting commutes - WPEC
entry.summary: Port St. Lucie streets flood after downpour, stranding vehicles and disrupting commutes    WPEC
entry.article_text: Heavy rain flooded roads across Port St. Lucie Tuesday afternoon, leaving some vehicles stranded, forcing children to walk through standing water after school and prompting a response from police officers and city crews. According to the City of Port St. Lucie , a large amount of rain fell in a short period of time, leading to temporary road closures and flooding in multiple areas. Public Works crews responded to flooding near Savona Boulevard and California Boulevard, closing the roadway until it was safe for travel. The city also reported high-water conditions near Thornhill Drive and Floresta Drive, where Phase 3 construction is underway. On Southwest Thornhill Drive, school buses continued dropping off students despite flooded streets. CBS12 News saw children step off buses carrying their shoes and walk barefoot through standing water to reach home. Along Southwest Broadview Avenue near Crosstown Parkway, residents watched as water spilled across the roadway, making it difficult for drivers to tell where the street ended and floodwater began. "If you didn't see the grass here, you wouldn't know where the road is," resident Kevin Burke told CBS12 News. "It was steady sheets of rain for a good hour. Non-stop, and I mean heavy, heavy." Police officers directed traffic while Public Works crews set up barricades and monitored conditions during the evening commute. Burke said flooding in the area has become a familiar problem during heavy downpours. "When it rains heavy like it did today, it's like this all the time, from that canal coming up," he said. Burke said standing water presents concerns beyond traffic issues. "We have a pond over there by Crosstown and Bayshore. It's got signs all around it saying there are gators in it. It's a long shot, but it could happen, and that's what worries me, with kids and the animals," he said. For some residents, the flooding disrupted everyday tasks. "She has her elderly brother, who's 83 years old, and she's in her 60s, and she was going to run out and get Chinese food, and now she's still sitting here waiting because she can't get to it," Burke said. Earlier in the day, Port St. Lucie police reported flooding at several intersections, including SE Evans Avenue and SE Airoso Boulevard, SE Eyerly Avenue and SE Airoso Boulevard, SW Bayshore Boulevard and SW Thornhill Drive, and NE Floresta Drive and NE Ardsley Drive. See also: Opponents, supporters clash over Palm Beach County Israel Bonds investments City officials said Public Works crews continued monitoring conditions as water slowly receded Tuesday evening. Officials also reminded residents not to walk or drive through flooded roadways because it can be difficult to determine how deep the water is.

entry.title: U.S Senate candidate Angie Nixon campaigns in Fort Pierce, talks economy and reproductive health - WPBF
entry.summary: U.S Senate candidate Angie Nixon campaigns in Fort Pierce, talks economy and reproductive health    WPBF
entry.article_text: Senate candidate Angie Nixon visited Fort Pierce on Tuesday to speak with voters about reproductive health care, the economy, and other issues as part of her campaign across Florida ahead of the general election. Nixon, who represents a Jacksonville-area district in the Florida House of Representatives and describes herself as a Democratic Socialist, is holding town hall meetings across the state to connect with voters. Planned Parenthood President and CEO Alexis McGill Johnson hosted the Fort Pierce town hall, focusing on reproductive freedom and Florida's maternal mortality crisis. McGill Johnson and Nixon outlined the leadership they believe Florida families need, including protecting abortion access and expanding comprehensive health care services statewide. "Representative Nixon is a true champion for reproductive freedom," McGill Johnson said. "In the Senate, she is going to stand up for affordable health care and our right to make our own decisions about our own bodies." During the event, Nixon addressed a question about a proposed Islamic center approved for construction in Palm Beach County. Deep Dive: WPBF 25 News Investigates "This is a country where folks should have freedom of religion," Nixon said. "I would speak out against that type of opposition and hate if it was directed at a synagogue being built, if it was directed at a church being built, if it was directed at any other spiritual facility." Nixon also discussed the state of reproductive health care in Florida and other issues raised by voters. "Gas is high, people are struggling to get to and from work, and then they can't even afford the food anymore, let alone taking their children to the movies or out to eat, that's null and void now," one voter said. Nixon won the Democratic primary in St. Lucie County with about 54% of the vote. When asked how she plans to close the gap between herself and Republican incumbent Ashley Moody, Nixon said she intends to continue engaging with voters, including those who may disagree with her. "They have someone who is going to put them first," Nixon said when asked about the message she hopes attendees took away from Tuesday's event. She added that her campaign for U.S. Senate is focused on putting money back in people's pockets. Nixon spoke with voters for about an hour. Her next stop is in the Orlando area. entry.title: 5 years after Gabriella Hanley's unsolved killing, family and police still calling on community for answers
entry.summary: Five years after Gabriella 'Gabi' Hanley was shot and killed in an apparent drive-by shooting in Port St. Lucie, no arrests have been made in her case. WATCH BELOW: Family seeks answers 5 years after loved one killed Gabi Hanley cold case: Port St. Lucie family seeks answers 5 years later Hanley, 20, was shot along Green River Parkway in 2021. Her boyfriend, who was in the car at the time, was also hit by gunfire but survived. Hanley left behind a 14-month-old daughter, who is now 6 years old. Port St. Lucie police identified several people of interest at the time of the shooting, but five years later, no one has been arrested. The pain of losing Gabi still lingers for her mother, Nicole Vigilante. 'It is tough, but I gotta be strong for my granddaughter,' Vigilante said. As Gabi's daughter grows older, the family is searching for answers for themselves and for her. 'Now she's getting older, and she has questions,' Vigilante said. 'And we want to be able to give her those answers,' Krystal Benitez, Gabi's cousin, added. For Gabi's loved ones, her daughter is a constant reminder of who she was. 'We're reminded of the situation every single day,' Alexia Perez, Gabi's best friend, said. 'We will never forget Gabi. Her daughter is walking memory of her.' 'Gabi was an amazing, amazing woman,' Benitez added. Port St. Lucie police turned to social media Tuesday, saying information that was not shared at the time of the shooting could make a difference today. They're asking anyone with information to contact the Port St. Lucie Police Department's Major Crimes Division at 772-871-5000 or Treasure Coast Crime Stoppers at 1-800-273-8477. Gabi's family and friends are doing their part to keep the case alive by sharing her story and raising awareness throughout the community. 'We have been spending the day handing out flyers going to all local businesses just trying to again raise awareness,' Benitez said. They are now calling on the community to come forward with information. 'There's a little girl right now that's being raised without her mother, so be brave for her and come forward,' Benitez said.

entry.title: No arrests after 17-year-old shot, killed at meetup in Indian River County, self-defense claim expected - WFLX
entry.summary: No arrests after 17-year-old shot, killed at meetup in Indian River County, self-defense claim expected    WFLX
entry.article_text: No arrests have been made in the shooting death of a 17-year-old at a teen meetup near Garcia’s Boat Ramp in Indian River County, with a self-defense claim expected in the case, Indian River County Sheriff Eric Flowers announced Monday. “We got kids out here losing their lives chasing likes and shares on social media,” Flowers said. The shooting occurred late Friday night when approximately 100 teens, ranging in age from 14 to 19, gathered at Garcia’s Boat Ramp in the 3700 block of County Road 512, the sheriff said. Deputies had broken up a similar group earlier that evening before the crowd moved to the boat ramp. “The 17-year-old, and a group of his friends, are approaching a truck, and there are two people, both 18 years old, inside of that truck. The 17-year-old opens the door, and he starts to punch,” Flowers said. “He’s going to punch on the people that are inside of that truck. That shot is the shot that ultimately killed 17-year-old in this case.” The teen’s friends drove him away from the scene, east on County Road 512, while calling 911 and a dispatcher told them to stop at Fellsmere City Hall, where emergency crews performed CPR, the sheriff said. He was taken to Sebastian River Medical Center and later flown to Holmes Regional Medical Center in Melbourne, where he died from his injuries. The two individuals in the truck were identified using the sheriff’s office’s Flock technology, the sheriff said. Flowers said both have been cooperative with investigators, surrendering the weapon used in the shooting and the truck. Additional individuals involved in the incident have also been identified through Flock, though some remain unidentified. Investigators also recovered other weapons from the vehicle in which the 17-year-old was transported from the scene. Flowers said a warrant will be submitted in the case, but it will be up to the state to determine whether charges are filed. “There have been no arrests on this case at this time, because the preliminary investigation shows that the 17-year-old was opening the door to attempt to fight with the two that were inside of the vehicle. They had a history of fighting,” Flowers said. “Self defense plays a part in these, and when these kids go out and videotape these fights, and now guns are involved, there’s going to be more of this.” Names of those involved are not being released as the investigation continues, the sheriff said. Investigators believe at least four fights occurred at the boat ramp on the night of the shooting. Multiple shell casings and rounds were recovered from the scene. During Monday’s news conference, Flowers released video of the shooting, noting the footage had already circulated widely on social media and that the victim’s mother had seen it. One of the 18-year-olds involved in the shooting attends Vero Beach High School. The sheriff said teen meetups like the one at Garcia’s Boat Ramp are coordinated through Snapchat, making them difficult for law enforcement to track in advance. “When it’s Snapchat, it’s basically a private conversation,” Flowers said. “But it quickly can escalate to over 100, 150, 200 people there.” Flowers said the meetups, which have included alcohol, fighting, and firearms, have been taking place for years across Indian River County, Okeechobee, and surrounding areas, but that social media has intensified the danger. “Now we’re adding guns and alcohol into the mix, and we’re adding social media into the mix, and so what we’re seeing is an escalation of each one of these,” Flowers said. There’s guns, and those two just don’t mix. And now add in the fuel of the fire of social media, and now we have a 17-year-old dead.” The sheriff said teens at these gatherings are motivated in part by a desire for online attention. “The kids like to fight, and they like to videotape it, and they like to get their likes and shares because of that,” Flowers said. Parents, you see these videos. You do not want your teens out at these meetups." With Vero Beach High School’s homecoming game scheduled for Friday and the dance on Saturday, Flowers said additional deputies will be on duty. Meanwhile, the sheriff urged parents to monitor their children’s whereabouts and report any information about planned meetups to the sheriff’s office. “Parents, if your kids are telling you that they’re headed out to one of these meetups, ask them where they’re going. Ask, find out the details. Share that with us,” Flowers said. He recommended parents use location-sharing apps such as Life360 to track their children and said a child appearing to be in a remote or unusual location can be an indicator that a meetup is taking place. The investigation remains active. Flowers said anyone who witnessed any of the events that night, including the shooting itself, and has not yet spoken to investigators is urged to come forward. “I can tell you, our investigation is not even remotely over, and if we are able to identify people that were involved in this, from underage drinking to fighting, hurting other people,” Flowers said. " If they did something wrong, they’re going to have to be accountable for that." Anyone with information is asked to call the Indian River County Sheriff’s Office at 772-569-6700 or Treasure Coast Crime Stoppers at 1-800-273-TIPS.

The counties included are: Baker, Bay, Calhoun, Columbia, Dixie, Escambia, Franklin, Gadsden, Gilchrist, Gulf, Hamilton, Holmes, Jackson, Jefferson, Lafayette, Leon, Liberty, Madison, Okaloosa, Santa Rosa, Suwannee, Taylor, Walton, Wakulla, and Washington. This order will allow the Florida Division of Emergency Management to stage critical preparedness resources and ensure Florida is ready to respond, DeSantis said. The governor urged Floridians to make disaster plans and check hurricane supplies. The current forecast indicates a tropical storm or hurricane could make landfall somewhere along the central Gulf Coast later this week, the governor said in a Tuesday statement. 'Impacts are expected to extend beyond the point of landfall, with heavy rainfall, strong winds, coastal flooding and isolated tornadoes possible across North Florida,' the statement said. 'Additional precipitation could further saturate soils and increase the potential for flash flooding following the states recent significant rainfall.'
